title: What is the purpose of subnet mask in TCP/IP networking?
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What is the purpose of a subnet mask in TCP/IP networking?

options.label: A
options.html: To identify the network portion of an IP address

options.label: B
options.html: To identify the host portion of an IP address

options.label: C
options.html: To convert IP addresses into domain names

solution: A subnet mask is used in TCP/IP networking to divide an IP address into two parts: the network portion and the host portion. It uses a 32-bit pattern of 1s and 0s, where 1s represent the network part and 0s represent the host part. This helps routers and devices determine whether a destination IP address is on the same local network or needs to be routed to another network. For example, in the IP address 192.168.1.10 with a subnet mask 255.255.255.0, the first three octets (192.168.1) represent the network, and the last octet (10) represents the host.

title: With an IP address of you currently have subnets. What
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: An IPv4 address has first octet 100. A classful network requires at least 80 subnets. Which value should be used in the second octet of the subnet mask to maximize the number of hosts per subnet?
solution:
Concept

In fixed-length classful subnetting, borrowing s bits from the host portion creates 2s subnet identifiers. To maximize hosts while meeting a requirement of N subnets, choose the smallest s for which 2s is at least N. In a mask octet, s borrowed bits appear as s leading 1-bits followed by 0-bits.

Application

The first octet 100 lies in the Class A range 1–126, so the classful default prefix is /8. Apply the minimum-bits rule:

  1. With 6 borrowed bits, 26 = 64, which is fewer than 80.

  2. With 7 borrowed bits, 27 = 128, which is at least 80; therefore 7 is the minimum.

  3. The new prefix is /8 + 7 = /15. Seven leading 1-bits in the second mask octet give 11111110 in binary, or 254 in decimal, so the full mask is 255.254.0.0.

Cross-check

A Class A subnet table lists 7 borrowed bits as 255.254.0.0 (/15), providing 128 subnet identifiers and 131070 usable host addresses per subnet. One fewer borrowed bit gives 255.252.0.0 and only 64 subnet identifiers; borrowing more bits would reduce the host capacity unnecessarily.

Result

The required second-octet value is 254, giving subnet mask 255.254.0.0 (/15).

solution:
Broadcast address is the last address in the subnet, where all the host bits are made to be 1's. A broadcast address targets all systems on a specific subnet instead of a single host.

Step 1: Use the bitwise AND operator on the binary IP address to the binary CIDR address to get the network address.

11001001.01100110.01001101.00100011 (201.102.77.35)

& 11111111.11111111.11111111.11100000 (/27)

-----------------------------------

11001001.01100110.01001101.00100000 (201.102.77.32)

[201.102.77.32]

Step 2: Next use the bitwise OR operator on the binary network address and the inverted CIDR address to get the broadcast address.

11001001.01100110.01001101.00100000 (201.102.77.32)

(or) 00000000.00000000.00000000.00011111 (inverted /27)

-----------------------------------

11001001.01100110.01001101.00111111 (201.102.77.63)

[201.102.77.63]

title: Suppose an organisation has CIDR based IP address Organisation decided
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Suppose an organisation has CIDR based IP address 215.58.204.10./20, Organisation decided to divide the network into three subnet name as X, Y, Z respectively. Which of the following is a valid IP address of the subnet Y?
solution:
Given: 215.58.204.10/20

Subnet mask: /20 = 255.255.240.0. Compute the network address: third octet 204 & 240 = 192, so the network is 215.58.192.0/20.

The /20 network range is 215.58.192.0 through 215.58.207.255.

One reasonable way to divide this /20 into three subnets is to allocate one /21 and two /22 subnets so the ranges do not overlap and cover the whole /20:

  • Subnet X: 215.58.192.0/21 — covers 215.58.192.0 to 215.58.199.255

  • Subnet Y: 215.58.200.0/22 — covers 215.58.200.0 to 215.58.203.255

  • Subnet Z: 215.58.204.0/22 — covers 215.58.204.0 to 215.58.207.255

Check the candidate addresses:

  • 215.58.201.100/22 falls inside 215.58.200.0–215.58.203.255, so it is a valid address for Subnet Y (and the /22 mask matches that subnet).

  • 215.58.192.12/22 and 215.58.196.254/21 both lie within 215.58.192.0–215.58.199.255 (Subnet X) under this partition, so they are not in Subnet Y.

Therefore the address 215.58.201.100/22 is a valid IP for subnet Y in this partitioning. Note: different valid partitions of the /20 are possible, but the partition above matches the provided correct option.

title: Router has the following (CIDR) entries in the routing table.

bodyHtml:
A router has the following (CIDR) entries in the routing table.

Next-hop for a packet with IP address 138.48.63.10
solution:
Given:

  • Routing table entries: 138.48.56.0/22 → I-0; 138.48.60.0/22 → I-1; 192.150.48.0/23 → R-1; default → R-2.

  • Packet IP: 138.48.63.10.

Key idea: match the packet to the most specific routing entry by checking which subnet contains the IP.

/22 networks have a block size of 4 in the third octet, so:

  • 138.48.56.0/22 covers third-octet values 56–59.

  • 138.48.60.0/22 covers third-octet values 60–63.

Since the packet's third octet is 63, the address 138.48.63.10 falls into 138.48.60.0/22.

Therefore the packet matches the 138.48.60.0/22 route and is forwarded to next-hop I-1.

title: IP address is found to be residing on sub-network with
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: IP address 172.16.123.213 is found to be residing on a sub-network with the following subnet mask: 255.255.255.240. What is the network address of this subnet?
solution:
Concept

The address of a subnet is obtained by a bitwise AND of a host IP address with its subnet mask. Wherever the mask holds a 1 the bit is a network bit and passes through unchanged; wherever the mask holds a 0 the bit is a host bit and is forced to 0. So the mask splits every address into a fixed network prefix and a host field, and zeroing that host field names the subnet itself rather than any machine on it.

Applying it here

  1. Write the mask in binary: 255.255.255.240 = 11111111.11111111.11111111.11110000. That is 24 + 4 = 28 network bits, so the prefix length is /28.

  2. The first three mask octets are all 1s, so the first three octets of the address survive the AND untouched: 172.16.123.

  3. Only the final octet is split. In binary 213 = 110101012 and 240 = 111100002.

  4. AND them bit by bit. The leading four bits 1101 sit under mask bits of 1, so they are preserved. The trailing four bits 0101 sit under mask bits of 0, so they become 0000. Result: 110100002.

  5. Convert back to decimal: 128 + 64 + 16 = 208.

  6. Network address = 172.16.123.208.

Cross-check with the block-size method

  • Four host bits give a block size of 24 = 16 addresses per subnet, which is also the familiar shortcut 256 - 240 = 16.

  • So every /28 boundary in the final octet is a multiple of 16: 0, 16, 32, ... 192, 208, 224, 240.

  • 213 falls between the boundary 208 (= 13 x 16) and the next boundary 224 (= 14 x 16), so its subnet runs 208-223 and starts at 208 - the same value the AND produced.

  • Note that "network address" means the base of that range. The first usable host would be 209 and the broadcast address would be 223; neither is what the question asks for.

Comparing the offered values

Final octet

Low four bits

Role under /28

213

0101

A host inside its block, not a boundary

240

0000

A /28 boundary (15 x 16), base of 240-255

245

0101

A host inside the block 240-255

208

0000

A /28 boundary (13 x 16), base of 208-223

The value 240 is a genuine /28 boundary, but it is the base of the block 240-255, which does not contain 213; 213 and 245 both carry a non-zero host field, so neither can name a subnet.

title: An organization is granted the block The administrator wants to
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml:
An organization is granted the block 130.56.0.0/16. The administrator wants to create 1024 subnets. .

Find first and last addresses of last subnet.
solution:
Final answer: 130.56.255.192 to 130.56.255.255

  1. Start with the given block: 130.56.0.0/16. You need 1024 subnets.

  2. Since 1024 = 2^10, you must borrow 10 bits from the host portion.

  3. New prefix length = 16 + 10 = /26.

  4. Addresses per subnet = 2^(32 - 26) = 64 addresses (62 usable hosts).

  5. Subnets increment by 64 in the last octet. The last subnet index is 1023, so offset = 1023 × 64 = 65472, which corresponds to .255.192 in the last two octets.

  6. Therefore the last subnet's network address = 130.56.255.192 and its broadcast (last address) = 130.56.255.255.

title: What does the term ‘NAT’ stand for in networking
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What does the term ‘NAT’ stand for in networking ?
solution: NAT stands for Network Address Translation. This is a fundamental networking concept used to remap one IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit across a traffic routing device. The primary purpose of NAT is to allow multiple devices on a local network to share a single public IP address when accessing the internet, which conserves IPv4 addresses and adds a layer of security by hiding internal network structures. Option B, Network Access Translation, is incorrect because NAT does not primarily deal with access control or authentication. Option C and D are also incorrect as they refer to 'Node' or 'Application' translation, which do not accurately describe the function of modifying IP addresses at the network layer. Therefore, Option A is the correct definition.

subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following IP addresses is a loopback address ?
solution: A loopback address is used for testing network software on the local machine without sending packets over a physical network. The standard IPv4 loopback address is 127.0.0.1, which always refers to the local host itself.

title: Identify the local link address from the following IPv6 addresses:
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Identify the link-local address from the following IPv6 addresses:
solution:
Concept

An IPv6 address is classified by the leading bits of its first hextet, which fix its scope and purpose. A link-local unicast address is valid only on a single network link (it is never routed off that link), and by RFC 4291 it lies in the FE80::/10 block. The /10 pins only the first 10 bits to 1111111010, so its first hextet ranges from FE80 to FEBF. The task is to match each address to its reserved prefix and pick the one whose high-order bits fall in that link-local range.

Applying the prefix rules

Address (first hextet)

Reserved prefix

Type / scope

2001:0db8:...

2001:db8::/32

Documentation / global

FE80:...

FE80::/10

Link-local unicast

FF02:...

FF00::/8

Multicast

::1

::1/128

Loopback

2001:4860:4860::...

2000::/3

Global unicast

Only the address whose first hextet is FE80 has high-order bits inside FE80::/10, so it is the link-local address.

Cross-check

Expand the first hextet to bits: FE80 = 1111 1110 1000 0000. Its first 10 bits are 1111111010, which is exactly the FE80::/10 pattern (any first hextet FE80-FEBF shares these 10 bits). None of the other addresses' high-order bits match this pattern, confirming the choice.

title: In classful addressing the IP address with 0(zero) as network
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: In a classful addressing the IP address with 0(zero) as network number:

options.label: B
options.html: refers to broadcast on the local network

options.label: C
options.html: refers to the broadcast on a distant network

solution:
Answer: An IP address whose network portion is all zeros refers to the current (local) network in classful addressing.

Key points:

  • This-network convention: A network field of all zeros is interpreted as "this network" (the local network).

  • Broadcast addresses: Broadcasts are indicated by setting the host portion to all ones (for example, 192.168.1.255 for a /24). A zero network number does not mean broadcast.

  • Directed (distant) broadcasts use a specific network number with all host bits set to one; they are not signified by an all-zero network field.

  • Loopback: Loopback addresses are in the 127.0.0.0/8 block (commonly 127.0.0.1), unrelated to the all-zero network convention.

  • Historical note: Early classful IPv4 specifications used the all-zero network convention. Modern practice prefers explicit network numbering to avoid ambiguity.

title: What is the purpose of routing table?
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What is the purpose of a routing table?

options.label: A
options.html: To store every address of every node

options.label: B
options.html: To know the exact location of destination address

options.label: D
options.html: To find most efficient route to the destination

solution:
Concept: A routing table is a data structure stored in a router (or host) that maps destination networks to the information needed to reach them — typically a destination network/prefix, a next-hop address, an outgoing interface, and a metric. Its governing purpose is path selection: for any incoming packet the router looks up the destination and decides the best (lowest-cost) way to forward it onward.

Application: When a packet arrives, the router reads its destination IP, searches the table for the matching entry using longest-prefix match, and forwards the packet to the next hop on the path with the most favourable metric (lowest cost / administrative distance). So the table exists to pick the most efficient route to the destination; it does not store the location of every individual host, and it does not record an exact geographic position.

Contrast: the other purposes describe what a routing table is not for:

  • Storing every address of every node: a routing table holds network prefixes and next hops, not an entry for every host; keeping every node's address would not scale and is not the table's job.

  • Knowing the exact location of the destination: a router only needs the direction of the next hop toward the destination network, not the destination's precise physical location.

  • Flooding the network: flooding sends a packet out on all links and is deliberately inefficient; it is the behaviour routing tables exist to avoid.

Result: the routing table's purpose is to find the most efficient route to the destination.

title: Routing information Protocol (RIP) uses
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Routing information Protocol (RIP) uses
solution:
Answer: RIP is a distance-vector routing protocol.

Key details:

  • Metric: Uses hop count as its routing metric; a hop count of 16 indicates an unreachable route.

  • Updates: Sends periodic routing updates (typically every 30 seconds).

  • Algorithm and loop mitigation: Implements the distance-vector (Bellman-Ford) approach and uses split horizon, route poisoning, and hold-down timers to help limit routing loops.

  • Versions: RIPv1 is classful; RIPv2 adds support for CIDR (classless addressing) and optional authentication.

  • Limitations: Not suitable for large networks due to slow convergence and the 15-hop limit.

Therefore, the correct characterization is that RIP uses the distance-vector routing method.

title: The subnet with routers with delays shown as line in
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: The subnet with 6 routers with delays shown as a line in the following graph. It uses distance-vector routing to build the tables. Router A has measured its routes to its neighbours B, C, and E. It gets the new distance of 2, 1, 5 for B, C, E respectively. A has received the following vectors from node B: (2,0,2,6,6,5), from node C: (1,4,0,9,7,7) and from node E: (6,8,7,5,0,3). Find which of the following is the new routing table at A.
solution:
Solution (step-by-step):

Given:

  • Direct costs from A to its neighbors: B = 2, C = 1, E = 5 (and A to A = 0).

  • Neighbor vectors received (order of destinations shown as A, B, C, D, E, F):

    • From B: (2, 0, 2, 6, 6, 5)

    • From C: (1, 4, 0, 9, 7, 7)

    • From E: (6, 8, 7, 5, 0, 3)

Compute the cost to each destination via each neighbor (cost to neighbor + neighbor's advertised cost):

  • Via B (add 2): (4, 2, 4, 8, 8, 7)

  • Via C (add 1): (2, 5, 1, 10, 8, 8)

  • Via E (add 5): (11, 13, 12, 10, 5, 8)

Now take the minimum for each destination (including direct cost where applicable):

  • To A: min(0, 4, 2, 11) = 0 → next hop: - (self)

  • To B: min(direct 2, via B 2, via C 5, via E 13) = 2 → next hop: B

  • To C: min(direct 1, via B 4, via C 1, via E 12) = 1 → next hop: C

  • To D: min(via B 8, via C 10, via E 10) = 8 → next hop: B

  • To E: min(direct 5, via B 8, via C 8, via E 5) = 5 → next hop: E

  • To F: min(via B 7, via C 8, via E 8) = 7 → next hop: B

Final routing table at A (destination → next hop, distance):

  • A → -, 0

  • B → B, 2

  • C → C, 1

  • D → B, 8

  • E → E, 5

  • F → B, 7

title: Suppose the host firewall of computer is configured to block
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Suppose the host firewall of a computer is configured to block all incoming ICMP packets. What could be its effect on function of TCP/IP protocol stack of the host?
solution: Blocking incoming ICMP packets disrupts Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD). PMTUD uses ICMP Type 3, Code 4 messages ('Fragmentation Needed') to inform senders when a packet exceeds the MTU of an intermediate link. If these messages are blocked, the sender cannot reduce packet size to fit the path MTU, potentially causing connection failures for large data transfers. TCP congestion control and slow start rely on ACKs and retransmission timeouts, not ICMP.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q98
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: How does split horizon help reduce the count-to-infinity problem in distance vector routing?

options.label: A
options.html: Stopping routers from sending updates on all ports

options.label: C
options.html: Preventing routers from advertising a route back on the interface

solution:
Concept

In distance-vector routing protocols (such as RIP), each router learns routes from its neighbors and re-advertises them onward. The count-to-infinity problem occurs when a route becomes unreachable but two neighboring routers keep advertising it to each other with steadily increasing hop counts, because each one still believes the other has a valid path. Split horizon is a loop-avoidance rule: a router omits a route from the update it sends out the very interface through which it originally learned that route, since re-advertising it there would just be echoing the neighbor’s own information back to it.

Application

Consider router B, which learns a route to network X from neighbor A on the link between them. Under split horizon, B does not include that route to X in the update it sends back to A on that same link. So if the link between A and X later fails, A does not receive a stale route to X from B claiming a working path via B, which is exactly the false information that would otherwise make A and B keep raising their advertised hop counts to each other toward infinity.

Cross-check

Contrast this with the other offered mechanisms. Suppressing updates on every port (rather than only the interface a specific route was learned on) would stop the router from advertising anything at all, which is not split horizon's selective, per-route, per-interface behaviour. Choosing distance over hop count is a metric-design decision (as in EIGRP), unrelated to which interface an update is withheld from. Turning off periodic updates concerns the update schedule (related instead to triggered updates), not the direction in which a specific route is withheld. RFC 1058 describes exactly this interface-specific withholding behaviour, confirming that preventing a router from advertising a route back on the interface it was learned from is the mechanism that reduces count-to-infinity here.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q67
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Assuming no routing loop is present, which situation would primarily cause a router to select a valid but suboptimal path even though every routing protocol involved continues to run and converge correctly?

options.label: A
options.html: Unequal cost metrics between heterogeneous routing protocols

solution:
A dynamic routing protocol compares the candidate paths it has learned using its own metric and selects whichever candidate has the lowest value of that metric, trusting that value as “best” regardless of whether the number actually reflects real-world path quality. Different protocols compute this metric on different scales: RIP simply counts hops, OSPF derives a cost from link bandwidth, and EIGRP combines bandwidth and delay into a composite value — so a metric value computed by one protocol is not comparable to a metric value computed by another.

When routes learned from one protocol are redistributed into a different protocol, the receiving protocol has no way to translate the original metric onto its own scale, so it must instead assign a seed (default) metric to the redistributed routes. Because that seed metric does not represent the routes' true cost, a router can end up preferring a path that its own metric marks as best even though a different, non-redistributed path is actually shorter or faster — and this happens purely from the metric mismatch, with every protocol involved still converging normally and operating exactly as designed.

The other three situations, by contrast, each describe an actual breakdown in protocol operation rather than a side effect of protocols working correctly:

  • A route-redistribution loop — the case this stem's “no routing loop” premise explicitly rules out — happens when a route is fed back into the very protocol it originated from; the metric keeps inflating (or the route oscillates) until it is discarded, a misconfiguration that breaks correct operation, not an artifact of it.

  • An MTU mismatch on a link used by a link-state protocol typically prevents the two routers from ever completing neighbor/adjacency formation, so the protocol is not functioning correctly once that happens — it simply fails to form a relationship on that link.

  • If link-state packets are never acknowledged, the reliable-flooding mechanism that keeps every router's link-state database synchronized has itself broken down — again a functional failure, not a consequence of correct operation.

So the situation that produces a suboptimal path while every routing protocol continues to run and converge correctly is unequal cost metrics between heterogeneous routing protocols.

title: Which of the following TCP/IP protocol allows an application program
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following TCP/IP protocol allows an application program on one machine to send a datagram to an application program on another machine?
solution:
Concept: In the TCP/IP suite, the transport layer offers two delivery styles. A connection-oriented byte-stream service (TCP) sets up a reliable, ordered connection before any data flows; a connectionless datagram service hands each self-contained message to the network independently, with no prior handshake. The protocol whose entire purpose is to let one application program ship a single datagram to another application program — addressed by port number, with minimal overhead and no connection setup — is the User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

Application: The defining specification (RFC 768) describes UDP exactly as the question phrases it: a procedure for application programs to send messages (datagrams) to other application programs with a minimum of protocol mechanism. UDP runs over IP, multiplexes to the right program using source and destination ports, and forwards each datagram on a best-effort basis without establishing or maintaining a connection. So the protocol that lets an application on one machine send a datagram to an application on another machine is UDP.

Contrast with the other choices:

  • VMTP — a transport protocol designed for request-response (transaction/RPC) message exchange in distributed systems, not the standard TCP/IP datagram delivery service for ordinary application programs.

  • X.25 — an older packet-switched WAN networking standard (network/data-link layers), not a TCP/IP transport protocol for application-to-application datagrams.

  • SMTP — an application-layer protocol for transferring email between mail servers; it relies on an underlying transport, it does not itself provide the datagram delivery service.

Cross-check: Of the four, only UDP sits at the transport layer with a connectionless, datagram (message) delivery model addressed by ports — matching the description precisely. The correct answer is UDP.

title: Port address in TCP/IP is bits long.
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Port address in TCP/IP is ________ bits long.
solution:
Concept

A port number is the transport-layer address that identifies a specific process or service running on a host. In both the TCP and the UDP segment headers, the Source Port and Destination Port are each stored in a fixed 16-bit field. A field of n bits can encode 2n distinct values, so the size of this field is what fixes how many ports can exist.

Application

  1. The TCP/UDP header reserves a 16-bit field for the port address (one for source, one for destination).

  2. With 16 bits, the number of distinct port values is 216 = 65,536.

  3. These are numbered 0 to 65,535, which is exactly the standard port range used by every operating system.

Cross-check

The well-known fact that valid ports run from 0 to 65,535 is the give-away: 65,535 = 216 − 1, which is only possible if the field holds 16 bits. A 32-bit field would allow over 4 billion ports, and a 48-bit field even more — neither matches the observed 0–65,535 range. Hence the port address is 16 bits long.

title: Which of the following services use TCP? DHCP ii) SMTP
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml:
Which of the following services use TCP?

i) DHCP

ii) SMTP

iii) HTTP

iv) TFTP

v) FTP
solution:
Concept — The transport protocol a service uses depends on what the application needs. TCP is connection-oriented and reliable: it performs a handshake and uses sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission so that every byte arrives correctly and in order. UDP is connectionless and lightweight: it has no handshake and no built-in reliability, which suits bootstrapping, broadcast, or small low-overhead transfers.

Application — Classify each service by the transport it relies on:

  • SMTP uses TCP: an email message must arrive complete and in order.

  • HTTP uses TCP: a web page and its resources must be delivered reliably.

  • FTP uses TCP for both its control and data connections, so whole files transfer without loss.

  • DHCP uses UDP: a client broadcasts to obtain configuration before it even has an IP address, which fits connectionless UDP.

  • TFTP uses UDP: it is deliberately 'trivial' and carries its own minimal acknowledgement scheme on top of UDP instead of relying on TCP.

Cross-check — Collecting the TCP services gives SMTP, HTTP and FTP, that is items ii, iii and v.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q153
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following is a connection-oriented protocol ?
solution:
A protocol is connection-oriented when the sender and receiver first establish a session (commonly via a handshake) and maintain state for that session throughout the exchange, so that delivery can be tracked, acknowledged, and reordered if needed. A connectionless protocol instead sends each unit of data independently, with no session setup and no guarantee of delivery or order.

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) begins every exchange with a three-way handshake — SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK — before any application data is sent. Once the connection is open, TCP numbers every byte, acknowledges receipt, retransmits lost segments, and closes the session explicitly at the end. This session-based, stateful behaviour is exactly what defines a connection-oriented protocol, so TCP fits the description in the stem.

Contrasting the other options confirms this:

  • UDP sends each datagram independently with no handshake and no session state, so it is connectionless rather than connection-oriented.

  • IP works at the network layer and forwards each packet on a best-effort basis without setting up or tracking any session between source and destination — also connectionless.

  • HTTP is an application-layer protocol that defines request/response message formats between a client and server; it does not itself establish the transport session — it runs on top of a transport-layer connection (typically TCP).

Hence, among the given options, TCP is the connection-oriented protocol.

title: TCP operates over Gbps link. If TCP uses the full
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: TCP operates over a 40 Gbps link. If TCP uses the full bandwidth continuously, how long would it take the sequence numbers to wrap around completely?
solution:
Key insight: TCP sequence numbers count bytes and the sequence number space is 2^32.

  • Sequence number space: 2^32 = 4,294,967,296 bytes.

  • Bandwidth: 40 Gbps = 40 × 10^9 bits/s = 5 × 10^9 bytes/s (8 bits = 1 byte).

  • Time to wrap = sequence number space / bandwidth.

  • Calculation: 4,294,967,296 bytes / (5 × 10^9 bytes/s) ≈ 0.858993459 s ≈ 859 ms.

Therefore the sequence numbers will wrap around in about 859 ms when sending continuously at 40 Gbps.

title: Let TCP operates over 32Gbps Gbps bit per second) link.
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Suppose a TCP-like protocol uses a sequence-number field that is 2 bits wider than TCP’s standard 32-bit field and operates over a 32 Gbps link (1 Gbps = 109 bits per second). If it continuously uses the full bandwidth, after how many seconds will the sequence number wrap around? Assume that one sequence number is consumed per byte, and give the answer to two decimal places.
solution:
Concept: For a continuously transmitting link, a byte-oriented k-bit sequence-number field has 2k distinct sequence positions. The wraparound time equals the total sequence space in bytes divided by the transmission rate in bytes per second.

Application:

  1. The standard TCP sequence-number field is 32 bits wide. The stem adds 2 bits, so k = 32 + 2 = 34 bits.

  2. Sequence space = 234 = 17,179,869,184 byte positions.

  3. Link rate = 32 Gbps = 32 × 109 bits per second = (32 × 109)/8 = 4 × 109 bytes per second.

  4. Wraparound time = 234/(4 × 109) = 17,179,869,184/4,000,000,000 = 4.294967296 seconds, which rounds to 4.29 seconds.

Cross-check: With the standard 32-bit field, the exact time would be 232/(4 × 109) = 1.073741824 seconds. Two extra bits multiply the sequence space and time by 22 = 4; using the exact value, 1.073741824 × 4 = 4.294967296 seconds, which again rounds to 4.29 seconds.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q52
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: In a TCP header, how many bits does each source port and destination port field contain?
solution:
Concept

A fixed-width unsigned field of n bits can represent 2n distinct bit patterns, spanning 0 through 2n − 1.

TCP uses source and destination port fields to identify the sending and receiving application endpoints within a segment.

Application

  1. In the TCP header layout defined by RFC 9293, Source Port occupies the first half of the opening 32-bit row.

  2. Destination Port occupies the second half of that same 32-bit row.

  3. Each half spans 16 bit positions, so both port fields are 16 bits wide.

Cross-check

An unsigned 16-bit field supplies 216 = 65,536 values, numbered 0 through 65,535. This matches the TCP port-number space.

Contrast

  • 8 bits would provide only 256 values.

  • 32 bits is the width of TCP sequence and acknowledgment fields, not either port field.

  • 128 bits is not the width assigned to a TCP port field.

Therefore, each source port and destination port field contains 16 bits.

title: Suppose client repeatedly connects via TCP to given port on

bodyHtml: Suppose a client C repeatedly connects via TCP to a given port on a server S, and that each time it is C that initiates the close. title: Choose the correct statement about SCTP.
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Choose the correct statement about SCTP.

options.label: A
options.html: SCTP stand for stream connection transmission protocol.

options.label: B
options.html: SCTP is message-oriented whereas TCP is stream-oriented.

options.label: D
options.html: SCTP may provide more flexibility for certain applications, like Voice over IP (VoIP).

solution:
Correct statements:

  • SCTP is message-oriented whereas TCP is stream-oriented.

  • SCTP can handle multiple simultaneous streams.

  • SCTP may provide more flexibility for certain applications, like Voice over IP (VoIP).

SCTP expansion: SCTP stands for Stream Control Transmission Protocol.

Explanation:

  • The statement claiming the expansion "stream connection transmission protocol" is incorrect because the protocol name is Stream Control Transmission Protocol.

  • Message-oriented versus stream-oriented: SCTP preserves application message boundaries so one send maps to one receive; TCP provides a continuous byte stream and does not preserve such boundaries, requiring application-level framing.

  • Multiple streams: SCTP associations can carry multiple independent streams with separate sequence spaces, which reduces head-of-line blocking compared to a single TCP stream.

  • Application suitability: Features such as multistreaming, multihoming, and optional partial reliability (PR-SCTP) make SCTP attractive for some real-time or message-oriented applications (for example, certain VoIP use cases). In practice, UDP with RTP is still widely used for VoIP, but SCTP can be a suitable alternative depending on requirements.

  • TCP behavior: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery across a single stream, which is different from SCTP's multistream, message-oriented behavior.

title: Consider an effect of slow start using msec round trip
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Consider an effect of slow start using 10 msec round trip time and no congestion. The receiver window is 24 KB and the maximum segment size is 2KB. How long does it take (in ms) before the first window can be sent?
solution:
Given: RTT = 10 ms, MSS = 2 KB, receiver window = 24 KB. Slow start begins with a congestion window of 1 MSS and doubles the congestion window each RTT.

  • Initial send at t = 0: send 1 MSS = 2 KB. Cumulative sent = 2 KB.

  • After 1 RTT (t = 10 ms): cwnd = 2 MSS, send 2 MSS = 4 KB. Cumulative sent = 6 KB.

  • After 2 RTTs (t = 20 ms): cwnd = 4 MSS, send 4 MSS = 8 KB. Cumulative sent = 14 KB.

  • After 3 RTTs (t = 30 ms): cwnd = 8 MSS, send 8 MSS = 16 KB. Cumulative sent = 30 KB, which exceeds the receiver window of 24 KB.

Conclusion: The sender can transmit the full 24 KB receiver window during the third RTT. Time = 3 × 10 ms = 30 ms.

title: Token bucket scheme is used for traffic shaping. new token
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: A token bucket scheme is used for traffic shaping. A new token is put into the bucket at every 10 µsec. Assume each token picks one packet which contains 2 bytes of data. It is observed that the initial capacity of the bucket is 10 Mbits. The computer can transmit at the full speed of 8 Mbps for ______ (in seconds upto 2 decimal places)
solution:
We know, C + R × S = M × S

Where, C = Initial capacity R = Token rate M = Output rate S = Bursty traffic

Given, C = 10 Mbits

Token arrives at an interval of 10 µsec.

Then in 1 sec 100000 tokens arrive.

So, 100000 × 16 bit = 16 × 10⁵ bits/sec = 1.6 Mbps

Hence R = 1.6 Mbps

Substituting we get

S = C / (M - R) = 10 / (8 - 1.6) = 1.5625

title: Computer on Mbps network is regulated by token bucket. The
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: A computer on a 80 Mbps network is regulated by a token bucket. The token bucket is filled at a rate of 10 Mbps. It is initially filled to capacity with 210 megabits. The time taken for the computer to transmit at the full 80 Mbps is ………… sec.
solution:
Given: initial tokens B = 210 Mbits, token arrival rate r = 10 Mbps, transmission rate C = 80 Mbps.

  • Net token consumption rate while transmitting at full rate = C − r = 80 − 10 = 70 Mbps.

  • Time to exhaust the initial token bucket: t = B / (C − r) = 210 / 70 = 3 s.

  • Verification: bits sent in 3 s = C × t = 80 × 3 = 240 Mbits. Tokens available = initial 210 + r × t = 210 + 10 × 3 = 240 Mbits → matches.

Answer: 3 seconds

title: An SMTP client sends an email of size KB over
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: An SMTP client sends an email of size 500 KB over a TCP connection with MSS = 1 KB. The connection uses slow start, doubling the congestion window every RTT until it reaches 32 KB. If the RTT is 100 ms, calculate the total time (in milliseconds) to send the email.
solution:
Key idea: slow start doubles the congestion window each RTT; with MSS = 1 KB, the window is measured in KB and you send up to cwnd KB each RTT.

  • RTTs to reach a 32 KB window: starting at 1 KB and doubling each RTT, 1 × 2^5 = 32, so it takes 5 RTTs to reach a 32 KB window.

  • Data sent during those 5 RTTs (windows of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 KB): 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 = 31 KB.

  • Remaining data after these RTTs: 500 − 31 = 469 KB.

  • With a 32 KB window thereafter, each RTT can send up to 32 KB, so the additional RTTs needed are ceil(469 / 32) = 15 RTTs.

  • Total RTTs = 5 + 15 = 20 RTTs. With RTT = 100 ms, total time = 20 × 100 ms = 2000 ms.

Final answer: 2000 ms.

title: What is the ideal TCP window size of sender to
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What is the ideal TCP window size of a sender to fully utilize a link of bandwidth 8192000bps and latency of 32ms?
solution: To fully utilize the link, the TCP window size must equal the Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP). First, calculate the Round-Trip Time (RTT), which is twice the one-way latency: RTT = 2 × 32 ms = 64 ms (0.064 seconds). Next, calculate the BDP in bits: 8,192,000 bps × 0.064 s = 524,288 bits. Finally, convert to bytes: 524,288 / 8 = 65,536 bytes.

title: What are the reasons for “Silly Window Syndrome”? Receiver announces
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml:
What are the reasons for “Silly Window Syndrome”?

a. Receiver announces advertised window as zero

b. Client generates only one byte at a time

c. Router processes only one byte data at a time.

d. Server consumes only one byte at a time.
solution:
The Silly Window Syndrome occurs due to inefficient data handling that leads to small, fragmented data transmissions. Reasons include:

[a] Receiver announcing an advertised window as zero (causing the sender to wait).

[b] Client generating only one byte at a time (inefficient data production).

[d] Server consuming only one byte at a time (slow processing by the server).

Option (c) Router processes only one byte at a time is irrelevant since routers operate at the Network Layer and handle packets, not individual bytes.

Hence, correct reasons are [a], [b], [d].

title: Which of the following statement is false about UDP.
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following statement is false about UDP.

options.label: A
options.html: UDP is used for management processes such as SNMP

options.label: B
options.html: UDP does not have any mechanism for flow control.

options.label: D
options.html: UDP is a suitable transport protocol for multicasting.

solution:
Answer: The false statement is "UDP provide congestion control like TCP."

  • UDP is used for management processes such as SNMP — True. SNMP typically uses UDP because it is lightweight and suitable for short request/response exchanges; reliability or retries are handled at the application layer if needed.

  • UDP does not have any mechanism for flow control — True. UDP is connectionless and does not implement flow control or windowing; senders are not paced by receiver feedback.

  • UDP provide congestion control like TCP — False. UDP does not implement congestion-control algorithms such as slow start, congestion avoidance, or retransmission timers. Applications or higher-level protocols built on UDP must implement any needed congestion control themselves.

  • UDP is a suitable transport protocol for multicasting — True. UDP supports sending datagrams to multicast addresses and does not require per-recipient connections, making it appropriate for group communication and streaming scenarios.

Additional note: UDP provides basic error detection via an optional checksum but does not provide acknowledgments, retransmission, or ordering guarantees. Those features, if required, must be implemented by the application or a higher-level protocol.

title: Which of the following field is not part of UDP
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following field is not a part of UDP header?
solution:
Correct answer: Window size is not a part of the UDP header.

Key point: UDP uses a fixed 8-byte header composed of four 16-bit fields.

  • Source Port — 16 bits (2 bytes): identifies the sender’s port; included in the UDP header.

  • Destination Port — 16 bits (2 bytes): identifies the receiver’s port; included in the UDP header.

  • Length — 16 bits (2 bytes): total length of UDP header plus payload in bytes.

  • Checksum — 16 bits (2 bytes): used for optional error-checking of the UDP header and data.

Contrast with TCP: Window size is a TCP header field used for flow control and does not exist in UDP, which is connectionless and does not provide flow control.

title: Which protocol is responsible for sending email messages?
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which protocol is responsible for sending email messages?
solution:
Concept

Application-layer protocols divide network communication into specialized services. A protocol’s command model and the resource it transfers identify its role more reliably than its name alone.

Email submission and relay use a store-and-forward exchange: a client or mail server declares the sender, specifies recipients, and supplies the message data for onward delivery.

Application

  1. SMTP expands to Simple Mail Transfer Protocol and provides the mail-transfer dialogue through commands such as MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, and DATA.

  2. These commands carry a message from a mail client to a submission server and relay it between mail servers.

  3. Therefore, the protocol responsible for sending email messages is SMTP.

Contrast

  • POP3 retrieves messages from a server mailbox, commonly downloading them to a client.

  • IMAP accesses and synchronizes mailboxes that remain on the server.

  • FTP transfers general files through separate control and data connections.

Result

SMTP is the sending and relay protocol among the offered choices.

title: Which the following is an email transfer protocol
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which the following is an email transfer protocol ?
solution: The correct answer is SMTP, which stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. This protocol is specifically designed to handle the transmission of email messages between servers and from clients to mail servers. When you send an email, SMTP is the underlying standard that ensures your message travels across the internet to reach its destination. It operates on port 25 and is dedicated solely to sending mail, making it the definitive email transfer protocol among the choices provided. In contrast, FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used for transferring files between computers on a network, not emails. HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is used for loading web pages and accessing resources on the World Wide Web. ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is used for diagnostic purposes, such as checking network connectivity with tools like ping. Therefore, only SMTP fits the specific function of email transfer.

title: Which protocol is used for sending emails
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which protocol is used for sending emails ?
solution: The Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the standard protocol used for sending emails across networks. It defines how mail servers communicate to deliver messages from a sender to a recipient.

title: In email communication, how are SMTP and POP3 different from
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: In email communication, how are SMTP and POP3 different from each other?

options.label: A
options.html: SMTP is used to get emails; POP3 is used to send emails

options.label: B
options.html: SMTP secures the message; POP3 stores it permanently

options.label: C
options.html: SMTP is used to send emails; POP3 is used to download them

options.label: D
options.html: SMTP manages file transfers; POP3 manages attachments

options.label: E
options.html: Both protocols do the same work in email systems

solution:
Correct answer: SMTP is used to send emails; POP3 is used to download them.

  • SMTP works as a mail sending/transfer protocol. It pushes outgoing messages from the sender’s client or mail server toward the recipient’s mail server.

  • POP3 is a mail access protocol. It lets a user download messages from a mail server to a local client, commonly for reading offline.

  • So the main contrast is sending/transfer by SMTP versus receiving/downloading by POP3.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q152
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which protocol is used to send emails?
solution:
Concept

Application-layer protocols in the TCP/IP model are each purpose-built for a specific kind of communication - one for transferring files, one for delivering hypertext, one for remote terminal access, and one for relaying electronic mail between mail servers. The protocol responsible for delivering (sending) email between mail servers is the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), defined in RFC 5321.

Application to this question

Here the question asks which protocol sends emails. SMTP supplies exactly this function: it defines the command sequence (HELO/EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA) that a sending mail server uses to hand a message to a receiving mail server, and it typically runs over TCP port 25 (or 587 for client submission).

Cross-check against the other protocols

  • HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) governs how a browser requests and a web server returns hypertext resources such as web pages; it carries no mail-relay commands.

  • FTP (File Transfer Protocol) governs uploading and downloading files between a client and a file server over separate control and data connections; it has no mail-header syntax.

  • Telnet governs opening an interactive text-based session on a remote host, sending keystrokes and receiving character output over a virtual terminal connection; it carries no email envelope or message-relay semantics.

Since only SMTP defines mail-relay commands between mail servers, SMTP is the protocol used to send emails.

title: TPSC Senior Computer Assistant — 2026 — Q69
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following is NOT an email protocol?
solution:
Concept

An application-layer protocol defines rules that network programs use to exchange a particular kind of data.

For electronic mail, transfer protocols send or relay messages, while access protocols retrieve and manage messages stored on a mail server.

Application

POP and IMAP are mail access protocols, and SMTP is a mail transfer protocol. SQL is a language for working with relational databases rather than a protocol for sending, relaying, or accessing email.

Contrast

  • POP: retrieves email from a mail server, commonly by downloading messages to a client.

  • SMTP: submits and relays email between clients and mail servers or between mail servers.

  • SQL: defines, queries, and modifies data in relational database systems.

  • IMAP: accesses and manages email while messages remain on the mail server.

Result

Therefore, SQL is the item that is not an email protocol.

title: MPPSC Paper 1 2026 Q21
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which protocol is used for sending e-mail?
solution:
Concept

Application-layer protocols define how a specific network service exchanges commands and data between programs.

For electronic mail, message submission and server-to-server relay use a dedicated push-style protocol over TCP; message retrieval uses separate access protocols.

Application

SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. A mail client can submit a message to a mail server, and mail servers can relay that message using SMTP commands such as EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, and DATA.

Contrast

  • FTP transfers files and directory listings through separate control and data connections.

  • HTTP transfers web resources through request-response exchanges.

  • TCP provides reliable, ordered transport to application protocols but does not itself define the electronic-mail submission workflow.

Result

Therefore, the protocol used for sending e-mail is SMTP.

title: Full form of IMAP?
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What is the full form of IMAP?
solution:
Full-form / acronym-expansion questions on networking protocols test both the exact standard wording and the protocol's underlying role. IMAP (RFC 3501) is one of the two dominant protocols — alongside POP3 — that a mail client uses to retrieve email from a server, and its core idea is letting the client repeatedly access messages that stay stored on the server, rather than downloading and removing them.

Expanding the acronym letter by letter:

  1. I — Internet: it operates over any standard Internet/TCP-IP connection.

  2. M — Message: it manages individual, stored email messages on the server.

  3. A — Access: its defining behaviour is giving the client ongoing access to those messages, not a one-time transfer.

  4. P — Protocol: a formally defined set of client-server communication rules.

Put together, this gives Internet Message Access Protocol. As a cross-check, contrast IMAP with POP3 (Post Office Protocol), which downloads mail and typically removes it from the server — IMAP's whole purpose is enabling multi-device access, which is exactly why an 'access' idea (not a one-time transfer) belongs in its name. This also rules out framings of IMAP as an international governance standard, a live chat/messaging service, an authority-granting mechanism, or a permission system — none of which match what IMAP actually does.

title: The cookie of HTTP client are stored at the which
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: The cookie of a HTTP client are stored at the which side of the system?
solution:
Answer: Cookies are stored on the client-side (in the user's browser).

Explanation:

  • How cookies work: Servers send cookies using the Set-Cookie HTTP header; the browser stores the cookie and automatically includes it with subsequent requests to the matching domain and path.

  • Cookies vs sessions: The cookie itself is stored client-side. Session data is typically stored server-side (in memory, files, or a database). The server usually issues a session identifier to the client via a cookie so it can link requests to the server-side session.

  • Types of cookies: Session cookies are deleted when the browser closes; persistent cookies remain until their expiration date.

  • Security note: Cookies can be protected using flags such as HttpOnly and Secure, and by restricting domain/path and using SameSite settings.

Therefore the correct response is the option that states cookies are stored client-side.

title: Which of the following is true about URL
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following is true about a URL ?

options.label: A
options.html: It is a Uniform Resource Locator

options.label: B
options.html: It is used to identify the source code of a website

options.label: C
options.html: It points to a specific IP address on the internet

options.label: D
options.html: It is a standard format for storing files on a server

solution: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. This is the literal, official name for a URL. Developed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994, a Uniform Resource Locator is a standardized string of characters that acts as a global address for identifying and locating resources on the World Wide Web.

title: The first part of complete URL is the needed to
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: The first part of a complete URL is the ________ needed to access the web resource.
solution:
Concept

A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a structured address that tells a browser both HOW to communicate and WHERE the resource lives. By the URI syntax (RFC 3986), the very first component of a complete URL is the scheme — commonly called the protocol — which names the communication method (for example http, https, ftp) to be used to reach the resource.

Application

Read a complete URL left to right and identify the leading segment:

  1. Take a concrete URL such as https://www.example.com/page.html.

  2. The portion before ://, here https, is the scheme/protocol. It comes FIRST and tells the browser which communication method to use.

  3. Only after the protocol come the host (www.example.com) and then the path (/page.html).

So the blank — the first part of a complete URL needed to access the resource — is filled by protocol.

Contrast

  • The host's name (the domain such as www.example.com) identifies the server, but it appears AFTER the scheme, not first.

  • A street- or memory-style address is not how a URL's leading component is named; the resource's machine address is resolved later from the host, not stated as the first part.

  • A generic location describes the whole URL's purpose (it locates a resource) rather than its first segment; the leading segment specifically names the access method.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q53
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What is a document found on the World Wide Web called?
solution:
CONCEPT

A web page is an individual resource designed to be displayed by a web browser. A website is a collection of web pages, while hyperlinks connect those pages and web crawlers discover them.

These terms describe different roles: content, collection, navigation, and automated discovery.

APPLICATION

The stem asks for the name of an individual document available on the World Wide Web. That object is a web page, so the offered value “A page” is the best match.

CONTRAST

  • A link is a reference used to navigate from one web resource to another.

  • A node is a general entity or connection point in a network or graph.

  • A spider is an automated program that follows links and retrieves web resources for indexing.

CROSS-CHECK

A browser displays a page; a link leads to a page; and a spider retrieves pages for indexing. The distinct roles confirm the terminology.

RESULT

A page.

title: Anuj is trying to transfer money to an agency from
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Anuj is trying to transfer money to an agency from his bank. On trying multiple times, connection to the bank failed. Because of the financial transactions, certain cookies helps to terminate the session when there is a time-out. These cookies are known as _____ cookies.
solution: Session cookies are temporary cookies that are created when a user logs into a website and are deleted when the user closes the browser or after a period of inactivity. They are used to maintain the user's session, such as keeping track of login status, shopping cart contents, or other temporary data. In the context of financial transactions, if a user's connection to the bank fails or they remain inactive for a certain period, the session cookie helps terminate the session automatically to ensure security and prevent unauthorized access.

title: Which one of the following allows the session to continue?
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which one of the following allows the session to continue?

options.label: B
options.html: When the user logs out and is invalidated by the servlet

options.label: C
options.html: When the session is timed out due to inactivity

options.label: D
options.html: When the user refreshes the browser and there is a persistent cookie

solution: A web session relies on the client (browser) identifying itself to the server, usually via a session ID stored in a cookie. When a user refreshes the browser, the browser re-sends this cookie to the server, allowing the server to recognize the user and keep the session active. In contrast, logging out (Option B) and timing out (Option C) explicitly terminate the session on the server side, while quitting the browser (Option A) typically clears non-persistent session cookies, effectively ending the active session. Therefore, only Option D describes a scenario where the session logic remains valid and continuous.

title: Suppose host also needed to use HTTP to download webpage
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Suppose host B also needed to use HTTP to download a webpage with four embedded image. The total number of RTT between the client and the server starting from initiates TCP connection to receive the Fourth object and close connection when using non- persistent HTTP without pipelining_______.
solution:
Answer (corrected): If you count only the four embedded images, the total is 8 RTT. If you include the initial HTML object plus the four embedded images, the total is 10 RTT.

Reasoning:

  • For non-persistent HTTP without pipelining, each object is fetched over a separate TCP connection.

  • Each new TCP connection requires 1 RTT for the TCP three-way handshake and 1 RTT for the HTTP request and for the first byte of the response to arrive. That is 2 RTT per object (handshake + request/response).

Calculations:

  • If counting only the four embedded images: 4 objects × 2 RTT per object = 8 RTT.

  • If including the initial HTML plus the four images: (1 + 4) objects × 2 RTT per object = 10 RTT.

Why the original solution was incorrect:

  • The original counted 3 RTT per file. That overcounts; the correct per-object cost is 2 RTT (one for TCP setup, one for the HTTP request/response).

title: Which HTTP status code is returned when requested web page
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which HTTP status code is returned when a requested web page has been permanently moved to a new URL?
solution:
Concept

HTTP response status codes classify the outcome of a request. The 3xx class contains redirection responses as well as related control responses such as 304 Not Modified.

A permanent redirect tells the client that the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI and that future references should use that URI.

Application

The stem describes a resource that has permanently moved. The HTTP code whose registered meaning is Moved Permanently is 301.

Cross-check and contrast

  • 200 OK describes successful processing of the current request.

  • 500 Internal Server Error describes an unexpected failure on the server.

  • 404 Not Found describes the absence of a current representation at the requested URI.

Result

Therefore, the required status code is 301 Moved Permanently.

title: Which protocol operates at the application layer and is used
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which protocol operates at the application layer and is used for secure web browsing ?
solution: The correct answer is HTTPS because it stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure, which operates at the application layer and encrypts data transmitted between a web browser and a server. This encryption ensures secure communication, protecting sensitive information like passwords and credit card details from interception during web browsing. title: Which FTP transfer mode reduces data size during transmission to
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which FTP transfer mode reduces data size during transmission to improve bandwidth efficiency?
solution:
FTP (File Transfer Protocol, RFC 959) supports three data transmission modes:

1. Stream mode — the file is sent as a continuous stream of bytes, exactly as stored, with no extra processing. This is the default mode.

2. Block mode — the file is sent as a series of data blocks, each preceded by a header that carries a byte count and descriptor codes.

3. Compressed mode — the data is compressed before transmission. It uses run-length encoding: a run of n identical data bytes is replaced by a short two-byte code, and long strings of filler bytes are collapsed into a single byte.

Only the compressed (compression) mode reduces the size of the data during transmission, which increases bandwidth efficiency on large transfers at a small extra CPU cost. Encapsulation, multiplexing and fragmentation are general networking concepts, not FTP transmission modes, and none of them compresses the data.

Hence the correct answer is Compression Mode.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q3
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: What does FTP stand for?
solution:
Concept

A network protocol is a standardized set of rules that lets computers communicate. An initialism uses the first letters of the words in its expanded name.

Application-layer protocols provide services directly used by network applications, such as moving files between a client and a server.

Application

In the initialism FTP, F represents File, T represents Transfer, and P represents Protocol. FTP therefore names the application-layer protocol used to transfer files across a network.

Contrast

  • Faster Than Post is an informal comparison about delivery speed.

  • Files To Publish is a phrase about documents selected for publication.

  • Format To Program is a phrase about preparing or formatting material for a program.

Cross-check

The Internet Engineering Task Force specification RFC 959 is titled “File Transfer Protocol (FTP),” which independently confirms the expansion.

Result

FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.

title: Which of the following statements best reflects how File Transfer

bodyHtml: Which of the following statements best reflects how File Transfer Protocol (FTP) functions at the Application Layer in a network system?

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.html: FTP secures files during transmission using UDP and built-in encryption.

options.label: D
options.html: FTP is primarily used to send emails with file attachments.

solution:
The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) operates at the Application Layer of the OSI model and uses a distinct, dual-connection architecture over TCP to manage file transfers reliably.

Instead of passing everything through a single channel, FTP splits the responsibilities into two separate TCP connections:

  1. Control Connection (Port 21): Used for sending commands and receiving responses (e.g., user authentication, browsing directories, requesting transfers). This connection remains open throughout the entire FTP session.

  2. Data Connection (Port 20 in Active Mode): Created dynamically every time a file transfer or directory listing is actually requested. This connection closes immediately after the data transfer finishes.

title: If Host and starts transmitting at the same time and
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: If Host B and C starts transmitting at the same time and collision occurs , then which host will receive a collision jamming signal
solution:
Answer: Hosts A, B and C receive the collision jamming signal.

Why: The hub is a Layer 1 repeater that forwards electrical signals to all ports, so it does not separate collision domains. When two hosts on the hub transmit at the same time, their frames collide and the collision (and any jam signal) is seen by every device on that shared medium.

  • Because Hosts B and C are connected to the same hub, the collision is confined to that hub's collision domain and will be received by Hosts A, B, and C.

  • Host D and the router are connected via a switch, which separates collision domains at each port, so they do not receive the hub's collision jamming signal.

  • Therefore the correct set of hosts that receive the collision jamming signal is Hosts A, B, and C.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q133
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: In a large enterprise network, which situation most strongly indicates the need for implementing VLANs rather than adding more physical switches ?

options.label: A
options.html: Bandwidth on trunk links is fully utilized

options.label: B
options.html: Devices need to be grouped logically rather than physically

options.label: D
options.html: The number of broadcast domains must be reduced

solution:
Concept: VLANs (Virtual LANs) let devices be placed into the same logical group -- by function, department, or project -- independent of the physical switch port, floor, or building they are wired into. On a purely physical switch topology, even with many additional switches, a device's group membership is fixed by whichever switch port it happens to be cabled into; moving a device into a different group means either re-patching a cable or reconfiguring that specific port. VLAN tagging (802.1Q) turns group membership into a port/configuration setting that can be reassigned from the switch's management interface without any new cable run, and that setting can be applied consistently across every switch in the trunked fabric.

Application: Checking each situation against this rule:

  1. Devices needing to be grouped logically rather than physically is exactly the situation additional physical switches cannot fix on their own: no matter how many switches are added, a device's group membership stays tied to whichever port it is physically cabled into unless VLANs are configured on the relevant ports (or, under dynamic VLAN assignment, tied to the device's identity) -- something plain physical wiring or extra switch hardware does not provide by itself.

  2. Trunk-link bandwidth being fully used is a link-capacity constraint, resolved by adding physical capacity to that link -- a faster trunk, an extra parallel uplink, or link aggregation -- rather than by any logical-segmentation feature.

  3. Collision domains growing too large is not a persistent problem on a modern full-duplex switched network: each switch port already forms its own separate, single-device collision domain, independent of how many switches or VLANs are configured.

  4. Needing the number of broadcast domains reduced runs the opposite direction from what VLANs do: configuring VLANs splits one flat broadcast domain into several smaller ones, which increases the total count of broadcast domains while shrinking each one's span. Wanting fewer broadcast domains would call for merging domains together, not adding VLAN segmentation.

Cross-check: This lines up with the standard Layer-2 segmentation principle -- VLANs provide logical, configuration-based grouping that is independent of physical wiring, which is the one property plain physical switch hardware cannot replicate by itself. Collision-domain size is already minimized per port on any switched network regardless of switch or VLAN count, and trunk-capacity limits are addressed by adding link capacity; only logical group independence from physical wiring specifically calls for VLANs.

title: Which of this is not network edge device? Asked in

title: Which of the following statements are false?
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which of the following statements are false?

options.label: A
options.html: A bridge uses IP address, while a router uses MAC address

options.label: B
options.html: The efficiency of ethernet increases with decrease in propagation delay and decrease in transmission delay

options.label: C
options.html: The efficiency of ethernet increases with decrease in propagation delay and increase in transmission delay

options.label: D
options.html: Router can connect between a LAN and a WAN

solution:
To determine which statements are false, analyze each option based on networking principles.

Option A: A bridge uses IP address, while a router uses MAC address

A bridge operates at the data link layer and uses MAC addresses to forward frames. A router operates at the network layer and uses IP addresses to route packets. This option incorrectly swaps the functions of bridge and router, making it false.

Option B: The efficiency of ethernet increases with decrease in propagation delay and decrease in transmission delay

Ethernet efficiency is given by the formula: Efficiency = 1 / (1 + 2a), where a = Tp / Tt. Here, Tp is propagation delay and Tt is transmission delay. As Tp decreases and Tt decreases, the value of 'a' decreases, which increases efficiency. This option correctly identifies the relationship between delays and efficiency, making it true.

Option C: The efficiency of ethernet increases with decrease in propagation delay and increase in transmission delay

Using the same formula, Efficiency = 1 / (1 + 2a), where a = Tp / Tt. If Tp decreases and Tt increases, 'a' decreases, which increases efficiency. However, this option incorrectly implies that increasing Tt alone increases efficiency, which is misleading because it ignores the effect of Tp. The statement is false because it misrepresents the relationship between delays and efficiency.

Option D: Router can connect between a LAN and a WAN

Routers operate at the network layer and are designed to connect different networks, including LANs and WANs. This option correctly describes the role of a router, making it true.

Therefore, the false statements are Option A and Option C.

title: Which internetworking devices can separate collision domains
subject: Computer Networks
bodyHtml: Which internetworking devices can separate collision domains
solution:
Correct answer: Router and Switch.

  • Switch: Separates collision domains per port. Each switch port is its own collision domain, so devices on different switch ports do not contend for the same collisions.

  • Router: Separates collision domains per interface. A router does not forward collisions between interfaces and also separates broadcast domains.

  • Hubs and repeaters: Operate at Layer 1 and extend a single collision domain; they do not separate collision domains.

Summary: The devices that separate collision domains are switches and routers; hubs and repeaters do not.

This distinguishes them from other devices that function at different layers.",

bodyHtml: Which device is used to connect two or more networks and forward packets between them ?
