title: Car travels from point to at speed of km/hr and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A car travels from point A to B at a speed of 60 km/hr and returns back to point A at a speed of 40 km/hr. What is the average speed of the car during the whole journey?
solution:
To find the average speed for the entire journey, we use the formula for average speed, which is total distance divided by total time. The distance traveled is the same for both legs of the journey, so let's call that distance "d".

Time to go from A to B = d / 60 hours

Time to return from B to A = d / 40 hours

Total time for the journey = d/60 + d/40 = (2d + 3d) / 120 = 5d / 120 = d / 24 hours

Total distance = 2d (since the car travels to B and then returns to A)

So, the average speed = (2d) / (d/24) = 2d × (24/d) = 48 km/hr.

title: Flight has to travel between cities and km apart. The
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A flight has to travel between 2 cities A and B, 3000 km apart. The flight was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip reduced by 200 km/hr and the time of flight increased by 30 min. The duration of the original speed is:
solution:
Concept

For a fixed distance, time = distance ÷ speed. If the same distance is covered at two different speeds, the difference between the two travel times equals the stated change. Writing that time difference as an equation in the unknown original speed lets you solve for it, after which the original duration follows directly.

Application

  1. Let the original speed be x km/hr. Original time = 3000/x hours.

  2. Reduced speed = (x − 200) km/hr, so the new time = 3000/(x − 200) hours.

  3. The journey takes 30 min = 0.5 hr longer, so 3000/(x − 200) − 3000/x = 0.5.

  4. Combine over a common denominator: [3000x − 3000(x − 200)] / [x(x − 200)] = 0.5, i.e. 600000 / [x(x − 200)] = 0.5.

  5. Cross-multiply: x(x − 200) = 1200000, giving x2 − 200x − 1200000 = 0.

  6. Factorise: (x − 1200)(x + 1000) = 0. Speed must be positive, so x = 1200 km/hr.

  7. Original duration = distance ÷ speed = 3000 ÷ 1200 = 2.5 hours.

Cross-check

At 1200 km/hr the trip takes 2.5 hr; at 1000 km/hr it takes 3000/1000 = 3 hr. The difference is exactly 0.5 hr = 30 min, matching the given condition.

title: Rohit travels from point to point at the speed of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Rohit travels from point A to point B at the speed of 16 km/hr and reaches point B at 3 p.m. He will reach point B at 2 p.m. if he travels at an average speed of 20 km/hr. At what average speed (in km/hr) should Rohit travel to reach point B at 1 p.m.?
solution:
Step-by-Step Solution

  1. Understand the Relationship: Since the distance between point A and point B is constant, the product of speed and time must be equal for different scenarios (Distance = Speed × Time). Let the distance be D and the time taken at 16 km/hr be t hours.

  2. Set up the Equations:

    • Scenario 1: At 16 km/hr, time = t. So, D = 16 × t.

    • Scenario 2: At 20 km/hr, he reaches 1 hour earlier (3 p.m. to 2 p.m.), so time = t - 1. So, D = 20 × (t - 1).

  3. Solve for t:

    • 16t = 20(t - 1)

    • 16t = 20t - 20

    • 4t = 20

    • t = 5 hours.

  4. Find the Distance (D):

    • D = 16 km/hr × 5 hours = 80 km.

  5. Calculate Required Speed:

    • To reach at 1 p.m. (which is 2 hours earlier than 3 p.m.), the time taken should be t - 2 = 5 - 2 = 3 hours.

    • Required Speed = Distance / Required Time = 80 km / 3 hours = 26 and 2/3 km/hr.

title: Person jogs at three times the speed of walking and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A person jogs at three times the speed of walking and runs at twice the speed of jogging. From his home to his office, he covers one-third of the distance by walking and the rest by jogging. On his way back home from office, he covers half the distance by jogging and the rest by running. The distance from his home to his office is 10 km, and he walks at a speed of 5 km/hr. Find his average speed (in km/hr) for the complete round trip (up to two decimal places).
solution:
Concept — Average speed is never the plain average of the separate speeds used on a journey. It is defined as total distance divided by total time. So whenever a trip is broken into stretches covered at different speeds, each stretch's time must be found on its own from time = distance ÷ speed, all those times added up, and only then is the total distance divided by that total time.

Application — Fix the three speeds from the given ratios, then time each of the four stretches of the round trip.

  1. Walking speed = 5 km/hr. Jogging is three times walking, so jogging = 3 × 5 = 15 km/hr. Running is twice jogging, so running = 2 × 15 = 30 km/hr.

  2. Home to office, walking stretch: one-third of 10 km = 10/3 km at 5 km/hr, so time = (10/3) ÷ 5 = 2/3 hr.

  3. Home to office, jogging stretch: the remaining 20/3 km at 15 km/hr, so time = (20/3) ÷ 15 = 4/9 hr.

  4. Office to home, jogging stretch: half of 10 km = 5 km at 15 km/hr, so time = 5 ÷ 15 = 1/3 hr.

  5. Office to home, running stretch: the remaining 5 km at 30 km/hr, so time = 5 ÷ 30 = 1/6 hr.

  6. Total time = 2/3 + 4/9 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 12/18 + 8/18 + 6/18 + 3/18 = 29/18 hr.

  7. Total distance = 10 + 10 = 20 km, so average speed = 20 ÷ (29/18) = 20 × 18/29 = 360/29 = 12.4137… ≈ 12.41 km/hr.

Cross-check — Collapse each 10 km leg into a single leg average speed and recombine the two legs independently.

  • Onward leg: 10 km in 2/3 + 4/9 = 10/9 hr, so the onward leg averages 10 ÷ (10/9) = 9 km/hr.

  • Return leg: 10 km in 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 hr, so the return leg averages 10 ÷ (1/2) = 20 km/hr.

  • The two legs are equal in distance, so the round-trip average is the harmonic mean of the leg speeds: (2 × 9 × 20) ÷ (9 + 20) = 360/29 ≈ 12.41 km/hr — the same value, reached by an independent route.

  • Note that the arithmetic mean of 9 and 20 is 14.5 km/hr, which is not the average speed of the trip; that gap is exactly what the concept above warns against.

Average speed for the complete round trip = 12.41 km/hr.

title: Rohit travelled km from home to school, km from school
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Rohit travelled 1⅛ km from home to school, 5/6 km from school to skating rink, 2/3 km from skating rink to work and 1/4 km from work to home in 4 hours, 3 hours, 2 hours and 1 hour, respectively. Then the average speed of Rohit is
solution:
CONCEPT: Average speed for a journey made up of several legs is the TOTAL distance covered divided by the TOTAL time taken — it is NOT the average of the individual leg speeds.

APPLICATION:

  1. Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 1⅛ km = 9/8 km.

  2. Write every leg's distance over the common denominator 24 (the LCM of 8, 6, 3 and 4): 9/8 = 27/24 km, 5/6 = 20/24 km, 2/3 = 16/24 km, 1/4 = 6/24 km.

  3. Add the four distances: total distance = (27 + 20 + 16 + 6)/24 = 69/24 = 23/8 km.

  4. Add the four times: total time = 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 hours.

  5. Average speed = total distance / total time = (23/8) / 10 = 23/80 km/hour.

CROSS-CHECK: Multiplying 23/80 km/hour back by the total time of 10 hours gives 23/8 km, which matches the independently-computed total distance, confirming the result.

title: IOCL - Junior Engineering Assistant IV - Mechanical - 2024 — Q78
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक लड़का 13 km/h की चाल से स्कूल जाता है। वह 7 km/h की चाल से वापस आता है। उसे स्कूल जाने और स्कूल से वापस आने में कुल 3 घंटे लगते हैं। उसके घर और स्कूल के बीच की दूरी (km में) ज्ञात कीजिए। उत्तर को निकटतम 0.1 km तक पूर्णांकित कीजिए; ठीक आधा आने पर अगले दसवें भाग की ओर पूर्णांकित करें।
solution:
अवधारणा

चाल = दूरी ÷ समय, इसलिए समय = दूरी ÷ चाल। समान दूरी की दो यात्राओं का कुल समय दोनों यात्राओं के अलग-अलग समयों का योग होता है।

यदि एक तरफ की दूरी d km है, तो कुल समय d/13 + d/7 होगा। पहले d का सटीक मान निकालते हैं, फिर प्रश्न के अनुसार उसे निकटतम 0.1 km तक पूर्णांकित करते हैं।

प्रयोग

  1. एक तरफ की दूरी d km मानें। जाने का समय d/13 घंटे और लौटने का समय d/7 घंटे है।

  2. कुल समय 3 घंटे है, इसलिए d/13 + d/7 = 3।

  3. समान हर लेने पर (7d + 13d)/91 = 3, अर्थात 20d/91 = 3।

  4. दोनों पक्षों को 91/20 से गुणा करने पर d = 3 × 91/20 = 273/20 = 13.65 km।

  5. 13.65 को निकटतम 0.1 km तक पूर्णांकित करने पर 13.7 km मिलता है।

पुनः जाँच

13.65/13 = 1.05 घंटे और 13.65/7 = 1.95 घंटे; इनका योग 3 घंटे है। अतः घर और स्कूल के बीच की दूरी, निकटतम 0.1 km तक, 13.7 km है।

subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A person travels from A to B at a speed of 4 km/h and returns from B to A at a speed of 5 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey, in km/h?
solution:
Concept: For a two-leg round trip where the same distance is covered at two different speeds, the average speed for the whole journey is not the arithmetic mean of the two speeds — the time spent at each speed differs. The correct measure is total distance travelled divided by total time taken, which for two equal-distance legs simplifies to the harmonic mean of the two speeds: 2 × v1 × v2 / (v1 + v2).

Application:

  1. Let the one-way distance from A to B be x km.

  2. Time for the outward leg at 4 km/h = x/4 hours.

  3. Time for the return leg at 5 km/h = x/5 hours.

  4. Total distance covered = 2x km. Total time taken = x/4 + x/5 = 9x/20 hours.

  5. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 2x ÷ (9x/20) = 40/9 ≈ 4.44 km/h.

Cross-check: Applying the harmonic-mean formula directly: 2 × 4 × 5 / (4 + 5) = 40/9 ≈ 4.44 km/h — the same result, confirming the derivation.

Answer: 4.44 km/h.

title: Car covers the first km of journey at speed of

bodyHtml: A Car covers the first 40 km of a journey at a speed of 20km/h and next 60 km at 30 km/h. What is the average speed (inkm / h) of the car for the entire journey?
solution:
Solution: Compute the average speed for the entire journey.

  • Total distance = 40 km + 60 km = 100 km.

  • Time for first part = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 hours.

  • Time for second part = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 hours.

  • Total time = 2 + 2 = 4 hours.

  • Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 km/h.

Therefore the average speed for the entire journey is 25 km/h.

title: Sharad completes his journey in hours. He covers half the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Sharad completes his journey in 11 hours. He covers half the distance of the journey at a speed of 20 km/hr and the remaining distance at a speed of 30 km/hr. Find the distance of the journey (in km).
solution:
For a journey split into two equal-distance legs travelled at speeds v1 and v2, total time = (half-distance ÷ v1) + (half-distance ÷ v2). Equivalently, the average speed for such a journey is the harmonic mean 2·v1·v2/(v1+v2), and total distance = average speed × total time.

Applying this to Sharad's journey:

  1. Let the total distance of the journey be D km, so each half of the journey is D/2 km.

  2. Time taken on the first half at 20 km/hr = (D/2) ÷ 20 = D/40 hours.

  3. Time taken on the second half at 30 km/hr = (D/2) ÷ 30 = D/60 hours.

  4. Total time = D/40 + D/60 = (3D + 2D)/120 = 5D/120 = D/24 hours.

  5. The question states the total journey takes 11 hours, so D/24 = 11.

  6. Solving for D: D = 11 × 24 = 264 km.

Cross-check using the average-speed formula: average speed = (2 × 20 × 30)/(20 + 30) = 1200/50 = 24 km/hr, and distance = average speed × time = 24 × 11 = 264 km, which matches. Direct verification: half of 264 km is 132 km; 132 ÷ 20 = 6.6 hours and 132 ÷ 30 = 4.4 hours, and 6.6 + 4.4 = 11 hours, exactly as given.

Hence, the distance of the journey is 264 km.

title: IOCL 2024 Numerical Ability Q89
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक कार का ओडोमीटर, यात्रा की शुरुआत में 12100 km और यात्रा की अंत में 12460 km प्रदर्शित करता है। यदि यात्रा में 4 घंटे लगे, तो कार की औसत चाल m/sec में ज्ञात कीजिए।
solution: ओडोमीटर द्वारा दर्शाई गई प्रारंभिक और अंतिम पठन के अंतर से तय दूरी \(12460 - 12100 = 360\) km मिलती है। समय 4 घंटे है, इसलिए औसत चाल \(\frac{360}{4} = 90\) km/h है। किमी प्रति घंटे को मीटर प्रति सेकंड में बदलने के लिए \(\frac{1000}{3600}\) से गुणा किया जाता है: \(90 \times \frac{1000}{3600} = 25\) m/s।

title: Hari and Ravi started race from opposite ends of the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Hari and Ravi started a race from opposite ends of the pool. After a minute and a half, they passed each other in the center of the pool. If they lost no time in turning and maintained their respective speeds, how many minutes after starting did they pass each other the second time?
solution:
Key insight: meeting at the centre after 1.5 minutes means both swimmers have equal speeds.

  • At 1.5 minutes: they meet at the centre.

  • Next 1.5 minutes (by 3 minutes): each swimmer reaches the opposite end.

  • Next 1.5 minutes (by 4.5 minutes): they swim back toward the centre and meet there for the second time.

Therefore, they meet the second time 4 ½ minutes after the start.

title: Train long passes in electric pole in seconds and another
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train 120 m long crosses an electric pole in 12 seconds. It crosses another train of the same length, travelling in the opposite direction, in 8 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
solution:
Concept: When a train crosses a stationary object such as an electric pole, the distance covered equals the train's own length, so its speed is simply length divided by time. When two trains cross each other while travelling in OPPOSITE directions, the total distance covered between them is the SUM of their two lengths, and because they are approaching each other, their individual speeds ADD together to give this combined (relative) speed: relative speed = v1 + v2 = (l1 + l2) / time.

Application:

  1. The first train's own speed is found from the pole-crossing: v1 = 120 m / 12 s = 10 m/s.

  2. When the two trains cross each other, the combined length to be covered is 120 m + 120 m = 240 m.

  3. The combined (relative) speed of the two trains is therefore 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s, which equals v1 + v2.

  4. The second train's speed is v2 = 30 - 10 = 20 m/s.

  5. Converting to km/hr: 20 m/s x 18/5 = 72 km/hr.

Cross-check: Redoing the whole calculation directly in km/hr confirms this independently: the first train's speed is 10 m/s x 18/5 = 36 km/hr; the combined relative speed is 30 m/s x 18/5 = 108 km/hr; so the second train's speed is 108 - 36 = 72 km/hr, matching the earlier result.

title: Badri and Vasu are running at the same speed of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Badri and Vasu are running at the same speed of 12 kms/hr. However, Badri started an hour earlier than Vasu. The distance between source and destination is 200 kms. After Vasu has covered 40 kms, he decides to increase his speed so that both of them reach the destination on time. By how much should Vasu increase his speed (in kms/hr)?
solution:
To find out how much Vasu must increase his speed, we need to calculate the time constraints for both runners to reach the 200 km destination.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Calculate Badri's total travel time:

Badri travels 200 km at 12 km/hr.

Time = Distance / Speed = 200 / 12 = 50/3 hours (approx. 16.67 hours).

Calculate Vasu's remaining time:

Badri started 1 hour earlier, so Vasu has 1 hour less to complete the journey.

Total time available for Vasu = (50/3) - 1 = 47/3 hours.

Analyze Vasu's journey:

Vasu has already covered 40 km at 12 km/hr.

Time taken for the first 40 km = 40 / 12 = 10/3 hours.

Remaining distance for Vasu = 200 - 40 = 160 km.

Remaining time for Vasu = (47/3) - (10/3) = 37/3 hours.

Calculate the required speed for the remaining distance:

Required Speed = Remaining Distance / Remaining Time = 160 / (37/3) = 480/37 km/hr.

Calculate the required increase:

Original speed = 12 km/hr = 444/37 km/hr.

Increase = (480/37) - (444/37) = 36/37 km/hr.

36 / 37 is approximately 0.9729 km/hr.

title: In kilometer race, beats by meters or by seconds. What
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a kilometer race, A beats B by 80 meters or by 10 seconds. What is the time taken by A over the course?
solution:
Concept

In a race where one runner beats another “by a distance or by a time”, both descriptions refer to the SAME finishing gap. The loser still has that distance left to run when the winner finishes, and the stated time is exactly how long the loser needs to cover that leftover distance. So the leftover distance divided by the stated time gives the loser’s speed, from which the loser’s full-course time follows, and the winner’s time is that minus the time gap.

Application

  1. Course length = 1000 m. When A finishes, B is 80 m behind, i.e. B has 80 m still to run, and B needs 10 s to cover those 80 m.

  2. Speed of B = leftover distance ÷ leftover time = 80 m ÷ 10 s = 8 m/s.

  3. Time for B to run the full 1000 m = 1000 ÷ 8 = 125 s.

  4. A finishes 10 s before B, so time taken by A = 125 − 10 = 115 s.

Cross-check

Speed of A = 1000 m ÷ 115 s ≈ 8.696 m/s. In A’s 115 s, B (at 8 m/s) runs 8 × 115 = 920 m, which is exactly 80 m short of 1000 m — matching the “beats by 80 m” condition. Both clues are satisfied.

Time taken by A over the course = 115 seconds.

title: Two friends and leave City and City simultaneously and travel
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Two friends A and B leave City P and City Q simultaneously and travel towards Q and P at constant speeds. They meet at a point in between the two cities and then proceed to their respective destinations in 54 minutes and 24 minutes respectively. How long did B take to cover the entire journey between City Q and City P?
solution:
Let the speed of the friend starting from City P be a and the speed of the friend starting from City Q be b. Let t minutes be the time until they meet.

Distance traveled by the friend from P before meeting = a·t. Distance traveled by the friend from Q before meeting = b·t.

After meeting, the friend from P takes 54 minutes to reach Q, so the remaining distance for that friend is a·54. After meeting, the friend from Q takes 24 minutes to reach P, so the remaining distance for that friend is b·24.

Because the two parts of the route meet at the same point, the distance the friend from P travels after meeting equals the distance the friend from Q traveled before meeting, and vice versa. Therefore:

  • b·t = a·54

  • a·t = b·24

Multiply the two equations:

(a·t)·(b·t) = (a·54)·(b·24) ⇒ ab·t² = ab·(54·24) ⇒ t² = 54·24

So t = √(54·24) = 36 minutes.

The friend from Q took 24 minutes after meeting plus the 36 minutes before meeting, so the total time for that friend to travel from City Q to City P is 36 + 24 = 60 minutes.

Answer: 60 minutes.

bodyHtml:
Two cars, X and Y, start from points 360 km apart and travel at constant speeds. If they move towards each

title: DSSSB TGT Hindi 23 Aug 2025 Shift 3 Q48
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a 2000 m race, vehicle A gives vehicle B a start of 300 m and still wins the race by 10 seconds. Alternatively, if vehicle A gives vehicle B a start of 500 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle A take to run 2000 m?
solution:
Concept

In a race with a "start", the runner receiving the start needs to cover only (race distance − start) while the other runs the full distance in the same time window. If the race ends in a dead heat, both take equal time to finish their respective distances; if one wins by t seconds, the other's time exceeds the winner's time by t seconds. Equating these times for two different start values gives two equations in the two speeds, which can be solved together.

Application

Let the speed of vehicle A be a m/s and the speed of vehicle B be b m/s over the 2000 m race.

  1. With a start of 500 m, B only has to cover 2000 − 500 = 1500 m while A covers the full 2000 m, and the race ends in a dead heat, so both take the same time: 2000/a = 1500/b.

  2. This gives the speed ratio a/b = 2000/1500 = 4/3, i.e., b = (3/4)a.

  3. With a start of 300 m, B only has to cover 2000 − 300 = 1700 m, and A wins by 10 seconds, so B's time exceeds A's time by 10 seconds: 1700/b − 2000/a = 10.

  4. Substituting b = (3/4)a: 1700 / ((3/4)a) − 2000/a = 10, which simplifies to (6800/3 − 2000)/a = 10, i.e., 800/(3a) = 10.

  5. Solving, 3a = 80, so a = 80/3 m/s.

  6. Vehicle A's time to run 2000 m = 2000 ÷ (80/3) = 2000 × 3/80 = 75 seconds = 1 minute 15 seconds.

Cross-check

With a = 80/3 m/s, b = (3/4)(80/3) = 20 m/s. In the 300 m-start race, B covers 1700 m in 1700/20 = 85 s while A covers 2000 m in 75 s — a winning margin of 85 − 75 = 10 seconds, matching the given condition. In the 500 m-start race, B covers 1500 m in 1500/20 = 75 s, exactly equal to A's 75 s, confirming the dead heat. Both conditions check out, so A takes 1 minute 15 seconds to run 2000 m.

title: Train covers distance of km in hours. What is its
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train covers a distance of 300 km in 5 hours. What is its speed?
solution:
We use the formula Speed = Distance / Time.

Distance is 300 km and Time is 5 hours.

So, 300 km / 5 hr = 60 km/hr.

title: Train meters long travelling at km/hr crosses the bridge in
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train 130 meters long travelling at 36 km/hr crosses the bridge in 30 sec. Then the length of the bridge is:
solution:
Concept

When a train crosses a bridge (or any platform), the distance it must travel equals the train's own length PLUS the length of the bridge, because the train is fully clear only after its rear end leaves the far end of the bridge.

The governing relation is: Distance = Speed × Time, and Distance covered = Length of train + Length of bridge.

Application

  1. Convert the speed from km/hr to m/s: multiply by 5/18. So 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

  2. Find the total distance covered in the given time: Distance = Speed × Time = 10 × 30 = 300 m.

  3. This total distance equals train length + bridge length: 300 = 130 + (bridge length).

  4. Solve for the bridge length: 300 − 130 = 170 m.

Cross-check

Add the parts back: train (130 m) + bridge (170 m) = 300 m, and at 10 m/s the train covers 300 m in 300/10 = 30 s, which matches the given time. Hence the bridge is 170 m long.

title: Train running at the speed of km/hr passed man in
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train running at the speed of 72 km/hr passed a man in 14 sec and a platform in 32 sec respectively. Find the length of the platform.
solution:
Correct Option
Option A: 360 meter

Step-by-Step Solution
Convert Speed from km/hr to m/s:

To convert 72 km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Speed = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s.

Calculate the Length of the Train:

The train passes a man in 14 seconds. When a train passes a man, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train.

Train Length = Speed * Time = 20 m/s * 14 s = 280 meters.

Calculate the Total Distance (Train + Platform):

The train passes a platform in 32 seconds.

Total Distance = Speed * Time = 20 m/s * 32 s = 640 meters.

Calculate the Length of the Platform:

Platform Length = Total Distance - Train Length = 640 meters - 280 meters = 360 meters.

title: Train travelled at an average speed of km/hr, stopping for
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train travelled at an average speed of 100 km/hr, stopping for 5 minutes after every 75 km. How long does it take to reach its destination 600 km from the starting point ?
solution:
Correct Option
Option B: 6 hrs. 35 mins

Step-by-Step Solution
Calculate the pure travel time:

The total distance is 600 km and the average speed is 100 km/hr.

Travel Time = Distance / Speed = 600 / 100 = 6 hours.

Determine the number of stops:

The train stops after every 75 km.

Total segments = 600 / 75 = 8 segments.

Since the train does not stop after the final segment (because it has reached its destination), the number of stops is 8 - 1 = 7 stops.

Calculate the total stoppage time:

Each stop is 5 minutes.

Total Stoppage Time = 7 stops * 5 minutes/stop = 35 minutes.

Calculate the total time:

Total Time = Travel Time + Stoppage Time = 6 hours + 35 minutes = 6 hours and 35 minutes.

title: Bus passes two bridges of length and in seconds and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A bus passes two bridges of length 500 m and 325 m in 90 seconds and 60 seconds respectively. The length (in m) of the bus is
solution:
Let the length of the bus be L metres and its speed be v m/s.

While crossing a bridge, the bus covers its own length plus the bridge length.

For the 500 m bridge: (L + 500)/v = 90.

For the 325 m bridge: (L + 325)/v = 60.

Divide the equations: (L + 500)/(L + 325) = 90/60 = 3/2.

2(L + 500) = 3(L + 325) gives 2L + 1000 = 3L + 975, so L = 25 m.

title: Train meters long travelling at km/hr crosses the bridge in
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train 130 meters long travelling at 54 km/hr crosses the bridge in 30 sec. Then the length of the bridge is:
solution:
Concept

When a train crosses a bridge (or platform), the train must travel a distance equal to its OWN length PLUS the length of the bridge, because the rear of the train only clears the far end after moving that combined distance. Distance = speed x time, and a speed in km/hr is converted to m/s by multiplying by 5/18.

Application

  1. Convert the speed: 54 km/hr = 54 x 5/18 = 15 m/s.

  2. Total distance covered while crossing = speed x time = 15 m/s x 30 s = 450 m.

  3. This total distance equals train length + bridge length, so bridge length = 450 - 130 = 320 m.

Cross-check

Add the bridge length back to the train length: 320 + 130 = 450 m. At 15 m/s, covering 450 m takes 450 / 15 = 30 s, which matches the given time. So the bridge is 320 m long.

title: Flyover has three spans whose lengths are in the ratio
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A flyover has three spans whose lengths are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. A bus whose length is one-fifth of the total length of the flyover takes t seconds to cross the first span. How many seconds does it take to cross the full flyover?
solution:
Concept

When a vehicle crosses a fixed object such as a bridge or flyover, the distance covered is the fixed object length plus the vehicle length.

At constant speed, time is proportional to this total crossing distance, not to the fixed object length alone.

Application

  1. Let the three span lengths be 2x, 3x, and 5x, so the total flyover length is 10x.

  2. The bus length is one fifth of the total flyover length, so the bus length is 2x.

  3. To cross the first span, the bus covers the first span plus its own length: 2x + 2x = 4x. Since this takes t seconds, its speed is 4x/t.

  4. To cross the full flyover, the bus covers the flyover plus its own length: 10x + 2x = 12x.

  5. The full crossing time is 12x divided by 4x/t, which equals 3t.

Cross-check

The measured first-span crossing distance is 4x, while the full crossing distance is 12x. The ratio 12x : 4x is 3 : 1, so the required time is 3t seconds.

title: Two trains meters and meters long are running in the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Two trains 200 meters and 240 meters long are running in the same direction with speeds of 82 km/hr and 64 km/hr, respectively. In how much time will the first train cross the second?
solution:
When two bodies move in the same direction, the relative speed between them is the difference of their individual speeds, since the faster one is only gaining on the slower one at that reduced rate. To completely cross each other, the faster body must cover a distance equal to the sum of both lengths, measured at this relative speed. A speed in km/hr converts to m/s by multiplying by 5/18.

  1. The trains travel in the same direction, so the relative speed is the difference of their speeds: 82 km/hr minus 64 km/hr = 18 km/hr.

  2. Convert this relative speed to m/s: 18 multiplied by 5/18 = 5 m/s.

  3. To completely cross, the first train must cover a distance equal to the sum of both lengths: 200 m + 240 m = 440 m.

  4. Time taken = distance divided by relative speed = 440 m divided by 5 m/s = 88 seconds.

Cross-check: converting each speed to m/s first gives 82 x 5/18 which is approximately 22.78 m/s and 64 x 5/18 which is approximately 17.78 m/s; their difference is again 5 m/s exactly, confirming the time is 440 divided by 5 = 88 seconds.

title: Train running at km/h crosses pole in seconds. How much
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a pole in 12 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take to cross a bridge 360 m long?
solution:
When a train crosses a stationary point object such as a pole, signal, or person, the distance it covers equals the train's own length, since only the engine-to-last-coach length needs to pass that point. When it crosses an extended object such as a bridge or platform of length L, the distance covered equals the train's own length plus L, because the front must clear the full extended length before the last coach also clears it. The train's speed stays the same in both crossings, so distance = speed x time applies identically each time.

  1. Convert the speed to consistent units: 72 km/h x 5/18 = 20 m/s.

  2. Crossing the pole covers only the train's own length: length = speed x time = 20 x 12 = 240 m.

  3. Crossing the 360 m bridge covers the train's length plus the bridge's length: total distance = 240 + 360 = 600 m.

  4. Time to cross the bridge = total distance / speed = 600 / 20 = 30 seconds.

This can be checked with an equivalent route: the extra distance beyond the pole-crossing is exactly the bridge's own 360 m, which takes 360 / 20 = 18 s at the same speed; adding that to the 12 s already needed to clear the pole gives 12 + 18 = 30 s, the same result.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q64
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train crosses a pole in 15 secs, while it crosses 100 metre long railway platform in 25 secs. The length of the train is
solution:
Concept: When a train crosses a stationary point object such as a pole or a person, the distance it covers equals the train's own length, since the point object has no length of its own. When the train crosses an extended object such as a platform or a bridge, the distance covered equals the train's length plus the object's length. In every case, distance = speed x time.

Application:

  1. Let the length of the train be L metres and its speed be v metres per second.

  2. Crossing the pole: the train covers only its own length L in 15 seconds, so L = 15v.

  3. Crossing the platform: the train covers its length plus 100 m in 25 seconds, so L + 100 = 25v.

  4. Substituting L = 15v into the second equation: 15v + 100 = 25v.

  5. Rearranging: 100 = 25v - 15v = 10v, so v = 10 m/s.

  6. Substituting back: L = 15 x 10 = 150 m.

Cross-check: At a speed of 10 m/s, the train covers its own length of 150 m in 150 / 10 = 15 s, matching the pole-crossing time. It covers the length plus the platform, 150 + 100 = 250 m, in 250 / 10 = 25 s, matching the platform-crossing time. Both conditions are satisfied, confirming the length of the train is 150 m.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2023 Q60
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A man sitting in a train which is travelling at 50 km ph observes that a goods train, travelling in opposite direction, takes 9 seconds to pass him. If the goods train is 280 m long, find its speed?
solution:
Concept

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds. A train of length L passing an observer, who counts as a point object, must cover exactly L at that relative speed, so time taken = L / relative speed. The unit bridge between the two systems is 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s, and 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h.

Application

  1. The observer is a single person, so the distance the goods train covers relative to him is its own full length, 280 m.

  2. Relative speed = distance / time = 280 m / 9 s = 280/9 m/s.

  3. Convert to km/h: 280/9 × 18/5 = 5040/45 = 112 km/h.

  4. The two trains run in opposite directions, so the relative speed is the sum: speed of goods train + 50 km/h = 112 km/h.

  5. Speed of the goods train = 112 - 50 = 62 km/h.

Cross-check

Adding back: 62 + 50 = 112 km/h, which is 112 × 5/18 = 280/9 m/s, about 31.11 m/s. The time to cover 280 m at that rate is 280 / (280/9) = 9 seconds, exactly the observation given. Note that the stated direction is load-bearing: had the trains run in the same direction the relative speed would be a difference, and 280/9 m/s would instead force a goods-train speed of 162 km/h.

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q79
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train runs at a speed of 74 km/hr and halts at 10 junctions for a certain time. It covers a distance of 1665 km in 24 hours. How long (in minutes) does the train stop at each junction if it halts for the same period of time at all the junctions?
solution:
Concept

For motion at a constant speed, running time equals distance divided by speed. When a journey also includes equal halts, total halt time equals total journey time minus running time, and the halt time per stop equals total halt time divided by the number of stops.

Application

  1. Running time = 1665 ÷ 74 = 22.5 hours.

  2. Total halt time = 24 − 22.5 = 1.5 hours.

  3. Convert to minutes: 1.5 × 60 = 90 minutes.

  4. Equal halt time at each junction = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 minutes.

Cross-check

Ten halts of 9 minutes total 90 minutes, which is 1.5 hours. Adding 1.5 hours of halts to 22.5 hours of running gives the stated 24-hour journey.

Result

The train stops for 9 minutes at each junction.

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q83
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Two trains having lengths of 180 m and 420 m are running at speeds of 70 km/h and 100 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
Concept

When one train overtakes another in the same direction, its effective speed relative to the other train is the difference between their speeds. To cross completely, the faster train must cover the sum of both train lengths relative to the slower train.

Use time = total relative distance ÷ relative speed, with distance and speed expressed in compatible units.

Application

  1. The total relative distance is 180 m + 420 m = 600 m.

  2. The relative speed is 100 km/h − 70 km/h = 30 km/h.

  3. Convert the relative speed: 30 × 1000 ÷ 60 = 500 m/min.

  4. Therefore, time = 600 ÷ 500 = 1.2 minutes.

Cross-check

In 1.2 minutes, a relative speed of 500 m/min covers 1.2 × 500 = 600 m, exactly the combined length of the two trains.

Therefore, the time taken is 1.2 minutes.

title: Train moving at speed of km/hr enters railway station and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A train moving at a speed of 63 km/hr enters a railway station and crosses the platform in 20 s. If the length of the train is 100 m, what is the length of the platform?
solution: First, convert the train's speed from km/hr to m/s by multiplying 63 by 5/18, which equals 17.5 m/s. Next, calculate the total distance covered in 20 seconds by multiplying speed (17.5 m/s) by time (20 s), resulting in 350 meters. Finally, subtract the train's length (100 m) from the total distance to find the platform length: 350 - 100 = 250 meters.

title: Ship, whose speed in km/hr in still water goes km
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A ship, whose speed in 15 km/hr in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. What is the speed of the stream in km/hr?
solution:
Let the speed of the stream be x km/hr.

Therefore the, speed of downstream = (15 + x) km/hr,

and speed of upstream = (15 – x) km/hr.

According to the question,

30/(15 + x) + 30/(15 – x) = 9/2

or, 900/(225 – x^2) = 9/2

or, 9x^2 = 225

or, x^2 = 25

or, x = 5 km/hr.

title: Boat takes hours for travelling downstream from point to point
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A boat takes 19 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and coming back to a point C midway between A and B. If the velocity of the stream is 4 km/h and the speed of the boat in still water is 14 km/h, what is the distance between A and B?
solution:
Solution:

Let the distance between A and B be x km.

Downstream speed = 14 + 4 = 18 km/h. Upstream speed = 14 - 4 = 10 km/h.

Time taken downstream (A to B) = x/18. Time taken upstream from B to midpoint C = (x/2)/10 = x/20.

Total time = x/18 + x/20 = 19 hours. Solve for x:

  1. Combine the fractions: x/18 + x/20 = (10x + 9x)/180 = 19x/180.

  2. Set 19x/180 = 19 ⇒ x = 19 * 180 / 19 = 180.

Therefore the distance between A and B is 180 km.

title: Mr. Vijay rows boat with the stream in km/hr and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Mr. Vijay rows a boat with the stream in 8 km/hr and against the stream in 4 km/hr. In still water, his rate of rowing in km/hr is:
solution:
Given:

Speed with the stream (downstream) = 8 km/hr

Speed against the stream (upstream) = 4 km/hr

Let speed in still water = b km/hr and speed of the stream = s km/hr.

Downstream speed = b + s and upstream speed = b − s.

So: b + s = 8 and b − s = 4.

Adding the two equations: 2b = 12, so b = 6.

Speed in still water = 6 km/hr.

title: Ratio of upstream speed to that of downstream speed is
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Ratio of upstream speed to that of downstream speed is 3 : 5. If speed of boat in still water is 24 km/hr then in how much time boat will cover 36 km upstream and 60 km downstream together?
solution:
To find the total time taken to cover the distances upstream and downstream, we follow a logical breakdown of speed and time relationships.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Define Variables:

Let the upstream speed be 3x and the downstream speed be 5x.

The boat speed in still water is the average of the upstream and downstream speeds: (3x + 5x) / 2 = 4x.

Calculate Speeds:

We are given that the boat speed in still water is 24 km/hr.

Setting 4x = 24 km/hr, we find x = 6.

Upstream speed = 3 * 6 = 18 km/hr.

Downstream speed = 5 * 6 = 30 km/hr.

Calculate Time Taken:

Time to cover 36 km upstream = Distance / Upstream Speed = 36 / 18 = 2 hours.

Time to cover 60 km downstream = Distance / Downstream Speed = 60 / 30 = 2 hours.

Total time = 2 hours + 2 hours = 4 hours.

Correct Option
Option A: 4 hours

title: Time taken to cover km in upstream is times the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Time taken to cover (A+4) km in upstream is 3 times the time taken to cover (A−2) km in downstream. If ratio of speed of boat in upstream to that of in downstream is 1 : 2 and time taken to cover (A+6) km in downstream is 2 hours. Then find speed of boat in still water?
solution:
Concept

Boats and streams: if upstream speed is u and downstream speed is d, then time = distance / speed, and the speed of the boat in still water is the average of the two, (u + d) / 2. Set up one equation per stated condition and solve.

Application

  1. Let upstream speed = u and downstream speed = d. Given u : d = 1 : 2, so d = 2u.

  2. Condition 1: time for (A+4) km upstream = 3 x time for (A-2) km downstream, i.e. (A+4)/u = 3(A-2)/d. Substitute d = 2u and cancel u: (A+4) = 3(A-2)/2.

  3. Solve: 2(A+4) = 3(A-2) -> 2A + 8 = 3A - 6 -> A = 14.

  4. Condition 2: time for (A+6) km downstream = 2 h, so (A+6)/d = 2 -> (14+6)/d = 2 -> d = 10 km/hr. Then u = d/2 = 5 km/hr.

  5. Still-water speed = (u + d)/2 = (5 + 10)/2 = 7.5 km/hr.

Cross-check

Times: upstream (A+4)=18 km at u=5 gives 3.6 h; downstream (A-2)=12 km at d=10 gives 1.2 h; 3 x 1.2 = 3.6 h, matching condition 1. Downstream (A+6)=20 km at d=10 gives 2 h, matching condition 2.

Result

The still-water speed works out to 7.5 km/hr, which is not listed among 4.5, 5.5 or 4 km/hr, so the correct choice is "None of these".

title: Boat running upstream takes hours minutes to cover certain distance,
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A boat running upstream takes 8 hours 48 minutes to cover a certain distance, while it takes 4 hours to cover the same distance running towards downstream. Then the ratio between the speed of boat and the speed of the water current is
solution:
For boat-and-stream problems, downstream speed equals the boat's speed plus the current's speed, and upstream speed equals the boat's speed minus the current's speed. For a fixed distance covered in different times, speed = distance ÷ time, so the two given times fix the two speeds.

  1. Convert the upstream time to hours: 8 hours 48 minutes = 8 + 48/60 hours = 8 + 4/5 hours = 44/5 hours.

  2. Let the common distance be D. Downstream speed = D / 4.

  3. Upstream speed = D / (44/5) = 5D / 44.

  4. Boat speed = half the sum of the two speeds: (D/4 + 5D/44) / 2. Writing D/4 as 11D/44, the sum is 16D/44, so boat speed = 8D/44 = 2D/11.

  5. Current speed = half the difference of the two speeds: (11D/44 − 5D/44) / 2 = (6D/44) / 2 = 3D/44.

  6. Boat speed : current speed = (2D/11) : (3D/44) = (8D/44) : (3D/44) = 8 : 3.

Check: with boat speed = 8k and current speed = 3k, downstream speed = 11k and upstream speed = 5k, so the time ratio (upstream : downstream) = 1/5k : 1/11k = 11 : 5 = 8.8 hours : 4 hours — exactly the 8 hours 48 minutes and 4 hours given in the question, confirming the ratio.

title: IOCL Technical Attendant Numerical Ability 2024 Q81
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक आदमी स्थिर जल में 9 km/h की चाल से नाव चला सकता है। उसे धारा की दिशा की तुलना में, धारा की विपरीत दिशा में उतनी ही दूरी तय करने में, दोगुना समय लगता है। धारा की चाल (km/h में) ज्ञात कीजिए।
solution:
अवधारणा

यदि स्थिर जल में नाव की चाल u और धारा की चाल v हो, तो अनुप्रवाह चाल u + v तथा प्रतिप्रवाह चाल u − v होती है।

समान दूरी d के लिए समय चाल के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है; अर्थात t = d/s।

प्रयोग

  1. यहाँ u = 9 km/h और धारा की चाल v km/h मानते हैं। इसलिए अनुप्रवाह चाल 9 + v तथा प्रतिप्रवाह चाल 9 − v है।

  2. दूरी d मानने पर प्रतिप्रवाह समय d/(9 − v) और अनुप्रवाह समय d/(9 + v) होगा। प्रश्नानुसार d/(9 − v) = 2d/(9 + v)।

  3. d को निरस्त करने पर 9 + v = 2(9 − v) मिलता है।

  4. अतः 9 + v = 18 − 2v, इसलिए 3v = 9 और v = 3 km/h।

पुनः-जाँच

v = 3 रखने पर अनुप्रवाह चाल 12 km/h और प्रतिप्रवाह चाल 6 km/h होती है। समान दूरी के लिए प्रतिप्रवाह समय का अनुप्रवाह समय से अनुपात 12/6 = 2 है, जो दी गई शर्त की पुष्टि करता है।

इसलिए धारा की चाल 3 km/h है।

title: Boat takes an hour to cover certain distance downstream in
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A boat takes an hour to cover a certain distance downstream in a river. It takes 1*1/2 hour to cover the same distance upstream. Assuming that the speed of boat is same in both downstream and upstream directions, what is the ratio of speed of boat to that of stream in the river?
solution:
Let the speed of the boat be B and the stream be S.
Since distance is constant, (B + S) × 1 = (B - S) × 1.5. Expanding gives B + S = 1.5B - 1.5S.
Rearranging terms yields 2.5S = 0.5B, which simplifies to B = 5S.
Thus, the ratio of boat speed to stream speed is 5:1.

title: IOCL 2024 Numerical Ability Q81
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक नाविक 40 km दूर एक स्थान तक नाव चलाकर 20 घंटे में वापस आता है। उसने पाया कि वह जितने समय में धारा की दिशा में 10 km तक नाव चला सकता है, उतने ही समय में धारा की विपरीत दिशा में 4 km तक नाव चला सकता है। धारा की चाल (km/h में) ज्ञात कीजिए।
solution: मान लीजिए स्थिर जल में नाव की चाल \(b\) km/h और धारा की चाल \(s\) km/h है। धारा के साथ चाल \(b+s\) और विपरीत दिशा में \(b-s\) होती है। दिया है \(\frac{10}{b+s}=\frac{4}{b-s}\), अतः \(10(b-s)=4(b+s)\), जिससे \(b=\frac{7}{3}s\)। 40 km दूर जाकर वापस आने का कुल समय 20 h है, इसलिए \(\frac{40}{b+s}+\frac{40}{b-s}=20\)। \(b=\frac{7}{3}s\) रखने पर \(\frac{40}{\frac{10}{3}s}+\frac{40}{\frac{4}{3}s}=20\), अर्थात् \(\frac{12}{s}+\frac{30}{s}=20\), अतः \(s=\frac{42}{20}=2.1\) km/h।

title: IOCL 2024 Numerical Ability Q88
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक नाव को धारा के विपरीत दिशा में एक निश्चित दूरी तय करने में 8 hrs 48 min लगते हैं, जबकि धारा की दिशा में समान दूरी को तय करने में उसे 4 hrs लगते हैं। नाव की चाल और धारा की चाल के बीच क्या अनुपात है?
solution: मान लें नाव की स्थिर जल में चाल \(b\) और धारा की चाल \(s\) है। 8 घंटे 48 मिनट = \(8\frac{4}{5}=\frac{44}{5}\) घंटे। समान दूरी \(D\) के लिए, धारा के विपरीत चाल \(b-s=\frac{5D}{44}\) और धारा के साथ चाल \(b+s=\frac{D}{4}\)। अतः \((b+s):(b-s)=\frac{D/4}{5D/44}=11:5\)। इसलिए \(b+s=11k\), \(b-s=5k\), जिससे \(b=8k\) और \(s=3k\)। नाव की चाल और धारा की चाल का अनुपात \(8:3\) है।

title: If man walks km/h, he is late to his office
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If a man walks 3 km/h, he is late to his office by 20 minutes. If he increases his speed to 6 km/h, he reaches the office 30 minutes early. The distance of his office from the starting place is ______.
solution:
Concept

For a fixed distance, time = distance ÷ speed. When the same distance is covered at two different speeds, the difference between the two travel times equals the total gap between the two arrival outcomes. If one trip is late by L and the other is early by E (relative to the same scheduled time), the slower trip takes (L + E) more time than the faster trip.

Application

Let the distance be d km. The scheduled (on-time) duration is the same in both cases, so we compare the two actual travel times.

  1. At 3 km/h the man is 20 min late and at 6 km/h he is 30 min early, so the slower trip takes 20 + 30 = 50 minutes longer than the faster trip.

  2. Convert the gap to hours: 50 minutes = 50 ÷ 60 = 5/6 hour.

  3. Travel time at 3 km/h is d/3 h; at 6 km/h it is d/6 h. Set their difference equal to the gap: d/3 − d/6 = 5/6.

  4. Combine the left side: d/3 − d/6 = (2d − d)/6 = d/6. So d/6 = 5/6.

  5. Multiply both sides by 6: d = 5. The distance is 5 km.

Cross-check

At 3 km/h, 5 km takes 5/3 h = 1 h 40 min; at 6 km/h, 5 km takes 5/6 h = 50 min. The difference is 1 h 40 min − 50 min = 50 min, matching the 20-min-late-plus-30-min-early gap. Hence 5 km is consistent.

title: Candidate secured marks in class and failed by marks. Another
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A candidate secured 36% marks in a class and failed by 24 marks. Another candidate secured 43% marks in the same exam and got 18 extra marks than the passing marks. Find the sum of the maximum marks and the passing marks of that exam ?
solution:
Let the total (maximum) marks be y and the passing marks be x.

  1. First candidate: scored 36% of total and failed by 24, so 36/100 × y + 24 = x.

  2. Second candidate: scored 43% of total and got 18 marks more than passing, so 43/100 × y - 18 = x.

  3. Equate the two expressions for x: 36/100 y + 24 = 43/100 y - 18.

  4. Rearrange: 24 + 18 = (43/100 - 36/100) y = 7/100 y, so 42 = 7y/100.

  5. Solve for y: y = 42 × 100 / 7 = 600. Thus the total marks are 600.

  6. Find passing marks x: x = 36/100 × 600 + 24 = 216 + 24 = 240.

  7. Therefore the maximum marks = 600 and the passing marks = 240. Their sum = 600 + 240 = 840.

Final answer: maximum marks = 600, passing marks = 240 (sum = 840).

title: In library of books are in English, is in German

title: Which of the given option is CORRECT?
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Which of the given option is CORRECT?
solution:
To compare fractions with different denominators, convert each fraction to its decimal value (divide the numerator by the denominator) or cross-multiply any two fractions being compared — whichever side gives the larger cross-product is the larger fraction. Applying this consistently across a chain shows whether the fractions are truly in ascending (or descending) order.

  1. Convert each fraction in this option to a decimal: 17/27 ≈ 0.6296, 15/22 ≈ 0.6818, and 13/17 ≈ 0.7647.

  2. Compare the decimals in order: 0.6296 < 0.6818, and 0.6818 < 0.7647.

  3. Both comparisons hold, so 17/27 < 15/22 < 13/17 is a genuine ascending chain.

Cross-multiplication confirms the same result without rounding: for 17/27 vs 15/22, 17 × 22 = 374 and 27 × 15 = 405, and since 374 < 405, 17/27 < 15/22. For 15/22 vs 13/17, 15 × 17 = 255 and 22 × 13 = 286, and since 255 < 286, 15/22 < 13/17. Both cross-multiplication checks agree with the decimal comparison, confirming the ascending order is exact, not just a rounding artifact.

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q95
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a ring, the ratio of gold and silver is 6 : 4. What is the percentage of gold in the ring?
solution:
Concept: When a quantity is split into parts according to a ratio, the percentage share of any part equals (that part's value ÷ sum of all ratio parts) × 100.

Application:

  1. The ratio of gold to silver in the ring is 6 : 4.

  2. The sum of the ratio parts is 6 + 4 = 10.

  3. Gold's share of the ring is 6 parts out of the 10 total parts.

  4. Percentage of gold = (6 ÷ 10) × 100 = 60%.

Cross-check: Silver's percentage = (4 ÷ 10) × 100 = 40%. Since 60% + 40% = 100%, the two shares account for the whole ring, confirming the calculation. Equivalently, 6 : 4 simplifies to 3 : 2, and 3/(3+2) = 3/5 = 60%, the same result by an independent route.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2023 Q66
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If 20% of A = 30% of B = 1/6 of C, then A : B : C is:
solution:
Concept — when several different multiples of different quantities are all set equal to one another, give that common value a single name, say k. Each quantity is then k divided by its own multiplier, so the quantities come out inversely proportional to those multipliers: the larger the fraction taken of a quantity, the smaller that quantity must be to reach the same k. Percentages and fractions therefore have to be rewritten as plain multiplying factors before the rule can be used.

Application — convert every expression to a multiplier, equate them, then solve for each letter.

  1. Rewrite each expression as a plain multiplier of its own letter: 20% of A = A/5, 30% of B = 3B/10, and one-sixth of C = C/6.

  2. All three are equal, so set them to one common value k: A/5 = 3B/10 = C/6 = k.

  3. Solve each equation for its own letter: A = 5k, B = 10k/3, and C = 6k.

  4. Write the ratio and cancel the common k: A : B : C = 5 : 10/3 : 6.

  5. Multiply every term by 3 to clear the fraction: A : B : C = 15 : 10 : 18.

Cross-check — substitute a value back, and test the inverse-proportion reasoning independently.

  • Take k = 30. Then A = 150, B = 100 and C = 180. Checking: 20% of 150 = 30, 30% of 100 = 30, and 1/6 of 180 = 30, so all three expressions do agree, and 150 : 100 : 180 reduces to 15 : 10 : 18.

  • Inverse-proportion sanity check: the multipliers are 0.30 for B, 0.20 for A and about 0.167 for C; since a larger multiplier needs a smaller quantity to reach the same k, the sizes must run C > A > B, and 18 > 15 > 10 follows that order.

Result — A : B : C = 15 : 10 : 18.

title: Of of an integer then minimum possible positive integer value
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: 1% of 9.6% of x = an integer then minimum possible positive integer value of x will be
solution:
Step 1: Convert percentages to fractions. 1% = 1/100 and 9.6% = 9.6/100 = 12/125.

Step 2: Multiply the fractions. (1/100)·(12/125) = 12/12500 = 3/3125.

Step 3: Use the integer condition. For (3/3125)·x to be an integer, x must be divisible by 3125 (gcd(3,3125)=1).

title: What part of is
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: What part of 1/12 is 3/8?
solution:
Concept

The phrase "what part of A is B" asks how many times the reference quantity A fits into B. By definition this part (or fraction) equals B divided by A: part = B / A. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

Application

  1. Identify the reference A = 1/12 (the quantity we measure against) and the target B = 3/8.

  2. Set up the part as a division: part = B / A = (3/8) / (1/12).

  3. Replace division by 1/12 with multiplication by its reciprocal 12/1: part = (3/8) × 12.

  4. Multiply: (3 × 12) / 8 = 36 / 8.

  5. Reduce 36/8 by dividing numerator and denominator by 4: 36/8 = 9/2.

Cross-check

Verify by multiplying the answer back by the reference: (9/2) × (1/12) = 9/24 = 3/8, which is exactly the target B. So 3/8 is 9/2 of 1/12.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2023 Q58
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A man spends 35% of his income on food, 25% on his children's education, and 80% of the remaining income on house rent. What percentage of his income is left?
solution:
Concept

When several expenses are expressed as percentages of the same original income, subtract them from 100% to find the first remainder.

If a later expense is a percentage of that remainder, multiply the remainder by the fraction that is left after that expense.

Application

  1. Assume the total income is ₹100.

  2. Food and education together use ₹35 + ₹25 = ₹60, so ₹100 − ₹60 = ₹40 remains.

  3. House rent uses 80% of ₹40: (80/100) × ₹40 = ₹32.

  4. The amount left after rent is ₹40 − ₹32 = ₹8.

Cross-check

Total spending is ₹35 + ₹25 + ₹32 = ₹92. Therefore, ₹100 − ₹92 = ₹8, which is 8% of the assumed income.

Result

The man is left with 8% of his income.

title: In society level election, there were two candidates, the winning

bodyHtml: In a society level election, there were two candidates, the winning candidate was supported by 49% of all the voters in the voting list and 20% of all the voters in the voting list did not cast their votes, and 40 voters cast their ballot paper blank. If the winning candidate won the election by 760, then find the total number of voters in the voting list.
solution:
Let the total number of voters be N.

  • Votes for the winning candidate = 49% of N = 0.49N.

  • Voters who did not vote = 20% of N = 0.20N. Blank votes = 40.

  • Valid votes cast = N − 0.20N − 40 = 0.80N − 40.

  • Votes for the other candidate(s) = valid votes − votes for winner = (0.80N − 40) − 0.49N = 0.31N − 40.

  • The winning margin is given as 760, so:

Margin = votes for winner − votes for other = 0.49N − (0.31N − 40) = 0.18N + 40

Set 0.18N + 40 = 760 and solve:

  1. 0.18N + 40 = 760

  2. 0.18N = 720

  3. N = 720 ÷ 0.18 = 4000

Therefore, the total number of voters in the voting list is 4000.

title: Is less than and more than Find is what more

bodyHtml: C is 20% less than A and 25% more than B. Find A is what % more than B?
solution:
Solution:

  1. Let C = 100 (choose a convenient value).

  2. Since C is 20% less than A, A = C / 0.8 = 125.

  3. Since C is 25% more than B, B = C / 1.25 = 80.

Therefore A is 225/4% more than B.

title: Three times the cost of wash basin, water heater and

bodyHtml: Three times the cost of a wash basin, 80% water heater and 20% basin is the cost of all water heater. What percent of the total cost is the cost of water heater?
solution:
Interpretation: we read the sentence as the equation: three times the basin cost plus 80% of the water heater plus 20% of the basin equals the entire cost of the water heater.

  • Let the basin cost be B and the water heater cost be H.

  • Set up the equation according to the interpretation: 3B + 0.8H + 0.2B = H.

  • Combine like terms: 3.2B + 0.8H = H.

  • Rearrange to solve for H in terms of B: 3.2B = 0.2H, so H = 16B.

  • Fraction of the total cost that is the water heater = H/(H + B) = 16B/(16B + B) = 16/17 ≈ 0.94117647.

Conclusion: Under this clear algebraic reading, the water heater is about 94.12% of the total cost. This does not match the provided 80% option, so either the answer key is incorrect or the original sentence was intended to mean something else.

Alternative (possible intended) wording that would give 80%: if the intended equation had been 3B + 0.2H + 0.2B = H (i.e., 20% of the water heater rather than 80%), then 3.2B + 0.2H = H gives H = 4B and the water heater would be 4/(4+1) = 80% of the total.

Final note: The problem statement is ambiguous; ask for clarification or correct wording before selecting an answer.

title: In an election between two candidates, one got of the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In an election between two candidates, one got 55% of the total valid votes, 20% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes was 7500, the number of valid votes that the other candidate got, was ______.
solution:
Concept

Only valid votes decide an election. When a fraction of all votes is invalid, Valid votes = Total votes × (1 − invalid fraction). In a two-candidate contest the candidates' valid-vote shares add up to 100%, so the other candidate's share = 100% − the first candidate's share, and a candidate's vote count = (that candidate's share) × (valid votes).

Application

  1. Invalid votes are 20% of the total, so valid votes are 80% of the total: valid = 7500 × 80/100 = 6000.

  2. One candidate took 55% of the valid votes, so the other candidate took the rest: 100% − 55% = 45% of the valid votes.

  3. Votes for the other candidate = 45% of 6000 = 6000 × 45/100 = 2700.

Cross-check

The two candidates together hold all the valid votes: 55% of 6000 = 3300 and 45% of 6000 = 2700, and 3300 + 2700 = 6000, which is exactly the valid-vote count. This confirms 2700.

title: Girl spends of her income. If her income increases by
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A girl spends 82% of her income. If her income increases by 15% and the savings decrease by 15%, then what is the percent increase in the expenditure (correct to one decimal place)?
solution:
Concept

When income is split between expenditure and savings, use the identity Income = Expenditure + Savings. A percentage change in one component should first be converted to an amount on a common base before comparing the final expenditure with the original expenditure.

Application

  1. Let the original income be 100. Since 82% is spent, the original expenditure is 82 and the original saving is 18.

  2. The new income is 100 x 1.15 = 115.

  3. The saving decreases by 15%, so the new saving is 18 x 0.85 = 15.3.

  4. The new expenditure is 115 - 15.3 = 99.7.

  5. The increase in expenditure is 99.7 - 82 = 17.7.

  6. The percentage increase is (17.7 / 82) x 100 = 21.585...%, which rounds to 21.6% to one decimal place.

Cross-check

On the original-income base, the saving changes from 18 to 15.3 while income changes to 115. Therefore expenditure changes from 82 to 99.7, giving the same percentage increase.

Result

The required percentage increase in expenditure is 21.6%.

title: In an election between two candidates, of the voters cast
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In an election between two candidates, 75% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 2% of the votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 9261 votes which is 75% of the total valid votes. Find the total number of voters enrolled in that election.
solution:
When a quantity passes through several percentage-based stages in sequence, the value at the end of the chain equals the original amount multiplied by the product of every stage's fraction. To recover the original amount from a value further down the chain, divide by that same product — this is the reverse-percentage / successive-percentage technique.

  1. Let the total number of voters enrolled be V.

  2. 75% of the voters cast their votes, so the votes cast = 0.75V.

  3. 2% of the votes cast were invalid, so 98% were valid: valid votes = 0.98 x 0.75V = 0.735V.

  4. The candidate received 75% of the valid votes: candidate's votes = 0.75 x 0.735V = 0.55125V.

  5. This equals the given figure: 0.55125V = 9261, so V = 9261 / 0.55125 = 16800.

Substituting V = 16800 back in: votes cast = 0.75 x 16800 = 12600; valid votes = 0.98 x 12600 = 12348; the candidate's votes = 0.75 x 12348 = 9261, matching the given figure and confirming the total enrolled voters.

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q72
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a university examination, it was found that 42% of the students passed in both English and Mathematics, 64% passed in Mathematics, and 52% passed in English. What is the percentage of students who failed in both the subjects?
solution:
For two overlapping groups expressed as percentages of the same population, the percentage belonging to at least one of the two groups equals the sum of the two individual percentages minus the percentage common to both groups, since the common portion would otherwise be counted twice. The percentage belonging to neither group then equals 100% minus this combined figure.

  1. Let M = percentage of students who passed in Mathematics = 64%, E = percentage of students who passed in English = 52%, and B = percentage of students who passed in both subjects = 42%.

  2. The percentage of students who passed in at least one of the two subjects = M + E − B = 64% + 52% − 42% = 74%.

  3. The percentage of students who failed in both subjects is the complement of this figure with respect to the whole student population: 100% − 74% = 26%.

As an independent check, partition the students into three mutually exclusive groups: those passing English only (52% − 42% = 10%), those passing Mathematics only (64% − 42% = 22%), and those passing both subjects (42%). These three groups add up to 10% + 22% + 42% = 74% of students passing at least one subject, matching the figure obtained above and confirming that 26% of the students failed in both subjects.

title: IOCL - Junior Engineering Assistant IV - Mechanical - 2024 — Q84
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक व्यक्ति अपनी मासिक आय के 20% की बचत करता है। यदि उसकी मासिक आय 30% बढ़ जाती है, तो वह पिछली बचत से 20% अधिक की बचत करता है। उसके व्यय में प्रतिशत वृद्धि क्या होगी?
solution:
अवधारणा

प्रतिशत परिवर्तन निकालने के लिए पहले मूल मात्रा और परिवर्तित मात्रा को समान आधार पर व्यक्त किया जाता है। आय = बचत + व्यय संबंध हर अवस्था में लागू रहता है।

यदि किसी मात्रा का नया मान पुराने मान का (1 + r/100) गुना हो, तो प्रतिशत वृद्धि = (वृद्धि ÷ पुराना मान) × 100 होती है।

अनुप्रयोग

  1. पुरानी मासिक आय को 100 इकाई मानें।

  2. पुरानी बचत = 20% × 100 = 20 इकाई, इसलिए पुराना व्यय = 100 − 20 = 80 इकाई।

  3. आय में 30% वृद्धि के बाद नई आय = 100 × 1.30 = 130 इकाई।

  4. बचत पिछली बचत से 20% अधिक है, इसलिए नई बचत = 20 × 1.20 = 24 इकाई।

  5. नया व्यय = नई आय − नई बचत = 130 − 24 = 106 इकाई। अतः व्यय में वृद्धि = 106 − 80 = 26 इकाई।

  6. व्यय में प्रतिशत वृद्धि = (26 ÷ 80) × 100 = 32.5%।

पुनः-जाँच

  1. पुराने व्यय को 32.5% बढ़ाने पर 80 × 1.325 = 106 इकाई मिलता है।

  2. नई आय में से यह व्यय घटाने पर 130 − 106 = 24 इकाई बचती है, जो पुरानी 20 इकाई बचत से 20% अधिक है।

इसलिए व्यय में प्रतिशत वृद्धि 32.5% है।

title: Three companies are working independently and receiving the savings If
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Three companies are working independently and receiving the savings 20%, 30%, 40%. If the companies work combinely, what will be their net savings ?
solution:
Answer: 30%

Explanation and steps:

  • Assume each company has the same base amount; take 100 for each company.

  • After a 20% saving the first company retains 80; after a 30% saving the second retains 70; after a 40% saving the third retains 60.

  • Total original amount = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300.

  • Total after savings = 80 + 70 + 60 = 210.

  • Total saving = 300 - 210 = 90, so combined saving percentage = 90 / 300 = 0.30 = 30%.

Therefore the net saving when the three companies are combined (assuming equal bases) is 30%.

Note: This conclusion relies on the assumption that each company starts from the same base amount. If instead the three percentage savings were applied sequentially to the same amount, the combined saving would be 1 - 0.8 * 0.7 * 0.6 = 0.664 = 66.4%, which is a different interpretation.

title: The population of town increases by in the first year
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The population of a town increases by 80% in the first year and further it increases by 20% in the second year. The overall increase percentage in population in two years is
solution:
To find the overall percentage increase when a population grows sequentially, you cannot simply add the percentages. Instead, you must calculate the effect of each increase on the new total.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Assume an initial value: Let the initial population be 100.

First-year increase (80%):

Increase = 80% of 100 = 80.

New population = 100 + 80 = 180.

Second-year increase (20%):

Increase = 20% of the new population (180).

Calculation: 0.20 × 180 = 36.

New population = 180 + 36 = 216.

Calculate overall percentage increase:

Total increase = Final population - Initial population = 216 - 100 = 116.

Percentage increase = (Total increase / Initial population) × 100

(116 / 100) × 100 = 116%.

title: If the side of square is increased by then percentage

title: An accountant divides the total by instead of multiplying by
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: An accountant divides the total by 7 instead of multiplying by 9. What is the percentage of error that creeps into the value ?
solution:
Solution: step-by-step

  • Let the original number be x. The correct operation (multiply by 9) gives the true value 9x.

  • The accountant instead divides by 7, giving the obtained value x/7.

  • Percentage error = (obtained − true) / true × 100% = (x/7 − 9x) / (9x) × 100%.

  • Compute the fraction: (1/7 − 9) / 9 = (1 − 63) / 63 = −62/63.

  • Thus percentage error = (−62/63) × 100% ≈ −98.4127%.

Answer: 98.41% (approximately).

Note: The negative sign indicates the accountant's value is smaller than the correct value; the magnitude of the error is 98.41%.

title: If exceeds by then is less than by what percent?
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If y exceeds x by 10% then x is less than y by what percent?
solution:
Concept

A reverse-percentage comparison is NOT symmetric: if a quantity is p% more than a base, the base is less than that quantity by a DIFFERENT percentage, because the two comparisons use different denominators. The drop is measured against the LARGER value, so it is always smaller than the original increase.

Rule: if A is less than B, then “A is less than B by” = ((B − A) / B) × 100 — the difference is divided by B (the value we compare against), not by A.

Application

  1. Let x be the base. y is 10% more than x, so y = x + 10% of x = 110x/100 = 11x/10.

  2. We want how much x is below y, so the comparison is against y: required % = ((y − x) / y) × 100.

  3. Difference: y − x = 11x/10 − x = x/10.

  4. Substitute: ((x/10) / (11x/10)) × 100 = (1/11) × 100 = 100/11 = 9 1/11%.

Cross-check

Take x = 100. Then y = 110. x is below y by 110 − 100 = 10, and 10/110 = 1/11 = 9 1/11% ≈ 9.09%. Note this is smaller than the original 10% rise, exactly as the asymmetry predicts.

solution:
B's income is 40% less than C's income, so B = 60% of C = 0.6C.

Therefore, C = B / 0.6 = 1.6667B.

Percentage by which C is more than B = (C - B)/B × 100.

= (1.6667B - B)/B × 100 = 66.7% (approximately).

The information about A is not needed for this particular question.

title: The salary of person was reduced by By what percentage
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The salary of a person was reduced by 40%. By what percentage should the reduced salary be raised so as to bring it at par with his original salary?
solution:
Concept: A percentage change always describes a movement measured against the base it acts on, and that base is whatever the quantity is worth at the moment the change is applied. So when a quantity first falls and then has to be brought back to its starting value, the fall is measured on the original base while the restoring rise is measured on the smaller value that survived the fall. The restoring rise is therefore (shortfall ÷ value after the fall) × 100, and a fall of x% needs a rise of 100x/(100 − x)% to return to the start.

Applying it here:

  1. Let the original salary be 100 units. Any base works, because the answer is a ratio and the units cancel.

  2. The salary falls by 40%, and that 40% is taken on the original base of 100, so the fall is 40 units.

  3. Salary after the fall = 100 − 40 = 60 units. This 60 is now the base for anything applied to the reduced salary.

  4. Shortfall still to be made up = 100 − 60 = 40 units.

  5. Express that shortfall on the new base: required rise = (40 ÷ 60) × 100 = (2/3) × 100 = 66 2/3%.

Cross-check: Raise 60 by 66 2/3%: the rise is (2/3) × 60 = 40, and 60 + 40 = 100, which is the original salary. The general formula agrees: 100x/(100 − x) with x = 40 gives 4000/60 = 66 2/3%.

Common slip: Adding the same 40% back on the reduced salary gives 60 + 24 = 84 units, short of 100, because 40% of 60 is smaller than 40% of 100. The percentage that comes off and the percentage that must go back on are never equal once the base has changed.

title: If exceeds by then is less than by what percent?
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If y exceeds x by 30% then x is less than y by what percent?
solution:
Concept

When a quantity y is larger than a quantity x by R%, the percent by which x falls short of y is NOT the same R%, because the base of comparison changes from x to y. The reverse percentage is R/(100 + R) × 100.

Application

  1. Let x be the smaller quantity. y exceeds x by 30%, so y = x + 30% of x = x(1 + 30/100) = 1.3x.

  2. The amount by which x falls short of y is y − x = 1.3x − x = 0.3x.

  3. x is less than y by (y − x)/y × 100 = 0.3x/1.3x × 100. The x cancels, leaving 0.3/1.3 × 100 = 30/130 × 100.

  4. Simplify 30/130 = 3/13, so the answer = 3/13 × 100 = 300/13 % = 23 1/13 %.

Cross-check

Using the direct identity R/(100 + R) × 100 with R = 30: 30/130 × 100 = 300/13 = 23 1/13 %, which matches the step-by-step result.

title: Man's salary is increased by In order to have his
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A man's salary is increased by 10%. In order to have his salary back to the original amount, it must be reduced by
solution:
Concept: When a quantity is increased by r%, restoring it to the original value is NOT the same as decreasing it by that same r% — the reduction is now taken as a percentage of the LARGER, already-increased amount, not the smaller original one. The required percentage decrease is r/(100+r) × 100.

  1. Let the original salary be 100 units, so every step below is a plain number.

  2. After a 10% increase, the new salary = 100 + 10 = 110 units.

  3. To bring 110 back down to 100, the amount to cut = 110 − 100 = 10 units.

  4. This cut of 10 units must be taken as a percentage of the CURRENT (increased) salary, 110, not the original 100: (10/110) × 100 = 1000/110 = 100/11 %.

  5. Converting 100/11 to a mixed number: 100 ÷ 11 = 9 remainder 1, so 100/11 = 9 1/11%.

Cross-check: Reduce 110 by 9 1/11%: that cut is (100/11 × 110)/100 = 10. Subtracting gives 110 − 10 = 100, exactly the original salary — confirming the reduction.

Answer: The salary must be reduced by 9 1/11%.

title: Woman saves of her income. If her income increases by
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A woman saves 18% of her income. If her income increases by 15% and her expenditure increases by 21.6%, then what is the percent decrease in her savings (correct to one decimal place)?
solution:
Concept

Savings = Income − Expenditure, so a change in savings depends on how income and expenditure move together. Any ‘percent decrease’ is found as (decrease ÷ the ORIGINAL value) × 100, using the original savings as the base — never the new income, new expenditure, or new savings. When a problem gives only percentages (no rupee figures), assume a convenient base income, such as 100, to convert the percentages into workable numbers.

Application

  1. Let the initial income = 100. Since she saves 18% of her income, original savings = 18% of 100 = 18, and original expenditure = 100 − 18 = 82.

  2. Income rises by 15%, so new income = 100 × 1.15 = 115.

  3. Expenditure rises by 21.6%, so new expenditure = 82 × 1.216 = 99.712.

  4. New savings = new income − new expenditure = 115 − 99.712 = 15.288.

  5. Decrease in savings = original savings − new savings = 18 − 15.288 = 2.712.

  6. Percent decrease in savings = (decrease ÷ original savings) × 100 = (2.712 ÷ 18) × 100 ≈ 15.1%.

Cross-check

Cross-check with a different base to confirm the percentage does not depend on the assumed income: with income = 1000, original savings = 180, new income = 1150, new expenditure = 820 × 1.216 = 997.12, new savings = 152.88, decrease = 27.12, and (27.12 ÷ 180) × 100 ≈ 15.1% — the same result, matching 15.1.

title: Due to economic surges the price of eggs suddenly reduced
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Due to economic surges the price of eggs suddenly reduced by 40%. This enabled a woman to buy 64 more eggs for $50. Then the reduced price per dozen is:
solution:
Concept

When the money spent is fixed, the number of items bought varies inversely with the price per item: items = money / price. A price reduction of 40% means the new price is the remaining 60% of the original (reduced BY 40%, not reduced TO 40%).

Application

  1. Let the original price per egg = x dollars. New price per egg = 60% of x = 0.6x.

  2. Eggs for $50 at original price = 50/x. Eggs for $50 at reduced price = 50/(0.6x) = 250/(3x).

  3. Extra eggs bought = 64, so 250/(3x) - 50/x = 64.

  4. Combine over 3x: (250 - 150)/(3x) = 64, so 100/(3x) = 64, giving x = 100/192 = 25/48.

  5. Reduced price per egg = 0.6x = 0.6 * 25/48 = 15/48 = 5/16 dollars.

  6. Reduced price per dozen = 12 * 5/16 = 60/16 = 15/4 = $3.75.

Cross-check

At the reduced rate 5/16 per egg, $50 buys 50 / (5/16) = 160 eggs; at the original rate 25/48 per egg, $50 buys 50 / (25/48) = 96 eggs. The increase 160 - 96 = 64 matches the given condition, confirming $3.75 per dozen.

title: If the price of an article increases by and the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If the price of an article increases by 49% and the sale of that article decreases by 21%, then what is the approximate effect on collection?
solution:
To find the total effect on the collection when both the price and sales change, we use the concept of successive percentage changes.

Step-by-Step Calculation
Understand the change factors:

Price increases by 49%: The new price factor is 1 + 0.49 = 1.49.

Sales decrease by 21%: The new sales factor is 1 - 0.21 = 0.79.

Calculate the combined effect:

Total Collection = (Price Factor) × (Sales Factor)

Total Collection = 1.49 × 0.79 = 1.1771

Convert to percentage:

An increase factor of 1.1771 represents an increase of 0.1771 (or approximately 17.71%).

Rounding to the nearest whole percentage, we get an 18% increase.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q67
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The price of sugar is increased by 25%. The percentage of reduction in consumption of sugar to keep the expenditure on sugar unchanged is
solution:
When the price of a commodity increases by r%, the percentage reduction in consumption needed to keep total expenditure (price times consumption) unchanged is given by the reverse-percentage relation: reduction % = [r / (100 + r)] × 100. This holds because expenditure is a product of two factors; when one factor rises by a given percentage, the other must fall by a smaller, compensating percentage — not by the same percentage — to keep the product constant.

  1. Let the original price be P and the original consumption be C, so the original expenditure is P × C.

  2. The price rises by 25%, so the new price is P + 25% of P = 1.25P.

  3. For expenditure to remain unchanged, the new consumption C' must satisfy 1.25P × C' = P × C.

  4. Solving for C' gives C' = C / 1.25 = 0.8C.

  5. The reduction in consumption is C - 0.8C = 0.2C, which is 20% of the original consumption.

  6. Equivalently, using the reverse-percentage formula directly: reduction % = [25 / (100 + 25)] × 100 = (25 / 125) × 100 = 20%.

Cross-check by substitution: new expenditure = 1.25P × 0.8C = 1.00PC, which equals the original expenditure PC. Since the two match, the 20% reduction is confirmed.

title: IOCL 2024 Numerical Ability Q77
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A person saves 20% of his monthly income. If his monthly income increases by 30%, then he saves 10% more than the previous savings. The percentage increase in his expenditure is ____
solution: Let the original monthly income be \(I\). Original savings are \(0.20I\), so original expenditure is \(0.80I\). After a \(30\%\) increase, income is \(1.30I\). Savings become \(1.10(0.20I)=0.22I\). New expenditure is \(1.30I-0.22I=1.08I\). The percentage increase in expenditure is \(\frac{1.08I-0.80I}{0.80I}\times 100=35\%\).

title: Akshay spends of his income. If he saves then find
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Akshay spends 70% of his income. If he saves ₹36,000, then find his income (in ₹).
solution:
When someone spends a fixed percentage of their income, the percentage left over equals the percentage saved, and Savings = (Saved percentage) x Income. So once the saved percentage and the actual savings amount are known, Income = Savings divided by (Saved percentage as a decimal).

  1. Percentage of income spent = 70%, so percentage saved = 100% minus 70% = 30%.

  2. Let the income be Rs. x. The amount saved is 30% of x, i.e., 0.30x.

  3. The savings are given as Rs. 36,000, so 0.30x = 36,000.

  4. Solving for x: x = 36,000 divided by 0.30 = Rs. 1,20,000.

Check: 70% of Rs. 1,20,000 is Rs. 84,000 spent; subtracting this from the income leaves Rs. 1,20,000 minus Rs. 84,000 = Rs. 36,000, matching the savings given in the question.

title: The price of sugar has increased by Find the percentage
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The price of sugar has increased by 25%. Find the percentage reduction in consumption so as to not increase the expenditure?
solution:
Key idea: keep expenditure constant when price changes.

  • Let the original price be P and original consumption be Q. Original expenditure = P × Q.

  • After a 25% price increase, new price = 1.25 × P. Let new consumption be Q'. To keep expenditure the same: 1.25P × Q' = P × Q.

  • Solve for Q': Q' = Q / 1.25 = 0.8 Q. Thus consumption must be 80% of the original.

  • Reduction = (Q − Q')/Q = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2 = 20%.

Answer: 20% reduction in consumption.
