title: Person marks his goods above the cost price. He sold
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A person marks his goods 40% above the cost price. He sold 30% of the goods at the marked price, 60% of the goods at a discount of 20%, and the remaining 10% of the goods at a discount of 40%. What is 60% of his overall gain percent?
solution:
Concept: When goods are sold in separate quantity-based batches at different discounts off the same marked price, the overall gain percent equals (total revenue − total cost) ÷ total cost × 100, where each batch's selling price = marked price × (1 − discount%).

  1. Assume total goods = 100 units at a cost price of ₹100 each, so total cost price = ₹10,000. Marked price = 140% of cost price = ₹140 per unit.

  2. Batch 1 — 30 units sold at the marked price: revenue = 30 × ₹140 = ₹4,200.

  3. Batch 2 — 60 units sold at 20% discount on the marked price: selling price = ₹140 × 0.8 = ₹112; revenue = 60 × ₹112 = ₹6,720.

  4. Batch 3 — the remaining 10 units sold at 40% discount on the marked price: selling price = ₹140 × 0.6 = ₹84; revenue = 10 × ₹84 = ₹840.

  5. Total revenue = ₹4,200 + ₹6,720 + ₹840 = ₹11,760. Overall gain = ₹11,760 − ₹10,000 = ₹1,760, so overall gain percent = 17.6%.

  6. The question asks for 60% of the overall gain percent: 0.6 × 17.6% = 10.56%.

Cross-check: each batch's own gain on ₹100 cost is +40% (30 units), +12% (60 units, since ₹112 vs ₹100), and −16% (10 units, since ₹84 vs ₹100). Weighting by quantity share: 0.30×40 + 0.60×12 + 0.10×(−16) = 12 + 7.2 − 1.6 = 17.6%, confirming the overall gain percent and the final value of 10.56%.

title: Person sold two flats for each. On one flat, he
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A person sold two flats for ₹45,00,000 each. On one flat, he gained 15%, while on the other, he lost 15%. Find his gain or loss in the transaction.
solution:
Step-by-Step Solution

  1. Understand the Concept: When two items are sold at the same selling price, and one is sold at a gain of x% while the other is sold at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss in the overall transaction.

  2. Use the Shortcut Formula: For cases with an equal percentage gain and loss (x%), the net loss percentage is calculated as: Net Loss % = (common percentage / 10)^2 OR (x^2 / 100)

  3. Apply the Values:

    • Here, x = 15.

    • Net Loss % = (15^2) / 100

    • Net Loss % = 225 / 100

    • Net Loss % = 2.25%.

title: Medical store owner purchased medicines worth from company. He sold
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A medical store owner purchased medicines worth ₹6,200 from a company. He sold one-third of the medicines at 33% loss. At what gain should he sell the rest of the medicines, so that he has neither gain nor loss?
solution:
Step-by-Step Solution

To achieve a "neither gain nor loss" (break-even) position, the total profit from the remaining goods must exactly equal the total loss incurred from the first part.

  1. Analyze the first part:

    • Portion of goods = 1/3

    • Loss percentage = 33%

    • Loss amount = (1/3) * 33% = 11% of the total cost price (CP).

  2. Analyze the remaining part:

    • Portion of goods = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3

    • We need this part to generate a profit percentage (P%) that covers the 11% loss.

  3. Set up the equation:

    • Profit from remaining = Loss from first part

    • (2/3) * P% = 11%

  4. Solve for P%:

    • P% = 11% * (3 / 2)

    • P% = 33 / 2

    • P% = 16.5%

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q99
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A man sells two T.V.s at the same rate. In case of first T.V. he makes 10% profit and in case of second one he loses 10%. Then his loss or gain percent is
solution:
Concept: When an article is sold at the same selling price once at x% profit and once at x% loss, the two transactions never cancel out — the overall result is always a loss equal to (x/10)2 percent of the combined cost price, regardless of the actual selling price used.

Application: Let the common selling price of each T.V. be SP.

  1. For the first T.V., a 10% profit means SP = CP1 × 1.10, so CP1 = SP / 1.10 = 10·SP/11.

  2. For the second T.V., a 10% loss means SP = CP2 × 0.90, so CP2 = SP / 0.90 = 10·SP/9.

  3. Total cost price = CP1 + CP2 = 10·SP/11 + 10·SP/9 = SP × (90 + 110)/99 = 200·SP/99.

  4. Total selling price = SP + SP = 2·SP = 198·SP/99.

  5. Since total CP (200·SP/99) is greater than total SP (198·SP/99), the deal produces a net loss = 200·SP/99 − 198·SP/99 = 2·SP/99.

  6. Loss% = (Loss / Total CP) × 100 = (2·SP/99) ÷ (200·SP/99) × 100 = 1%.

Cross-check: Using the shortcut identity for equal-selling-price profit/loss pairs, loss% = (x/10)2 with x = 10 gives (10/10)2 = 12 = 1%, confirming the step-by-step result independently.

Result: The overall transaction is a net loss of 1%.

title: Suppose fraud shopkeeper sells rice to the customer at the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Suppose a fraud shopkeeper sells rice to the customer at the cost price, but he uses a false weight of 900 gm for a kg then his percentage gain is ______
solution:
Key idea: the shopkeeper gives 900 g of rice but charges for 1000 g (1 kg).

  • Take an easy cost price: assume cost price of 1 kg = Rs 100.

  • He gives 900 g, so cost for 900 g = Rs 90. But he charges for 1 kg, so selling price received = Rs 100.

  • Profit = Selling price − Cost = 100 − 90 = Rs 10.

  • Profit percent = (Profit / Cost for 900 g) × 100 = (10 / 90) × 100 = 11.11% (repeating).

Answer: 11.11%

title: Marked price of an article is Rs. more than its
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Marked price of an article is Rs. 360 more than its cost price. If profit earned is equal to the discount given then find the profit earned ?
solution:
Correct Option
Option D: Rs. 180

Step-by-Step Solution
Define the variables:

Let Cost Price = CP.

Marked Price (MP) = CP + 360.

The problem states: Profit = Discount.

Relate Selling Price (SP) to variables:

SP = MP - Discount.

SP = CP + Profit.

Equate the two SP expressions:

Since both expressions equal SP, we have: MP - Discount = CP + Profit.

Substitute and solve:

Because Profit = Discount, we can substitute Discount with Profit: MP - Profit = CP + Profit.

Rearrange: MP - CP = Profit + Profit = 2 * Profit.

From our initial definition, MP = CP + 360, so (MP - CP) = 360.

Therefore, 360 = 2 * Profit.

Profit = 360 / 2 = 180.

title: Dealer marked the price of an item above the cost
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A dealer marked the price of an item 40% above the cost price. He then gave successive discounts of 20% and 25% to a particular customer, resulting in a loss of ₹720. At what price did he sell the item to the customer?
solution:
Concept

A markup and a discount are percentages of different bases: the markup is taken on the cost price, while each discount is taken on the price standing just before it. So the chain is multiplicative — SP = CP × (1 + markup) × (1 − d1) × (1 − d2) — and the loss is simply CP − SP. Since every percentage factor is known, one unknown cost price can be recovered from the given loss amount.

Applying it here

  1. Let the cost price be ₹x. A markup of 40% above cost gives the marked price MP = 1.40x.

  2. The first discount of 20% leaves 80% of the marked price: 1.40x × 0.80 = 1.12x.

  3. The second discount of 25% is taken on that reduced price and leaves 75% of it: 1.12x × 0.75 = 0.84x. So SP = 0.84x.

  4. Loss = CP − SP = x − 0.84x = 0.16x.

  5. The loss is given as ₹720, so 0.16x = 720, which gives x = 720 ÷ 0.16 = ₹4,500 as the cost price.

  6. Therefore the selling price is SP = 0.84 × 4,500 = ₹3,780.

Cross-check

Rebuild the whole chain from a cost price of ₹4,500 and confirm that the loss comes back to ₹720:

Stage

Amount

Cost price (CP)

₹4,500

Marked price = CP + 40%

₹6,300

After the 20% discount

₹5,040

After the further 25% discount (SP)

₹3,780

Loss = CP − SP

₹720

Note the trap: discounts of 20% and 25% are not a single 45% discount. Their combined effect is 1 − (0.80 × 0.75) = 0.40, i.e. 40% off. Even so, a 40% markup followed by 40% off ends in a loss, because the 40% is taken off the larger marked price while the 40% was added to the smaller cost price.

title: Dealer offers cash discount of and still makes profit of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A dealer offers a cash discount of 20% and still makes a profit of 20% when he further allows 16 articles to a dozen to a particularly sticky bargainer. By what percent above the cost price were his articles listed?
solution:
Let the cost price of one article be Rs. 1, and let the marked (listed) price of one article be Rs. M.

The deal has two layers. First, the dealer gives a 20% cash discount on the marked price. Second, "16 articles to a dozen" means the bargainer pays for a dozen (12 articles) but actually receives 16 articles.

Money the dealer receives = price charged for 12 articles after the 20% discount = 12 x M x (1 - 0.20) = 12 x 0.8 x M = 9.6M.

Goods the dealer hands over = 16 articles, costing 16 x 1 = Rs. 16.

He still makes a 20% profit, so his receipts equal 120% of his cost: 9.6M = 1.20 x 16 = 19.2.

Therefore M = 19.2 / 9.6 = 2. The marked price is Rs. 2 against a cost price of Rs. 1, i.e. twice the cost price.

So the articles were listed 100% above the cost price.

title: The successive discounts of and are equal to single discount
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The successive discounts of 20% and 15% are equal to a single discount of
solution:
For two successive percentage discounts applied one after another, the second discount is taken off the price that has already been reduced by the first discount, not off the original price. If the first rate is r1% and the second is r2%, the single discount that has the same overall effect is r1 + r2 − (r1 × r2)/100 — equivalently, the fraction of the original price left after both discounts equals (1 − r1/100) × (1 − r2/100).

  1. Take the original price as 100 (any convenient base works, since a percentage discount is scale-independent).

  2. Apply the first 20% discount: the price becomes 100 × (1 − 20/100) = 100 × 0.80 = 80.

  3. Apply the second 15% discount on this already-reduced price of 80 (not on the original 100): the price becomes 80 × (1 − 15/100) = 80 × 0.85 = 68.

  4. The total amount removed from the original price is 100 − 68 = 32 out of 100, so the single discount that has the same effect as the two successive discounts is 32%.

Cross-check with the direct successive-discount formula: combined discount = r1 + r2 − (r1 × r2)/100 = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15)/100 = 35 − 3 = 32%, which matches the step-by-step computation above.

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q100
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A book seller gives discount successively at the rate 25% and 16% on a book. By selling the book, he gets Rs. 63. What is the actual price of the book?
solution:
CONCEPT: When two discounts are applied successively (one after the other), the final price is not the marked price reduced by the simple sum of the two percentages. Each discount acts on the price left after the previous discount, so the overall retained fraction of the marked price is the PRODUCT of the two individual retained fractions: retained fraction = (1 − first discount/100) × (1 − second discount/100).

Applying this to the question:

  1. Let the actual (marked) price of the book be P.

  2. After the first successive discount of 25%, the retained price is P × (1 − 25/100) = 0.75P.

  3. The second successive discount of 16% is applied to this already-reduced price (not to the original price P): 0.75P × (1 − 16/100) = 0.75P × 0.84 = 0.63P.

  4. This final amount equals the selling price stated in the question: 0.63P = Rs. 63.

  5. Solving for P: P = 63 ÷ 0.63 = Rs. 100.

CROSS-CHECK: Apply the two discounts forward on Rs. 100 to confirm. A 25% discount on Rs. 100 leaves Rs. 75. A further 16% discount on Rs. 75 removes Rs. 12, leaving Rs. 63 — which matches the selling price given in the question, confirming the result.

So the actual (marked) price of the book is Rs. 100.

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q77
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The list price of an article is ₹44000 and a discount of 10% is offered on the list price. What additional discount per cent on the already discounted price must be offered to a customer to bring the net selling price to ₹792?
solution:
Concept

Sequential discounts are applied one after another to the current price, not independently to the original price.

For a price P and a discount d%, the new price is P(1 − d/100). A second discount x% multiplies the already discounted price by (1 − x/100).

Application

  1. After the first 10% discount, the price is ₹44,000 × (1 − 10/100) = ₹44,000 × 0.90 = ₹39,600.

  2. Let x% be the additional discount. The required net price gives ₹39,600 × (1 − x/100) = ₹792.

  3. Divide by ₹39,600: 1 − x/100 = 792/39,600 = 0.02. Hence x/100 = 0.98, so x = 98.

Cross-check

An additional 98% discount leaves 2% of ₹39,600, and ₹39,600 × 0.02 = ₹792, which reproduces the required net selling price.

Therefore, the required additional discount is 98%.

title: IOCL Technical Attendant Numerical Ability 2024 Q76
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: एक वस्तु का क्रय मूल्य ₹1839 है। विक्रेता 11% की छूट देने के बाद 22% लाभ अर्जित करना चाहता है। वस्तु का अंकित मूल्य कितना है? [अपना उत्तर निकटतम पूर्णांक तक दें।]
solution:
अवधारणा

लाभ प्रतिशत क्रय मूल्य पर लगाया जाता है: विक्रय मूल्य = क्रय मूल्य × (1 + लाभ प्रतिशत/100)।

छूट अंकित मूल्य पर लगती है: विक्रय मूल्य = अंकित मूल्य × (1 − छूट प्रतिशत/100)। इन दोनों संबंधों से अंकित मूल्य निकाला जाता है।

प्रयोग

  1. 22% लाभ के लिए आवश्यक विक्रय मूल्य = ₹1839 × 1.22 = ₹2243.58।

  2. 11% छूट के बाद ग्राहक अंकित मूल्य का 89% देता है, इसलिए 0.89 × अंकित मूल्य = ₹2243.58।

  3. अंकित मूल्य = ₹2243.58 ÷ 0.89 = ₹2520.876…।

  4. निकटतम पूर्णांक में अंकित मूल्य ₹2521 है।

पुनः जाँच

₹2521 पर 11% छूट देने से विक्रय मूल्य ₹2521 × 0.89 = ₹2243.69 मिलता है। यह निकटतम पूर्णांक में किए गए अंकित-मूल्य निर्धारण के कारण लक्ष्य ₹2243.58 से केवल ₹0.11 अलग है और लाभ लगभग 22.01% रहता है। अतः निकटतम पूर्णांक ₹2521 है।

title: Mobile phone retailer sells phone for and earns profit of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml:
A mobile phone retailer sells a phone for ₹P and earns a profit of 20%. For a special festive offer, he marks
the same phone at ₹1.5P. At the offer, he provides a discount of 10%. What will be the percentage profit that he
will make during the festive offer?
solution:
Original selling price P gives 20% profit, so CP = P/1.2.

Festival marked price = 1.5P, and a 10% discount gives SP = 1.35P.

Profit percentage = (1.35P - P/1.2)/(P/1.2) = 62%.

title: DSSSB TGT English 24 Aug 2025 5-7 PM Q51
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If an item marked at ₹8,100 is sold for ₹810, what is the discount percentage?
solution:
Concept

Discount percentage measures how much the marked price (MP) is reduced to reach the selling price (SP): Discount % = ((MP − SP) ÷ MP) × 100. Equivalently, SP = MP − Discount amount, so a larger discount percentage corresponds to a smaller selling price relative to the marked price.

Application

  1. Marked price (MP) = ₹8,100; Selling price (SP) = ₹810.

  2. Discount amount = MP − SP = ₹8,100 − ₹810 = ₹7,290.

  3. Discount % = (Discount amount ÷ MP) × 100 = (7,290 ÷ 8,100) × 100.

  4. 7,290 ÷ 8,100 = 0.9, so Discount % = 0.9 × 100 = 90%.

Cross-check

Apply a 90% discount back to the marked price: 90% of ₹8,100 = ₹7,290, and ₹8,100 − ₹7,290 = ₹810, which matches the given selling price — confirming the discount percentage.

bodyHtml: Find the value of the following expression:
solution:
Two identities are used here: (1) simplifying a surd of the form √(a2·b) = a√b, and similarly, the cube root of a perfect cube reduces directly to its cube-root value; and (2) rationalizing a denominator of the form 1/(√x − √y) by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√x + √y), using the identity (√x − √y)(√x + √y) = x − y.

  1. Simplify each root term individually: √20 = √(4×5) = 2√5; √12 = √(4×3) = 2√3; the cube root of 27 = 3; √25 = 5.

  2. Rationalize the fraction by multiplying by the conjugate: 4/(√5−√3) = [4(√5+√3)] / [(√5−√3)(√5+√3)] = [4(√5+√3)] / (5−3) = [4(√5+√3)] / 2 = 2√5 + 2√3.

  3. Substitute all the simplified terms back into the original expression: 2√5 + 2√3 + 3 − (2√5 + 2√3) − 5.

  4. Group like terms: the surd terms cancel out completely, since (2√5 − 2√5) = 0 and (2√3 − 2√3) = 0, leaving only the constant terms 3 − 5.

  5. Compute the remaining constants: 3 − 5 = −2.

As a numerical check: √20 is approximately 4.47, √12 is approximately 3.46, the cube root of 27 is exactly 3, √5 − √3 is approximately 0.504 so 4 divided by that is approximately 7.94, and √25 is 5. Combining with the given signs: 4.47 + 3.46 + 3 − 7.94 − 5 is approximately −2.01, which matches the exact algebraic result.

So the value of the expression is −2.

bodyHtml: If (9/7)3 × (49/81)(2x-6) = (7/9)9, then the value of x is:
solution:
Law of Exponents — Equal Bases Rule: if am = an for a base a with a ≠ 0, 1, -1, then the exponents must be equal, i.e. m = n. Two fractional bases that are reciprocals of each other, such as 9/7 and 7/9, can always be rewritten as powers of one another using (b/a) = (a/b)-1.

  1. Rewrite every term with base 9/7. Since 49/81 = 72/92 = (7/9)2 = (9/7)-2, write (49/81)(2x-6) as (9/7)-2(2x-6).

  2. Rewrite the right-hand side similarly: since 7/9 = (9/7)-1, (7/9)9 = (9/7)-9.

  3. Substitute the rewritten terms so the whole equation has base 9/7 on both sides: (9/7)3 × (9/7)^(-2(2x-6)) = (9/7)-9.

  4. Combine the exponents on the left-hand side using am·an = a(m+n): (9/7)3-2(2x-6) = (9/7)-9.

  5. Apply the equal-bases rule to equate the exponents: 3 - 2(2x - 6) = -9.

  6. Expand the bracket: 3 - 4x + 12 = -9, which simplifies to 15 - 4x = -9.

  7. Solve for x: -4x = -9 - 15 = -24, so x = 6.

  1. Substitute x = 6 back into the original equation: 2x - 6 = 6, so the middle term's exponent in base 9/7 is -2(6) = -12; adding the leading exponent 3 gives a total left-hand exponent of -9.

  2. This matches the right-hand exponent -9 exactly (since 7/9 is the reciprocal of 9/7), so the equation balances at this value, confirming x = 6.

title: Find the sum of digits of product TCS This test
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Find the sum of the digits of the product 16100 × 125135.
solution:
Concept: For numbers expressed as prime powers, (am)n = amn, and when two bases multiply to a round number such as 2 × 5 = 10, grouping (2a × 5a) = 10a turns a product into a power of ten times whatever factor is left over. Multiplying by 10a only appends a zeros to that leftover factor's digits, so the digit sum of the whole product equals the digit sum of the leftover factor alone.

  1. Write 16 as a power of 2: 16 = 24, so 16100 = (24)100 = 2400.

  2. Write 125 as a power of 5: 125 = 53, so 125135 = (53)135 = 5405.

  3. Multiply the two results, pairing as many 5's with 2's as possible: 2400 × 5405 = 2400 × 5400 × 55 = (2 × 5)400 × 55 = 10400 × 55.

  4. Evaluate the leftover factor: 55 = 54 × 5 = 625 × 5 = 3125.

  5. So the product equals 3125 followed by 400 zeros; every digit besides that leading '3125' block is 0, so the digit sum of the whole number is just the digit sum of 3125: 3 + 1 + 2 + 5 = 11.

Cross-check: 55 = 3125 can be verified directly (52 = 25, 53 = 125, 54 = 625, 55 = 3125), and re-adding its digits (3 + 1 + 2 + 5) confirms 11 independently of the exponent manipulation above.

bodyHtml: If (−3)m+1 ×(−3)5 =(−3)7 , then the value of m is:
solution:
Given: (−3)^(m+1) × (−3)^5 = (−3)^7

Step 1: Use the law of exponents: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n).

Apply to left side: (−3)^(m+1) × (−3)^5 = (−3)^(m+1+5) = (−3)^(m+6).

Step 2: Set equal to right side: (−3)^(m+6) = (−3)^7.

Step 3: Since the bases are the same and non-zero, equate the exponents: m+6 = 7.

Step 4: Solve for m: m = 7 - 6 = 1.

Thus, the value of m is 1.

solution:
Concept

When an expression of the form √(m + n√k) is written as a + b√k, square both sides and compare the rational part and the surd part separately.

This comparison gives equations such as a2 + k b2 = m and 2ab = n, which determine the coefficients before the requested expression is evaluated.

Application

  1. Here √48 = 4√3, so 31 + 3√48 = 31 + 12√3.

  2. Let √(31 + 12√3) = a + b√3. Squaring gives a2 + 3b2 + 2ab√3 = 31 + 12√3.

  3. Compare the rational and surd parts: a2 + 3b2 = 31 and 2ab = 12, so ab = 6.

  4. The positive pair a = 2, b = 3 satisfies a2 + 3b2 = 4 + 27 = 31 and ab = 6.

  5. Then b2 - a2 = 9 - 4 = 5, so √(b2 - a2) = √5 ≈ 2.236..., which rounds to 2.2.

Cross-check

(2 + 3√3)2 = 4 + 27 + 12√3 = 31 + 12√3, so the coefficients reproduce the original radical.

Result

The required one-decimal value is 2.2.

title: The value of 1 / √(15 - 6√6) is closest to
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The value of 1 / √(15 - 6√6) is closest to:
solution:
CONCEPT

For a surd in a square root, first see whether the radicand can be written as a perfect-square form such as (a - b)2 or (√m - √n)2. Then simplify the square root before taking the reciprocal.

When the expression asks for the closest option, compute the simplified decimal only after the exact radical form has been reduced.

APPLICATION

  1. Write the denominator as √(15 - 6√6). We look for numbers m and n such that m + n = 15 and 2√(mn) = 6√6.

  2. From 2√(mn) = 6√6, we get √(mn) = 3√6, so mn = 54. The pair m = 9 and n = 6 satisfies m + n = 15 and mn = 54.

  3. Therefore 15 - 6√6 = (√9 - √6)2 = (3 - √6)2.

  4. So √(15 - 6√6) = 3 - √6, because 3 is greater than √6 and the denominator is positive.

  5. Now rationalize: 1 / (3 - √6) = (3 + √6) / (9 - 6) = (3 + √6) / 3.

  6. Using √6 ≈ 2.449, the value is (3 + 2.449) / 3 ≈ 5.449 / 3 ≈ 1.816.

CROSS-CHECK / CONTRAST

  • 2.4 is too high because it is about 0.58 above the computed value.

  • 1.2 is too low because it is about 0.62 below the computed value.

  • 1 is farther below the computed value than the nearest decimal option.

  • The closest listed value to about 1.816 is 1.8.

Result: the value of the expression is closest to 1.8.

bodyHtml: The square root of ((10 + √25)(12 – √49)) is:
solution:
Concept: To simplify the square root of a product like √[(a)(b)], first evaluate any perfect-square roots inside each factor, then multiply the simplified factors, and finally extract the largest perfect-square factor from the result using the identity √(m²·n) = m√n.

Applying it here:

  1. Evaluate the inner square roots: √25 = 5 and √49 = 7.

  2. Substitute back into each factor: (10 + 5) = 15 and (12 − 7) = 5.

  3. Multiply the two simplified factors: 15 × 5 = 75.

  4. Factor 75 to isolate the largest perfect square: 75 = 25 × 3.

  5. Apply √(m²·n) = m√n: √75 = √(25 × 3) = 5√3.

Cross-check: Squaring 5√3 gives 25 × 3 = 75, which matches the product computed above, confirming the simplification.

title: If and is reciprocal of then what is the value
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If x = (√7 − √5) / (√5 + √7) and y is the reciprocal of x, then what is the value of √(x³ + y³)?
solution:
Concept. A fraction whose denominator is a sum of two square roots is rationalised by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate of that denominator, because (√a + √b)(√a − √b) = a − b carries no radical. Two numbers that are reciprocals of each other have product 1, so once their sum is known a sum of cubes follows from the identity x3 + y3 = (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y), with no need to cube either number separately.

Application. Working through the given expression:

  1. Rationalise x. Multiply numerator and denominator of (√7 − √5)/(√7 + √5) by the conjugate (√7 − √5). The denominator becomes 7 − 5 = 2, and the numerator becomes (√7 − √5)2 = 7 + 5 − 2√35 = 12 − 2√35. Hence x = (12 − 2√35)/2 = 6 − √35.

  2. Form y. Since y = 1/x = (√7 + √5)/(√7 − √5), multiplying numerator and denominator by (√7 + √5) gives y = (12 + 2√35)/2 = 6 + √35.

  3. Collect the two symmetric quantities. x + y = (6 − √35) + (6 + √35) = 12, and xy = (6 − √35)(6 + √35) = 36 − 35 = 1, which also confirms that y is the reciprocal of x.

  4. Substitute into the identity. x3 + y3 = (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y) = 123 − 3(1)(12) = 1728 − 36 = 1692.

  5. Take the square root and pull out the perfect square. 1692 = 36 × 47, so √1692 = √36 × √47 = 6√47.

Cross-check. Numerically √35 ≈ 5.9161, so x ≈ 0.0839 and y ≈ 11.9161. Then x3 + y3 ≈ 0.0006 + 1691.9994 ≈ 1692, and √1692 ≈ 41.13, which agrees with 6 × √47 ≈ 6 × 6.8557 = 41.13. Because 47 is prime it holds no square factor, so 6√47 is the fully simplified surd and the value of √(x3 + y3) is 6√47.

title: The average of numbers is The average of first three
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The average of 7 numbers is 29. The average of first three of them is 23 and the last three of them is 42. Then the fourth number is:
solution:
Concept

The average of a set of numbers equals their total sum divided by how many numbers there are, so Sum = Average × Count. When the same numbers are split into overlapping or adjacent groups, the sum of every individual number must still add up to the one grand total — a missing term is found by subtracting all the known partial sums from that total.

Application

  1. Total of all 7 numbers = 29 × 7 = 203.

  2. Sum of the first three numbers = 23 × 3 = 69.

  3. Sum of the last three numbers = 42 × 3 = 126.

  4. The first three, the fourth number, and the last three together make all seven, so: 69 + (fourth) + 126 = 203.

  5. 69 + 126 = 195, therefore fourth = 203 − 195 = 8.

Cross-check

Add the parts back: 69 + 8 + 126 = 203, which equals 29 × 7. The grand total is reproduced exactly, so the fourth number is 8.

title: The average of consecutive integers starting with is What is
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The average of 5 consecutive integers starting with m is n. What is the average of 6 consecutive integers starting with (m+2)?
solution:
To determine the average of 6 consecutive integers starting with (m + 2), let's break down the problem systematically.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Analyze the first sequence:

The 5 consecutive integers starting with m are: m, (m + 1), (m + 2), (m + 3), (m + 4).

The average of these integers is the middle term, which is (m + 2).

Given that this average is n, we establish the relationship: n = m + 2.

Analyze the second sequence:

The 6 consecutive integers starting with (m + 2) are: (m + 2), (m + 3), (m + 4), (m + 5), (m + 6), (m + 7).

The sum of these 6 integers is: 6m + (2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7) = 6m + 27.

The average is the sum divided by the count: (6m + 27) / 6 = m + 4.5.

Express the new average in terms of n:

We know from Step 1 that m = n - 2.

Substitute this into the average expression from Step 2: (n - 2) + 4.5 = n + 2.5.

Convert n + 2.5 into a fraction: (2n + 5) / 2.

Correct Option
Option A: (2n+5)/2

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q81
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The average of the first 91 odd natural numbers is:
solution:
Concept

The first n odd natural numbers form an arithmetic progression from 1 to 2n − 1 with common difference 2.

For any arithmetic progression, the average equals half the sum of its first and last terms. Applying this identity to the first n odd numbers makes their average equal to n.

Application

  1. Let n = 91. The last odd number is 2n − 1 = 2 × 91 − 1 = 181.

  2. Average = (first term + last term) ÷ 2 = (1 + 181) ÷ 2 = 182 ÷ 2 = 91.

Cross-check

  1. The sum of the first n odd natural numbers is n2. Thus, the sum is 912 = 8,281.

  2. Dividing the total by 91 terms gives 8,281 ÷ 91 = 91, confirming the endpoint-average calculation.

Result: the average is 91.

title: The average weight of class of students is kgs. If
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The average weight of a class of 29 students is 40 kgs. If the weight of the teacher be included, the average rises by 500 grams. What is the weight of the teacher?
solution:
Concept

When a new member joins a group, their value equals the difference between the new total and the old total. Equivalently: newcomer = new average + (number of original members) × (rise in average).

Application

  1. Find the original total. With 29 students averaging 40 kg, the total weight is 29 × 40 = 1160 kg.

  2. Find the new average. The average rises by 500 grams = 0.5 kg, so the new average for 30 people is 40 + 0.5 = 40.5 kg.

  3. Find the new total. For 30 people at 40.5 kg each, the total is 30 × 40.5 = 1215 kg.

  4. Find the teacher's weight. The teacher's weight is the increase in total: 1215 − 1160 = 55 kg.

Cross-check

bodyHtml: The average of 50 numbers is 38. If two numbers namely 45 and 55 are discarded, the average of rest 48 numbers is
solution:
Concept: The average of a set of numbers is the sum of all the numbers divided by how many numbers there are. When some numbers are removed from the set, the new average of the remaining numbers equals (original sum minus the sum of the removed numbers) divided by the new count.

Application:

title: DSSSB TGT Special Education Teacher 26 Jun 2025 Shift 3 Q56
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml:
The average of 7 numbers is 49. If each number is decreased by 4, what will the new

average be?
solution:
The average (mean) of a group of numbers is (sum of all the numbers) divided by (how many numbers there are). Because of this definition, a fixed rule holds: if the same amount is added to, or subtracted from, every single number in a group, the average changes by exactly that same amount, since the total sum changes by (count of numbers x that amount), and dividing by the count leaves the change unchanged.

  1. The average of 7 numbers is given as 49, so their total sum = 7 x 49 = 343.

  2. Each of the 7 numbers is decreased by 4, so the total sum decreases by 7 x 4 = 28.

  3. New sum = 343 - 28 = 315.

  4. New average = new sum / count = 315 / 7 = 45.

Cross-check using the rule directly: new average = old average - (amount subtracted from each number) = 49 - 4 = 45, which matches the sum-based calculation above.

So the new average is 45.

title: The average of numbers is The average of first three
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The average of 7 numbers is 30. The average of the first three of them is 23 and the last three of them is 42. Then the fourth number is:
solution:
Concept

The sum of a set of numbers equals its average multiplied by how many numbers there are (Sum = Average x Count). When a whole group is split into adjoining sub-groups, a single missing value can be recovered by subtracting the sub-group sums from the total sum.

Application

Seven numbers are split as: the first three, the single fourth number, and the last three. Compute each known sum, then isolate the fourth:

  1. Total of all 7 numbers = 30 x 7 = 210.

  2. Sum of the first three = 23 x 3 = 69.

  3. Sum of the last three = 42 x 3 = 126.

  4. Fourth number = Total - (first three) - (last three) = 210 - 69 - 126 = 15.

Cross-check

Add the parts back: 69 (first three) + 15 (fourth) + 126 (last three) = 210, and 210 / 7 = 30, which matches the given overall average. So the fourth number is 15.

title: Average weight of boys in class is kg while average
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Average weight of boys in a class is 55 kg while average weight of girls in the same class is 35 kg. If the average of all the students in the class is 40 kg, find the ratio of boys and girls in the class.
solution:
Concept

When two groups are combined, the overall (weighted) average lies between the two group averages. The rule of alligation states that the two groups split in the inverse ratio of their distances from the overall average:

(number in group 1) : (number in group 2) = (distance of group 2's average from the mean) : (distance of group 1's average from the mean).

Application

  1. Boys' average = 55 kg, girls' average = 35 kg, overall average = 40 kg. Let the number of boys be b and girls be g.

  2. Total weight equation: 55b + 35g = 40(b + g).

  3. Expand the right side: 55b + 35g = 40b + 40g.

  4. Collect like terms: 55b − 40b = 40g − 35g, so 15b = 5g.

  5. Divide both sides by 5: 3b = g, hence b : g = 1 : 3.

Cross-check (alligation)

Distance of boys' average from the mean = 55 − 40 = 15; distance of girls' average from the mean = 40 − 35 = 5. By alligation, boys : girls = 5 : 15 = 1 : 3, which matches.

So boys : girls = 1 : 3.

title: How many real solutions does the equation x7+14x5+16x3+30x−560=0 have?
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: How many real solutions does the equation x7 + 14x5 + 16x3 + 30x − 560 = 0 have?
solution:
Concept

A continuous function has at least one real zero when its values change sign. A function whose derivative is positive everywhere is strictly increasing, so it can have at most one real zero.

For an odd-degree polynomial with positive leading coefficient, the value tends to −∞ as x tends to −∞ and to +∞ as x tends to +∞.

Application

  1. Define f(x) = x7 + 14x5 + 16x3 + 30x − 560. This polynomial is continuous for every real x.

  2. Differentiate: f′(x) = 7x6 + 70x4 + 48x2 + 30.

  3. For every real x, the even powers x6, x4, and x2 are non-negative. Therefore f′(x) ≥ 30 > 0, so f is strictly increasing and can cross zero at most once.

  4. Because f(x) tends to −∞ as x tends to −∞ and to +∞ as x tends to +∞, continuity guarantees at least one real zero.

Cross-check

Direct values bracket a zero: f(1) = −499 < 0, while f(2) = 204 > 0. Thus a real zero lies between 1 and 2; strict increase prevents any second zero.

Therefore, the equation has exactly 1 real solution.

title: If then the value of is
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 527, then the value of x + 1/x is
solution:
Concept

For any nonzero x, the symmetric powers are linked by repeated squaring of the basic sum s = x + 1/x. Squaring a sum adds the cross term, so (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2. With b = 1/a the middle term is the constant 2, which lets each higher power be reached from the one below.

Application

  1. Let s = x + 1/x. Squaring: s2 = x2 + 2 + 1/x2, so x2 + 1/x2 = s2 - 2.

  2. Square again: (x2 + 1/x2)2 = x4 + 2 + 1/x4, so x4 + 1/x4 = (x2 + 1/x2)2 - 2.

  3. Substitute: 527 = (x2 + 1/x2)2 - 2, so (x2 + 1/x2)2 = 529 and x2 + 1/x2 = ±23.

  4. For real x, x2 + 1/x2 ≥ 2 (a square plus its reciprocal is always at least 2 by AM-GM), so the -23 branch is impossible and x2 + 1/x2 = 23.

  5. Back to step 1: s2 - 2 = 23, so s2 = 25 and s = x + 1/x = ±5.

Choosing the value

s2 = 25 admits both +5 and -5 (for real x, +5 corresponds to x > 0 and -5 to x < 0). Only positive values are offered here, so the answer is 5, matching the standard convention of taking the positive root for this problem type.

Cross-check

Forward from s = 5: x2 + 1/x2 = 52 - 2 = 23, and x4 + 1/x4 = 232 - 2 = 527, matching the given value (s = -5 gives the same fourth power, since only even powers appear).

title: Which among the following can be expressed as where and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Which among the following can be expressed as (10p + q) (10q + p), where p and q are integers?
solution:
For any integers p and q — not necessarily single digits — let a = 10p + q and b = 10q + p; b swaps the coefficients of p and q, the same pattern as reversing a two-digit number's digits when p, q happen to be 0-9. The product expands algebraically to (10p + q)(10q + p) = 10p2 + 101pq + 10q2. Since a + b = 11(p + q) and a − b = 9(p − q), a target number N is expressible in this form ONLY IF N has some factor pair (a, b) — checked across ALL its divisor pairs, not only ones that look like two-digit reversals — whose sum is a multiple of 11 AND whose difference is a multiple of 9; p and q are then recovered as p = (10a − b) / 99 and q = (10b − a) / 99.

  1. Check 1207: its factor pair 17 × 71 gives sum 17 + 71 = 88 = 11 × 8 (a multiple of 11) and difference 71 − 17 = 54 = 9 × 6 (a multiple of 9) — both required conditions hold.

  2. Recover p and q from a = 17, b = 71: p = (10a − b) / 99 = (170 − 71) / 99 = 1 and q = (10b − a) / 99 = (710 − 17) / 99 = 7, both integers.

  3. So p = 1, q = 7 gives 10p + q = 17 and 10q + p = 71, and 17 × 71 = 1207 exactly — the required form is satisfied.

  4. Checking every divisor pair of the other three values the same way: for 1344, three pairs have a sum divisible by 11 — (3, 448) with sum 451, (8, 168) with sum 176, and (14, 96) with sum 110 — but none of their differences (445, 160, and 82) is divisible by 9; for 1728 and 1296, no divisor pair at all has a sum divisible by 11. So none of 1344, 1728, or 1296 has any factor pair meeting both conditions, for any integers p and q — not only when p, q are restricted to single digits.

Cross-check by substituting p = 1 and q = 7 directly into the expansion: 10p2 + 101pq + 10q2 = 10(1) + 101(7) + 10(49) = 10 + 707 + 490 = 1207, matching independently.

So 1207 is the only one of the four values expressible as (10p + q)(10q + p) for integers p and q.

title: Question 73858
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
solution:
Difference of cubes: for any x and y, x3 − y3 factorises as (x − y)(x2 + xy + y2). When a fraction's denominator already matches the second factor x2 + xy + y2, the whole fraction collapses to x − y without evaluating any cube directly.

  1. 64 = 43, so 64 × (0.888)3 = (4 × 0.888)3 = (3.552)3. Take x = 5.169 and y = 4 × 0.888 = 3.552.

  2. The numerator, (5.169)3 − 64 × (0.888)3, is exactly x3 − y3.

  3. The denominator, (5.169)2 + (3.552)2 + 4(0.888)(5.169), equals x2 + y2 + xy: here y2 = (3.552)2 and xy = 5.169 × 3.552 = 4(0.888)(5.169), so the given denominator is precisely x2 + xy + y2, the second factor of the identity.

  4. The fraction therefore reduces to x − y = 5.169 − 3.552 = 1.617.

  5. Since the expression equals (2 − k), set 2 − k = 1.617 and solve: k = 2 − 1.617 = 0.383.

Direct evaluation confirms this without factoring: (5.169)3 ≈ 138.108 and 64 × (0.888)3 ≈ 44.815, giving a numerator ≈ 93.294; the denominator (5.169)2 + (3.552)2 + 4(0.888)(5.169) ≈ 57.696. Dividing gives ≈ 1.617, matching x − y independently and confirming k = 0.383.

solution:
अवधारणा

किन्हीं दो राशियों a और b के लिए (a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab होता है। इसलिए a2 + b2 = (a + b)2 − 2ab लिखा जा सकता है।

संयुग्मी राशियों p + q और p − q का योग 2p तथा गुणनफल p2 − q2 होता है। इन नियमों से वर्गों का योग सीधे निकाला जा सकता है।

अनुप्रयोग

  1. √4 = 2, इसलिए x = 3 + 2 = 5 और y = 3 − 2 = 1।

  2. अब x + y = 5 + 1 = 6 तथा xy = 5 × 1 = 5।

  3. पहचान लगाने पर x2 + y2 = (x + y)2 − 2xy = 62 − 2 × 5 = 36 − 10 = 26।

पुनः जाँच

प्रत्यक्ष गणना से 52 + 12 = 25 + 1 = 26 मिलता है, जो पहचान से प्राप्त मान की पुष्टि करता है।

परिणाम

अतः x2 + y2 का मान 26 है।

title: IOCL Technical Attendant Numerical Ability 2024 Q87
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If a2 + b2 + c2 = 139, ab + bc + ca = 5/2, and a + b + c < 0, then what is the value of (a + b + c)3?
solution:
Concept

For any three numbers, (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca). This identity converts the given symmetric sums into the square of their total.

Once the square of a real total is known, a sign condition selects its positive or negative square root. Cubing then preserves that selected sign.

Application

  1. Let s = a + b + c.

  2. Apply the identity: s2 = 139 + 2(5/2).

  3. Simplify the product: 2(5/2) = 5, so s2 = 139 + 5 = 144.

  4. Therefore s = ±12. The condition s < 0 selects s = −12.

  5. Cube the selected value: s3 = (−12)3 = −1728.

Cross-check

Squaring −12 gives 144, which equals 139 + 2(5/2), and −12 satisfies the stated negative-sign condition. Hence (a + b + c)3 = −1728.

title: If and find the value of ab. TCS This test
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If a - b = 3 and a2 + b2 = 29, find the value of ab.
solution:
Concept: For any two numbers a and b, the identity (a - b)2 = a2 + b2 - 2ab links the square of their difference, the sum of their squares, and their product. Rearranging it gives 2ab = (a2 + b2) - (a - b)2, so ab can be found directly once a - b and a2 + b2 are both known — no need to find a and b individually.

Applying it here:

  1. Square the given difference: a - b = 3, so (a - b)2 = 32 = 9.

  2. Use the given sum of squares: a2 + b2 = 29.

  3. Substitute both into the identity: 2ab = (a2 + b2) - (a - b)2 = 29 - 9 = 20.

  4. Divide by 2 to isolate ab: ab = 20 / 2 = 10.

Cross-check: Since (a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab = 29 + 20 = 49, a + b = ±7. Taking a + b = 7 with a - b = 3 gives a = 5, b = 2; taking a + b = -7 with a - b = 3 gives a = -2, b = -5. In both cases a × b = 10 — the same value obtained above.

title: If 2a+3b+6c=0, then at least one root of the equation
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If 2a + 3b + 6c = 0, then at least one root of the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 lies in the interval:
solution:
Correct answer: (0,1)

Why do we choose F(x)? The equation whose root we need is ax² + bx + c = 0. Rolle’s theorem gives a zero of a derivative, so we deliberately construct a function F(x) whose derivative is this quadratic.

Let

F(x) = ax³/3 + bx²/2 + cx + d.

Then

F'(x) = ax² + bx + c.

Now compare F(1) and F(0):

F(1) - F(0) = a/3 + b/2 + c = (2a + 3b + 6c)/6.

Given 2a + 3b + 6c = 0, we get F(1) - F(0) = 0, so F(1) = F(0).

By Rolle’s theorem, there exists some ξ in (0,1) such that F′(ξ) = 0. Therefore aξ² + bξ + c = 0, so at least one root lies in (0,1).

solution:
Concept: For any two numbers a and b, the difference of cubes factorises as a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2). So whenever a2 + ab + b2 is not zero, the quotient (a3 − b3) ÷ (a2 + ab + b2) reduces to the single difference a − b, and the cubes never have to be evaluated.

Application

  1. Match the expression to the identity: here a = 0.867 and b = 0.321, the numerator is a3 − b3, and the denominator is exactly a2 + ab + b2.

  2. Factorise the numerator using the identity: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

  3. Cancel the common factor a2 + ab + b2, which is positive here, so the cancellation is valid; the expression becomes simply a − b.

  4. Substitute the given values: a − b = 0.867 − 0.321 = 0.546.

Cross-check by direct computation

  • Numerator: 0.8673 − 0.3213 = 0.651714363 − 0.033076161 = 0.618638202.

  • Denominator: 0.8672 + 0.867 × 0.321 + 0.3212 = 0.751689 + 0.278307 + 0.103041 = 1.133037.

  • Quotient: 0.618638202 ÷ 1.133037 = 0.546, which matches the factorised result exactly.

Watch out: If the numerator carried a plus sign, the sum-of-cubes identity a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) would apply instead, and the middle term of the quadratic factor would be −ab, giving a + b. Mixing the two forms breaks the cancellation, so always check the sign pattern of the middle term before cancelling.

title: Question 12660
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
solution:
Given: log(x/y) + log(y/x) = log(x+y)

Combine the logarithms on the left:

log((x/y)·(y/x)) = log(x+y)

Simplify the product:

log(1) = log(x+y) ⇒ 0 = log(x+y) ⇒ x + y = 1

Domain conditions:

  • x and y must be nonzero (arguments of log).

  • x/y and y/x must be positive, so x and y have the same sign.

  • x + y must be positive for log(x+y) to be defined.

  • Combining these conditions implies x > 0 and y > 0.

Final answer: x + y = 1 with x > 0 and y > 0.

title: If two is added to the denominator of rational number
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If two is added to the denominator of a rational number it becomes 1/3 and if 4 is added to the numerator it becomes 1/2. Then the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the rational number is:
solution:
Concept

A statement "a fraction becomes 1/k when something is changed" is an equation between two fractions. Cross-multiply each such statement to turn it into a linear equation, then solve the resulting system (here by elimination) for the unknown numerator and denominator.

Application

Let the rational number be x/y, where x is the numerator and y the denominator.

  1. First condition: adding 2 to the denominator gives 1/3, so x/(y+2) = 1/3. Cross-multiplying: 3x = y + 2, i.e. 3x − y = 2.

  2. Second condition: adding 4 to the numerator gives 1/2, so (x+4)/y = 1/2. Cross-multiplying: 2(x+4) = y, i.e. 2x − y = −8.

  3. Eliminate y by subtracting the second equation from the first: (3x − y) − (2x − y) = 2 − (−8), which gives x = 10.

  4. Substitute x = 10 into 3x − y = 2: 30 − y = 2, so y = 28.

  5. The required sum is x + y = 10 + 28 = 38.

Cross-check

Verify both conditions with x = 10, y = 28: x/(y+2) = 10/30 = 1/3 ✓ and (x+4)/y = 14/28 = 1/2 ✓. Both hold, so the numerator-plus-denominator sum is 38.

solution:
To determine the difference between the initial populations of town A and town B, we can set up an algebraic equation based on the population changes over 30 years.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Define the variables:

Let P_A be the initial population of town A.

Let P_B be the initial population of town B.

Express the population after 30 years:

Town A decreases by 10,000 every year: P_A - (10,000 × 30)

Town B increases by 15,000 every year: P_B + (15,000 × 30)

Set the populations as equal after 30 years:

P_A - 300,000 = P_B + 450,000

Find the difference between initial populations (P_A - P_B):

Rearrange the equation to solve for (P_A - P_B):

P_A - P_B = 450,000 + 300,000

P_A - P_B = 750,000

title: If two is added to the denominator of rational number
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If two is added to the denominator of a rational number it becomes 1 and if 4 is added to the numerator it becomes 1/2. Then the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the rational number is:
solution:
Concept

A rational number is a fraction numerator/denominator. When a worded condition says a fraction "becomes" a value after changing its numerator or denominator, translate each statement into a linear equation and solve the resulting system by substitution.

Application

Let the rational number be N/D, where N is the numerator and D is the denominator.

  1. Adding 2 to the denominator makes the fraction equal to 1: N / (D + 2) = 1, so N = D + 2.

  2. Adding 4 to the numerator makes the fraction equal to 1/2: (N + 4) / D = 1/2, so 2(N + 4) = D, that is 2N + 8 = D.

  3. Substitute N = D + 2 into 2N + 8 = D: 2(D + 2) + 8 = D, giving 2D + 4 + 8 = D.

  4. Simplify: 2D + 12 = D, so D = -12, and then N = D + 2 = -10.

  5. Required sum = N + D = -10 + (-12) = -22.

Cross-check

With N = -10 and D = -12 the fraction is -10/-12 = 5/6. Verify: N/(D+2) = -10/-10 = 1 and (N+4)/D = -6/-12 = 1/2. Both conditions hold, so the sum -22 is correct.

title: If is added to the denominator of rational number, it
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If 2 is added to the denominator of a rational number, it becomes 1/2 and if 34 is added to the numerator it becomes 1/4 . Then the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the rational number is:
solution:
Concept

A rational number is written as a fraction numerator/denominator. When a condition says the fraction equals a target value after a change, translate it into an equation by cross-multiplication: a/b = p/q means a*q = b*p. Two independent conditions give two linear equations, which are solved simultaneously for the numerator and the denominator.

Application

Let the numerator be N and the denominator be D, so the number is N/D.

  1. Condition 1 - adding 2 to the denominator gives 1/2: N/(D + 2) = 1/2. Cross-multiply: 2N = D + 2, so D = 2N - 2.

  2. Condition 2 - adding 34 to the numerator gives 1/4: (N + 34)/D = 1/4. Cross-multiply: 4(N + 34) = D, so D = 4N + 136.

  3. Equate the two expressions for D: 2N - 2 = 4N + 136, which gives -2N = 138, so N = -69.

  4. Substitute back: D = 2(-69) - 2 = -140.

  5. Required sum = N + D = -69 + (-140) = -209.

Cross-check

The number is -69/-140 = 69/140. Add 2 to the denominator: -69/(-138) = 69/138 = 1/2. Add 34 to the numerator: (-69 + 34)/-140 = -35/-140 = 35/140 = 1/4. Both conditions hold, so the sum is -209.

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q78
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A father is 30 years older than his son. He will be three times as old as his son after 5 years. Father’s present age is
solution:
Concept: In age-relationship problems, assign a variable to one person's present age, express the other person's present age in terms of it using the given age gap, then translate 'after n years' by adding n to each age. The stated ratio at that future time gives one linear equation in the variable, which is solved directly.

Application:

  1. Let the son's present age be s years. Since the father is 30 years older, the father's present age is s + 30 years.

  2. After 5 years, the father's age is (s + 30) + 5 = s + 35, and the son's age is s + 5.

  3. The given condition states the father's age after 5 years is three times the son's age at that time: s + 35 = 3(s + 5).

  4. Expanding: s + 35 = 3s + 15.

  5. Rearranging: 35 - 15 = 3s - s, so 20 = 2s, giving s = 10.

  6. The father's present age is therefore s + 30 = 10 + 30 = 40 years.

Cross-check: With father's present age 40 and son's present age 10, the gap is 40 - 10 = 30 years, matching the given condition. Five years later the father is 45 and the son is 15, and 45 = 3 × 15, confirming the ratio condition holds.

If 3^(x+1) = 5^(x-2), then find the value of x.
(Take log 5 = 0.6989 and log 3 = 0.4771)
solution:
Solution: Solve the equation 3^(x+1) = 5^(x-2) by taking logarithms.

  • Take logarithm of both sides: (x + 1) log 3 = (x - 2) log 5.

  • Expand: x log 3 + log 3 = x log 5 - 2 log 5.

  • Collect x terms: x (log 3 - log 5) = -2 log 5 - log 3.

  • Solve for x: x = (2 log 5 + log 3) / (log 5 - log 3).

  • Substitute the given values: numerator = 2 × 0.6989 + 0.4771 = 1.8749; denominator = 0.6989 - 0.4771 = 0.2218.

  • Compute: x = 1.8749 / 0.2218 ≈ 8.45, which rounds to 8.5.

title: If the thrice of three consecutive odd no is equal
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If thrice the first of three consecutive odd numbers is equal to 3 more than twice the last number, then find the 3rd largest of these odd numbers.
solution:
Three consecutive odd numbers can be represented algebraically as x, x + 2, and x + 4, where x is the first (smallest) and x + 4 is the last (largest) of the three. To find a specific term such as the '3rd largest', first solve for x from the given condition, then rank the three resulting numbers from largest to smallest.

Applying this to the given condition:

  1. Let the three consecutive odd numbers be x, x + 2, and x + 4.

  2. The condition states thrice the first number equals 3 more than twice the last number: 3x = 2(x + 4) + 3.

  3. Expand the right-hand side: 3x = 2x + 8 + 3 = 2x + 11.

  4. Solve for x: 3x - 2x = 11, so x = 11.

  5. The three consecutive odd numbers are 11, 13, and 15.

  6. Ranking them from largest to smallest: 15 is the 1st largest, 13 is the 2nd largest, and 11 is the 3rd largest.

Cross-check: 3 × 11 = 33, and 2 × 15 + 3 = 33 — both sides match, confirming x = 11 is correct.

Hence, the 3rd largest of the three odd numbers is 11.

title: The sum of positive number and its reciprocal is twice
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The sum of a positive number and its reciprocal is twice the difference of the number and its reciprocal. The number is:
solution:
Concept: To translate a word problem about the sum and difference of a number and its reciprocal into an equation, let the number be x, write the sum as x + 1/x and the difference as x − 1/x, translate the given relationship between the two into a single equation, and solve for x — keeping only the root(s) that satisfy any stated constraint such as positivity.

Application:

  1. Let the positive number be x, so its reciprocal is 1/x.

  2. The sum of the number and its reciprocal is x + 1/x, and their difference is x − 1/x.

  3. The problem states that the sum equals twice the difference: x + 1/x = 2(x − 1/x).

  4. Expand the right-hand side: x + 1/x = 2x − 2/x.

  5. Move the 1/x terms to the left and the x terms to the right: 1/x + 2/x = 2x − x.

  6. Combine like terms on each side: 3/x = x.

  7. Multiply both sides by x: 3 = x2.

  8. Since the number is positive, take the positive square root: x = √3.

Cross-check: With x = √3, the reciprocal 1/x = √3⁄3. Sum = √3 + √3⁄3 = 4√3⁄3, and difference = √3 − √3⁄3 = 2√3⁄3, so twice the difference = 4√3⁄3 — equal to the sum, confirming the value.

Result: The number is √3.

title: Directions Solve the quadratic and answer the following questions. One
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml:
Directions: Solve the quadratic equations and answer the question that follows.

A: (x − 2)2 = −3x2 + 22 + 25x − P
B: (10y2 − 32y + 2/3) × 3 + 10y = 0

One root of equation A is 5.

Which of the following are the roots of equation B?
solution:
Concept

A quadratic in the form ay2 + by + c = 0 is solved by first reducing the given expression to this standard form, then factorising the middle term (split b into two parts whose product is a·c and whose sum is b). The two factors give the two roots. Always simplify every bracket and multiplier before reading off a, b and c.

Application — Equation B

  1. Expand the inner bracket times 3: (10y2 − 9y + 2/3) × 3 = 30y2 − 27y + 2. (Note 32 = 9 and (2/3)×3 = 2.)

  2. Add the remaining 10y: 30y2 − 27y + 2 + 10y = 30y2 − 17y + 2 = 0. So a = 30, b = −17, c = 2.

  3. Split the middle term using a·c = 30 × 2 = 60 and sum = −17: the parts are −12 and −5 (since −12 × −5 = 60 and −12 + −5 = −17).

  4. Factorise: 30y2 − 12y − 5y + 2 = 6y(5y − 2) − 1(5y − 2) = (5y − 2)(6y − 1) = 0.

  5. Set each factor to zero: 5y − 2 = 0 → y = 2/5; 6y − 1 = 0 → y = 1/6.

Roots of equation B: 2/5 and 1/6.

Cross-check

Sum of roots should equal −b/a = 17/30. Check: 2/5 + 1/6 = 12/30 + 5/30 = 17/30. ✓ Product should equal c/a = 2/30 = 1/15. Check: (2/5)(1/6) = 2/30 = 1/15. ✓ Both match, confirming the roots.

title: In each of these questions, two equation and (II) are
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml:
In each of these questions, two equation (I) and (II) are given. You have to solve both the equations and give answer.

I. 4x² + 20x + 25 = 0
II. 2y² + 11y + 15 = 0

options.label: E
options.html: If x = y or no relation can be established between x and y

solution:
Concept

To compare two variables that are each defined by a separate quadratic equation, solve each equation on its own to get its roots, then compare every root of the first variable against every root of the second. A single overall relation (≥, ≤, >, < or =) holds only when it is true for all such pairings; if some pairs give one sign and others give equality or the opposite sign, the relation must be widened or declared indeterminate. A perfect-square quadratic gives one repeated root.

Application

  1. Equation I: 4x2 + 20x + 25 = 0 is a perfect square, since it equals (2x + 5)2 = 0. So 2x + 5 = 0, giving the single repeated root x = −5/2 = −2.5.

  2. Equation II: 2y2 + 11y + 15 = 0. Factor by splitting the middle term: 2y2 + 6y + 5y + 15 = 2y(y + 3) + 5(y + 3) = (2y + 5)(y + 3) = 0. So y = −5/2 = −2.5 or y = −3.

  3. Compare x = −2.5 with each y value: against y = −2.5 we get x = y; against y = −3 we get −2.5 > −3, i.e. x > y.

  4. Across both cases x is never less than y — it is either equal to y or greater than y — so the relation that holds for every pair is x ≥ y.

Cross-check

Place the values on a number line: x sits at −2.5, while y is at −2.5 or −3. The smallest y (−3) lies to the left of x, and the largest y (−2.5) coincides with x. There is no y to the right of x, so x can never be strictly less than y; the tightest single relation covering both equal and greater cases is x ≥ y.

solution:
Given quadratic equation:
x² + 2x − 15 = 0

title: If and are the roots of the equation then the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If x1​ and x2​ are the roots of the equation 2x2+3x−9=0 then the equation which has the roots 1/x1​ and 1/x2 is:
solution:
Concept

For a quadratic ax2+bx+c=0 with roots α and β, Vieta's formulas give the sum α+β = −b/a and the product αβ = c/a. To build a new quadratic whose roots are expressions of α and β, first compute the new sum S and new product P, then write x2 − Sx + P = 0.

Reciprocal-root shortcut: replacing x with 1/x in ax2+bx+c=0 (i.e. reversing the order of the coefficients) yields the equation whose roots are 1/α and 1/β, namely cx2+bx+a=0.

Application

  1. Here a=2, b=3, c=−9, so the original roots satisfy x1+x2 = −b/a = −3/2 and x1x2 = c/a = −9/2.

  2. New sum: 1/x1 + 1/x2 = (x1+x2)/(x1x2) = (−3/2)/(−9/2) = 1/3.

  3. New product: 1/(x1x2) = 1/(−9/2) = −2/9.

  4. Form the equation: x2 − (1/3)x + (−2/9) = 0, i.e. x2 − (1/3)x − 2/9 = 0.

  5. Multiply through by 9 to clear the denominators: 9x2 − 3x − 2 = 0.

Cross-check

Apply the reciprocal shortcut directly: substitute x → 1/x in 2x2+3x−9=0 to get 2/x2 + 3/x − 9 = 0; multiplying by x2 gives 2 + 3x − 9x2 = 0, and multiplying by −1 gives 9x2 − 3x − 2 = 0 — the same equation, confirming the result.

title: Is negative number such that then what is the value
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml:
k + k-1 = -2. k is a negative number satisfying this. What is the value of

?
solution:
Concept: For an equation of the form k + k-1 = c, multiplying both sides by k (k not equal to 0) clears the fraction into k2 - ck + 1 = 0. When c = -2, this becomes k2 + 2k + 1 = 0 - the perfect-square identity a2 + 2ab + b2 = (a + b)2 with a = k, b = 1 - so it factors as (k + 1)2 = 0. A repeated root like this pins down a single value of k, unlike a generic quadratic with two distinct roots.

Application:

  1. Multiply the given equation by k: k2 + 1 = -2k.

  2. Rearrange to standard form: k2 + 2k + 1 = 0.

  3. Recognise the perfect-square identity: (k + 1)2 = 0, so k = -1 - which is indeed negative, matching the given condition.

  4. Substitute k = -1 into the numerator: k2 + 4k - 2 = 1 - 4 - 2 = -5.

  5. Substitute k = -1 into the denominator: k2 + k - 5 = 1 - 1 - 5 = -5.

  6. Divide the two: (-5) / (-5) = 1.

Cross-check: Plugging k = -1 back into the original condition confirms it: -1 + (-1)-1 = -1 + (-1) = -2, which matches what was given. So the value of the expression is 1.

title: If 2x+2/x=3 then the value of is:
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If 2x + (2/x) = 3, then the value of x³ + (1/x³) + 2 is:
solution:
Given: 2x + (2/x) = 3.

Divide both sides by 2: x + (1/x) = 3/2.

Use the identity (x + 1/x)³ = x³ + 1/x³ + 3(x + 1/x).

Rearranging: x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)³ - 3(x + 1/x) = (3/2)³ - 3(3/2).

Since (3/2)³ = 27/8 and 3(3/2) = 9/2 = 36/8, we get x³ + 1/x³ = 27/8 - 36/8 = -9/8.

Finally add 2: x³ + 1/x³ + 2 = -9/8 + 16/8 = 7/8.

Therefore the required value is 7/8.

title: Twenty times positive integer is less than its square by
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Twenty times a positive integer is less than its square by 96. What is the integer?
solution:
Concept: A word problem translates into an equation phrase by phrase. "A is less than B by C" means B − A = C. Let the positive integer be x; "its square" is x2 and "twenty times" the integer is 20x, so the stated relation becomes the quadratic x2 − 20x = 96.

  1. Set up the equation: x2 − 20x = 96, i.e. x2 − 20x − 96 = 0.

  2. Factor the quadratic: find two numbers whose product is −96 and whose sum is −20 — these are −24 and 4, since (−24) × 4 = −96 and (−24) + 4 = −20.

  3. So x2 − 20x − 96 = (x − 24)(x + 4) = 0, giving x = 24 or x = −4.

  4. The problem restricts the integer to be positive, so reject x = −4 and keep x = 24.

Cross-check: 242 − 20 × 24 = 576 − 480 = 96, exactly the difference stated in the question, confirming the value.

title: If then is?
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If (1 + x - 2x2)6 = 1 + a1x + a2x2 + ... + a12x12 , then a2 + a4 + ... a12 is?
solution:
Expand and write (1 + x - 2x^2)^6 = 1 + a1·x + a2·x^2 + ... + a12·x^12.

We need the sum of the even-index coefficients a2 + a4 + a6 + a8 + a10 + a12.

Step 1 — Substitute x = 1: f(1) = (1 + 1 - 2)^6 = 0^6 = 0. This gives a0 + a1 + a2 + ... + a12 = 0.

Step 2 — Substitute x = -1: f(-1) = (1 - 1 - 2)^6 = (-2)^6 = 64. This gives a0 - a1 + a2 - a3 + ... + a12 = 64.

Step 3 — Add the two results: f(1) + f(-1) = 2(a0 + a2 + a4 + ... + a12) = 0 + 64 = 64, so a0 + a2 + a4 + ... + a12 = 32.

Step 4 — The constant term a0 equals f(0) = 1 (the value of the constant in the expansion). Therefore a2 + a4 + ... + a12 = 32 - 1 = 31.

Hence the required sum a2 + a4 + ... + a12 = 31.

title: What will be the remainder when we divide by
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: What will be the remainder when we divide (x71 + 71) by (x + 1)?
solution:
Key idea: Use the Remainder Theorem: the remainder when dividing a polynomial by x + 1 equals the polynomial evaluated at x = -1.

Let P(x) = x^71 + 71.

  1. Set x = -1 because x + 1 = 0 at x = -1.

  2. Compute P(-1) = (-1)^71 + 71 = -1 + 71 = 70.

Therefore the remainder is 70.

title: If and then the minimum value of 2y−3x is:
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If −5 ≤ x ≤ 3 and −1 ≤ y ≤ 0, then the minimum value of 2y − 3x is:
solution:
Concept: A linear expression in variables that vary independently over a rectangular (box) domain reaches its extreme values at the corner points, and each term can be optimised on its own. A term with a positive coefficient is made as small as possible by taking its variable at the low end of its interval; a term with a negative coefficient is made as small as possible by taking its variable at the high end.

Application: Here the expression is f = 2y - 3x, and x and y vary independently within their given intervals.

  1. The term 2y has a positive coefficient, so it is smallest when y is at its lowest value, y = -1, giving 2y = -2.

  2. The term -3x has a negative coefficient, so it is smallest when x is at its highest value, x = 3, giving -3x = -9.

  3. Adding the two smallest contributions: f = (-2) + (-9) = -11.

Cross-check: At the corner (x, y) = (3, -1): 2(-1) - 3(3) = -2 - 9 = -11. The opposite corner (x, y) = (-5, 0) gives 2(0) - 3(-5) = 15, which is the maximum, so -11 is indeed the minimum.

title: Can finish the work in days and in days. They
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A can finish the work in 25 days and B in 25 days. They both work together for 5 days and then B leaves. How many more days will A take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
Concept

Work-and-time problems use rates: if a worker finishes a job in n days, that worker's one-day rate is 1/n of the job. Rates add when people work together, and Work done = rate × time. The remaining fraction of the job is 1 minus the fraction already completed, and time for one worker to finish it equals remaining work ÷ that worker's rate.

Application

  1. A's one-day rate = 1/25 of the job; B's one-day rate = 1/25 of the job.

  2. Combined one-day rate = 1/25 + 1/25 = 2/25 of the job.

  3. Work done together in 5 days = 5 × 2/25 = 10/25 = 2/5 of the job.

  4. Remaining work = 1 − 2/5 = 3/5 of the job.

  5. A finishes the remaining 3/5 alone: time = (3/5) ÷ (1/25) = (3/5) × 25 = 15 days.

Cross-check

In 15 days A does 15 × (1/25) = 15/25 = 3/5 of the job, which is exactly the remaining work. Adding the 2/5 done in the first 5 days gives 2/5 + 3/5 = 1 (the whole job), so 15 days is consistent.

title: If it takes two workers, working separately but at the
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: If it takes two workers, working separately but at the same speed, 2 hours and 40 minutes to complete a particular task, about how long will it take one worker, working at the same speed, to complete the same task alone?
solution:
To solve this problem, we must understand the inverse relationship between the number of workers and the time required to complete a task.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Standardize Units: First, convert the given time into minutes for easier calculation.

2 hours and 40 minutes = (2 × 60) + 40 = 120 + 40 = 160 minutes.

Analyze the Work Relationship: The problem states two workers take 160 minutes working separately. This implies that if both workers were working simultaneously on the same task, the time would be shorter; however, the prompt clarifies they are working "separately but at the same speed" to complete a particular task. If the total man-hours required for the task is distributed among them, reducing the workforce to one worker means the remaining worker must perform the total work alone.

Calculate the Time for One Worker: Since one worker is doing the work that two workers were splitting, it will take twice as long.

Time = 160 minutes × 2 = 320 minutes.

Convert Back to Hours and Minutes:

320 minutes ÷ 60 minutes/hour = 5 hours with a remainder of 20 minutes.

Total time = 5 hours and 20 minutes.

Correct Option
Option D: 5 hrs. 20 min

title: Can finish the work in days and in days. They
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A can finish the work in 30 days and B in 40 days. They both work together for 5 days and then B leaves. How many days will A take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
Concept

In work-rate problems, each worker's one-day output is the reciprocal of the time they take alone. Outputs add when people work together, the total job equals 1 (or, conveniently, the LCM of the individual times in "units"), and remaining time equals remaining work divided by the rate of whoever finishes it.

Application

  1. Take the total work as the LCM of 30 and 40, which is 120 units. Then A does 120/30 = 4 units per day and B does 120/40 = 3 units per day.

  2. Working together, their combined output is 4 + 3 = 7 units per day. Over 5 days they complete 7 x 5 = 35 units.

  3. Work still left after B leaves = 120 - 35 = 85 units.

  4. A finishes this alone at 4 units per day, so the time needed = 85 / 4 = 21.25 days.

Cross-check

Using fractions instead of units: in 5 days the pair completes 5 x (1/30 + 1/40) = 5 x 7/120 = 7/24 of the job, leaving 17/24. A alone needs (17/24) / (1/30) = (17/24) x 30 = 21.25 days, which matches.

bodyHtml: Worker X completes a task in 8 days and worker Y completes the same task in 10 days. If both X and Y work together, in how many days they will complete the task?
solution:
Concept: When a worker finishes a job in n days, that worker's one-day work (rate) is 1/n of the job. The rates of people working together ADD UP, and the total time to finish together is the reciprocal of the combined one-day rate.

  1. X finishes in 8 days, so X's one-day work = 1/8 of the task.

  2. Y finishes in 10 days, so Y's one-day work = 1/10 of the task.

  3. Working together, their one-day work adds: 1/8 + 1/10. Taking the common denominator 40 gives 5/40 + 4/40 = 9/40 of the task per day.

  4. Time to finish together = reciprocal of the combined one-day work = 1 / (9/40) = 40/9 days.

Cross-check: in 40/9 days, X does (1/8)(40/9) = 5/9 and Y does (1/10)(40/9) = 4/9; 5/9 + 4/9 = 1 whole task, which confirms the result.

title: Combined work rate with 8-hour workday
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: X can complete one work in 5 days. Y can complete the same work twice in 15 days, and Z can complete the same work three times in 7 days. If they work together for 8 hours a day, how much time will they take to complete one work?
solution:
CONCEPT: In time-and-work questions, each person's capacity is converted into a rate: work completed per day. When people work together, their rates are added; if a workday has fixed hours, fractional working days are converted into hours by multiplying by hours per day.

  1. X completes 1 work in 5 days, so X's rate is 1/5 work per day.

  2. Y completes 2 works in 15 days, so Y's rate is 2/15 work per day.

  3. Z completes 3 works in 7 days, so Z's rate is 3/7 work per day.

  4. Combined rate = 1/5 + 2/15 + 3/7 = 21/105 + 14/105 + 45/105 = 80/105 = 16/21 work per day.

  5. Time for 1 work = 1 divided by (16/21) = 21/16 working days.

  6. Each working day is 8 hours, so time = (21/16) × 8 = 21/2 hours = 10.5 hours.

CROSS-CHECK: In 10.5 working hours, the fraction of an 8-hour day is 10.5/8 = 21/16 days; multiplying this by the combined rate 16/21 gives exactly 1 full work.

Therefore, the required time is 10 hours 30 minutes.

solution:
To solve this problem, we need to determine the work rates of each individual or pair. The work rate is the portion of the total work completed in one day.

Step-by-Step Calculation
Define the Work Rates:

Let the work rate of X be x, Y be y, and Z be z.

X + Y = 1/60 (rate per day)

Y + Z = 1/90 (rate per day)

X + Y + Z = 1/45 (rate per day)

Find the individual rate of Y:

First, add the rates of (X + Y) and (Y + Z):
(X + Y) + (Y + Z) = 1/60 + 1/90
X + 2Y + Z = 3/180 + 2/180 = 5/180 = 1/36

Now, subtract the trio's rate (X + Y + Z) from this sum to isolate Y:
(X + 2Y + Z) - (X + Y + Z) = 1/36 - 1/45
Y = 5/180 - 4/180 = 1/180 per day.

Find the combined rate of X + Z:

We know X + Y + Z = 1/45.

X + Z = (X + Y + Z) - Y

X + Z = 1/45 - 1/180

Convert to common denominator: 4/180 - 1/180 = 3/180 = 1/60 per day.

Calculate the time for X + Z:

Since X + Z complete 1/60 of the work in one day, they will take 60 days to complete the entire job.

title: DSSSB TGT English 24 Aug 2025 5-7 PM Q57

bodyHtml: Jitesh and Kamal can complete a certain piece of work in 9 and 12 days respectively. They started to work together, and after 5 days, Kamal left. In how many days will Jitesh complete the remaining work?
solution:
Work-rate method: if a person completes a job in T days, their work rate is 1/T of the job per day. When two people work together, their combined rate is the sum of their individual rates, and the work completed over any period equals rate multiplied by time.

  1. Jitesh's rate = 1/9 of the work per day; Kamal's rate = 1/12 of the work per day.

  2. Combined rate working together = 1/9 + 1/12 = 4/36 + 3/36 = 7/36 of the work per day.

  4. Remaining work after Kamal leaves = 1 - 35/36 = 1/36 of the work.

  5. Time for Jitesh alone to finish 1/36 of the work at his rate of 1/9 per day = (1/36) / (1/9) = 9/36 = 1/4 day = 0.25 days.

Cross-check with the LCM method: take total work as 36 units (LCM of 9 and 12). Jitesh's rate = 36/9 = 4 units/day, Kamal's rate = 36/12 = 3 units/day, combined = 7 units/day. In 5 days together they finish 35 units, leaving 1 unit. At 4 units/day, Jitesh needs 1/4 = 0.25 day to finish the remaining 1 unit, confirming the same result.

title: Seven girls can do piece of work in days, six
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Seven girls can do a piece of work in 13 days, six boys can do the same piece of work in 12 days, nine men can do the same piece of work in 9 days and six women can do the same piece of work in 14 days. Who are the most efficient?
solution:
Concept

Efficiency means work done per person per day, not the number of days a whole group takes. If a group of N people finishes one unit of work in D days, the team's combined person-days is N x D, and each individual's daily rate is 1 / (N x D). The smaller the value of N x D, the higher the individual efficiency.

Applying it to each group

  1. Girls: N x D = 7 x 13 = 91, so each girl's rate = 1/91 per day.

  2. Boys: N x D = 6 x 12 = 72, so each boy's rate = 1/72 per day.

  3. Men: N x D = 9 x 9 = 81, so each man's rate = 1/81 per day.

  4. Women: N x D = 6 x 14 = 84, so each woman's rate = 1/84 per day.

Cross-check

Cross-check: compare the person-day totals 91, 72, 81 and 84. The smallest total is 72, which gives the largest individual daily rate 1/72. Hence one boy does more work per day than one girl, one man or one woman, so boys are the most efficient.

title: TPSC CMIS Pre 2015 Q98
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: 6 men or 8 women can do a work in 25 days. The number of days required by 8 men and 6 women to complete the work is
solution:
When two groups can each finish the very same job in the very same number of days, their total daily outputs must be equal — this equality is what fixes the ratio between one individual's daily work in one group and one individual's daily work in the other group. That per-person efficiency ratio, combined with the job's total size, is what then decides how long any differently composed team needs for the same job.

  1. Let one man's one-day work be m and one woman's one-day work be w.

  2. Since 6 men finish the job in 25 days and 8 women finish the same job in 25 days, both groups produce the same total work: 6m × 25 = 8w × 25, so 6m = 8w, i.e. m : w = 4 : 3.

  3. Write the job as 24 units (the LCM of 6 and 8). Then 6 men completing 24 units in 25 days gives 1 man's daily work = 24 ÷ (6 × 25) = 4/25 unit; 8 women completing 24 units in 25 days gives 1 woman's daily work = 24 ÷ (8 × 25) = 3/25 unit — consistent with the 4 : 3 ratio.

  4. The new team of 8 men and 6 women therefore does 8 × 4/25 + 6 × 3/25 = 32/25 + 18/25 = 50/25 = 2 units per day.

  5. Days required = total work ÷ daily rate = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 days.

Cross-checking with the man-equivalent route: since 1 woman = 3/4 man (from the 4 : 3 ratio), 8 men and 6 women equal 8 + 6 × 3/4 = 12.5 man-equivalents. The whole job equals 6 men's 25-day output, i.e. 6 × 25 = 150 man-days. So the new team needs 150 ÷ 12.5 = 12 days — the same result.

So the work is completed in 12 days.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q72
