bodyHtml: 3 men or 4 women can build a wall in 43 days. The number of days that 7 men and 5 women take to build it is
solution:
Concept: When a problem says that "A men OR B women can do a job in D days", it means each group ALONE completes the SAME job in D days, so their total effort in worker-days is equal: A × D man-days = B × D woman-days = one full job. This lets us find each individual's daily work rate, and then combine any mix of men and women using those rates.

Application:

  1. Total work in man-days: 3 men complete the wall in 43 days, so total work = 3 × 43 = 129 man-days.

  2. Total work in woman-days: 4 women complete the wall in 43 days, so total work = 4 × 43 = 172 woman-days.

  3. One man's daily rate = 1/129 of the wall, since 129 man-days make up 1 wall.

  4. One woman's daily rate = 1/172 of the wall, since 172 woman-days make up 1 wall.

  5. Combined daily rate of 7 men and 5 women = 7 × (1/129) + 5 × (1/172) = 7/129 + 5/172.

  6. Put both fractions over the LCM of 129 and 172, which is 516: 7/129 = 28/516 and 5/172 = 15/516.

  7. Add the fractions: 28/516 + 15/516 = 43/516 = 1/12 of the wall per day.

  8. At a combined rate of 1/12 of the wall per day, the whole wall is finished in 12 days.

Cross-check: Convert everyone into 'man-equivalent' workers using the given exchange rate 3 men = 4 women, i.e. 1 woman = 3/4 man in daily output. Then 7 men and 5 women together equal 7 + 5 × (3/4) = 7 + 3.75 = 10.75 man-equivalents. Since 3 men finish the wall in 43 days, one man-equivalent's daily rate is 1/(3 × 43) = 1/129 of the wall, matching the rate found in step 3, so 10.75 man-equivalents' daily rate is 10.75/129 = 43/516 = 1/12 of the wall per day — the same rate found above, confirming the day count.

Result: 7 men and 5 women together complete the wall in 12 days.

title: Can finish the work in days and in days. They
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A can finish the work in 15 days and B in 30 days. They both work together for 5 days and then B leaves. How many days will A take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
Concept

When several workers act together, their one-day work rates ADD UP. If a worker finishes a job in n days, that worker's one-day rate is 1/n of the job. Treat the whole job as 1 unit, find the fraction done in the given period, subtract from 1 to get the remaining fraction, then divide that remaining fraction by the rate of whoever finishes it.

Application

  1. A's one-day rate = 1/15 of the job; B's one-day rate = 1/30 of the job.

  2. Combined one-day rate of A and B = 1/15 + 1/30 = 2/30 + 1/30 = 3/30 = 1/10 of the job.

  3. Work done together in 5 days = 5 × 1/10 = 5/10 = 1/2 of the job.

  4. Remaining work = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2 of the job.

  5. A finishes this alone at 1/15 per day, so time = (1/2) ÷ (1/15) = (1/2) × 15 = 15/2 = 7.5 days.

Cross-check

In 7.5 days A alone does 7.5 × 1/15 = 7.5/15 = 1/2 of the job. Added to the 1/2 already completed in the first 5 days, the total is exactly 1 whole job, which confirms the result.

title: IOCL Technical Attendant Numerical Ability 2024 Q77
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: हितेश अकेले एक कार्य को 11 दिनों में पूरा कर सकता है और जितेश उसी कार्य को अकेले 10 दिनों में पूरा कर सकता है। उन्होंने एक साथ कार्य करना शुरू किया, लेकिन हितेश को कार्य पूरा होने से 6 दिन पहले कार्य छोड़ना पड़ा। कार्य कितने दिनों में पूरा होगा?
solution:
अवधारणा

यदि कोई व्यक्ति किसी कार्य को a दिनों में पूरा करता है, तो उसकी एक दिन की कार्य-दर 1/a होती है। साथ काम करते समय दरें जुड़ती हैं; जो व्यक्ति पहले काम छोड़ता है, उसके कार्य-दिन कुल समय से अलग गिने जाते हैं।

कुल किए गए कार्य को 1 मानकर प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की दर × उसके वास्तविक कार्य-दिन लिखने से समय का समीकरण बनता है।

अनुप्रयोग

  1. मान लें कि कार्य पूरा होने में कुल t दिन लगे। जितेश ने t दिन और हितेश ने t − 6 दिन काम किया।

  2. दोनों का किया हुआ कार्य जोड़ने पर (t − 6)/11 + t/10 = 1।

  3. हर को 110 से गुणा करने पर 10(t − 6) + 11t = 110।

  4. अर्थात 10t − 60 + 11t = 110, इसलिए 21t = 170।

  5. अतः t = 170/21 = 8 2/21 दिन।

पुनः जाँच

  1. कुल कार्य 110 इकाई मानें। तब हितेश और जितेश की दरें क्रमशः 10 और 11 इकाई प्रतिदिन हैं।

  2. यदि दोनों x दिन साथ काम करें और जितेश अंतिम 6 दिन अकेले काम करे, तो 21x + 11 × 6 = 110।

  3. इससे x = 44/21 दिन और कुल समय x + 6 = 170/21 = 8 2/21 दिन मिलता है।

परिणाम

कार्य 8 2/21 दिनों में पूरा होगा।

title: IOCL 2024 Numerical Ability Q87
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: आदित्य किसी कार्य को अकेले 12 दिनों में पूरा कर सकता है और भगवान उसी कार्य को अकेले 8 दिनों में पूरा कर सकता है। उन्होंने एक साथ कार्य करना शुरू किया, लेकिन कार्य पूरा होने से 7 दिन पहले आदित्य को कार्य छोड़ना पड़ा। कार्य कितने दिनों में पूरा होगा?
solution: मान लें कुल कार्य \(24\) इकाई है। आदित्य की दर \(\frac{24}{12}=2\) इकाई प्रतिदिन और भगवान की दर \(\frac{24}{8}=3\) इकाई प्रतिदिन है। मान लें कार्य \(T\) दिनों में पूरा होता है। आदित्य \(T-7\) दिन कार्य करता है, भगवान \(T\) दिन कार्य करते हैं। अतः \(2(T-7)+3T=24\)। हल करने पर \(5T=38\), अतः \(T=\frac{38}{5}=7\frac{3}{5}\) दिन।

title: An army post with men has provision of food for
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: An army post with 1800 men has provision of food for 50 days. After 10 days, some of the men go back to the base camp due to injuries. The remaining food is now enough for the next 50 days for the remaining men. What is the number of men who went back to the base camp?
solution:
Concept

In ration/provision problems, total food is measured in man-days: total man-days = (number of men) × (number of days the food lasts). This quantity is conserved — the man-days consumed plus the man-days still available always equal the original total, regardless of how the men or days change.

Application

  1. Original total food = 1800 men × 50 days = 90000 man-days.

  2. Food eaten in the first 10 days by all 1800 men = 1800 × 10 = 18000 man-days.

  3. Food left after 10 days = 90000 − 18000 = 72000 man-days.

  4. Let the number of remaining men be R. This leftover food must last the next 50 days, so R × 50 = 72000, giving R = 1440 men.

  5. Men who went back = original − remaining = 1800 − 1440 = 360.

Cross-check

Verify by the other route: the untouched 40 days of the original schedule hold 1800 × 40 = 72000 man-days, which matches the leftover food. Spread over 50 days that is 72000 ÷ 50 = 1440 men, so 360 men must have left — consistent with the man-days balance.

title: An army of men has provision for days. After days
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: An army of 2100 men has provision for 50 days. After 10 days due to injuries some of them left and the food were now enough for next 50 days for remaining men. The number of men left is:
solution:
Concept

In any provisions/work problem the total resource is conserved and equals the product men × days, measured in man-days. The same stock of food gives a fixed number of man-days; if the number of men changes, the days it lasts adjust so that men × days stays equal to the food that remains.

Application

  1. Total food provisioned at the start = 2100 × 50 = 105000 man-days.

  2. Food consumed in the first 10 days by all 2100 men = 2100 × 10 = 21000 man-days.

  3. Food still remaining after 10 days = 105000 − 21000 = 84000 man-days.

  4. Let the number of men remaining be R. This remaining food must last 50 more days: R × 50 = 84000.

  5. Solve for R: R = 84000 ÷ 50 = 1680 men remaining.

  6. Men who left = original men − remaining men = 2100 − 1680 = 420.

Cross-check

Put R = 1680 back in: 1680 men for 50 days need 1680 × 50 = 84000 man-days, which is exactly the food left after 10 days. The balance holds, so 420 men left.

title: An army of men has provision for days. After days
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: An army of 1500 men has provisions for 50 days. After 10 days, due to injuries some of them left, and the remaining food was now sufficient for the next 50 days for the remaining men. The number of men who left is:
solution:
Concept

In provision problems the total stock of food is measured in man-days: total man-days = (number of men) x (number of days). This quantity is fixed by how much food exists, so the food eaten in any period equals (men present) x (days elapsed), and the food still left equals the original total minus what has been consumed.

Application

  1. Total food at the start = 1500 x 50 = 75000 man-days.

  2. Food consumed in the first 10 days (all 1500 men present) = 1500 x 10 = 15000 man-days.

  3. Food remaining after 10 days = 75000 - 15000 = 60000 man-days.

  4. Let the number of men remaining be R. This remaining food must last the next 50 days, so R x 50 = 60000, giving R = 60000 / 50 = 1200 men.

  5. Men who left = original men - remaining men = 1500 - 1200 = 300.

Cross-check

Verify the balance: 1200 remaining men over 50 days need 1200 x 50 = 60000 man-days, exactly the food left after the first 10 days. So 300 is the number of men who left.

title: IOCL Junior Engineering Assistant - IV Numerical Ability 2024 Q78
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: 102 men have provisions for 12 days. If 34 men leave, for how many days will the same provisions last for the remaining men?
solution:
Concept

For a fixed quantity of provisions and an unchanged daily consumption rate per person, the number of people and the number of days vary inversely.

Therefore, people × days remains constant; this product is the total supply measured in man-days.

Application

  1. Calculate the available supply: 102 × 12 = 1,224 man-days.

  2. Calculate the remaining group: 102 − 34 = 68 men.

  3. Let the provisions last d days. Then 68d = 1,224, so d = 1,224 ÷ 68 = 18 days.

Cross-check

At 68 men for 18 days, consumption is 68 × 18 = 1,224 man-days, exactly the original supply.

Hence, the provisions will last 18 days.

title: Men can do work in days working hours day. If
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: 10 men can do a work in 15 days working 4 hours a day. If after 5 days, 4 men leave the work, then remaining work can be done in how many days?
solution:
Total work: 10 men * 15 days * 4 hours/day = 600 man-hours.

Work done in 5 days: 10 men * 5 days * 4 hours/day = 200 man-hours.

Remaining work: 600 - 200 = 400 man-hours.

Remaining men: 10 - 4 = 6 men.

Calculate remaining days (D): 6 men * D * 4 hours/day = 400 man-hours.

24 * D = 400

D = 400 / 24 = 50 / 3 days.

Final Answer: Option 1 (50/3)

title: The water from one outlet, flowing at constant rate, can

If both the outlets are used at the same time, approximately what is the number of hours required to fill the pool?
solution:
Assume tank capacity is 45 Liters.

Given that the first pipe fills the tank in 9 hours.

So its capacity is 45 / 9 = 5 Liters/ Hour.

Second pipe fills the tank in 5 hours.

So its capacity is 45 / 5 = 9 Liters/Hour. If both pipes are opened together, then combined capacity is 14 liters/hour.

To fill a tank of capacity 45 liters, Both pipes takes 45 / 14 = 3.21 Hours.

title: Solution is percent liquid and percent water. If kilograms of
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Solution Y is 30 percent liquid X and 70 percent water. If 2 kilograms of water evaporate from 8 kilograms of solution Y and 2 kilograms of solution Y are added to the remaining 6 kilograms of liquid, what percent of this new solution is liquid X?
solution:
Y is 3/10 liquid X and 7/10 water. We start with 8kg of the solution. So the solution is 3/10 * 8 = 2.4kg of liquid X. Therefore there are 8 - 2.4 = 5.6kg water.

From this we subtract the 2kg water that has evaporated, leaving 5.6 - 2 = 3.6 kg water. We now have 2.4 kg liquid X and 3.6 kg water. To this we now add 2kg of solution. So that would be 0.6kg of liquid X and 1.4 kg of water that we are adding (solution is 3/10 liquid X and 7/10 water). So we now have 2.4 + 0.6 = 3 kg of liquid X, and 3.6 + 1.4 = 5kg of water and we have 8kg in total. So the percent of this new solution that is liquid X is: 3/8 = 37.5%

title: There are four mixtures and containing liquids and in different
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: There are four mixtures (P, Q, R and S) containing liquids X and Y in different proportions. Mixture P contains X and Y in the ratio 1:2, Q in the ratio 11:13, R in the ratio 5:3 and S in the ratio 19:5. Which of the following parts, mixed in equal quantity will have the highest concentration?
solution:
Step 1: Find the fraction of X in each mixture:

  • P: X/(X+Y) = 1/(1+2) = 1/3 = 8/24

  • Q: 11/(11+13) = 11/24

  • R: 5/(5+3) = 5/8 = 15/24

  • S: 19/(19+5) = 19/24

Step 2: When equal quantities of two mixtures are mixed, the resulting fraction of X is the average of their fractions.

  • Q and R: (11/24 + 15/24)/2 = 26/48 = 13/24 ≈ 0.5417

  • P and R: (8/24 + 15/24)/2 = 23/48 ≈ 0.4792

  • P and S: (8/24 + 19/24)/2 = 27/48 = 9/16 = 0.5625

  • Q and P: (11/24 + 8/24)/2 = 19/48 ≈ 0.3958

Conclusion: Mixing P and S yields the highest concentration of X (9/16 ≈ 0.5625), so choosing the pair P and S is correct.

title: One type of liquid contains of Kerosene, the other contains
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: One type of liquid contains 25% of Kerosene, the other contains 30% of Kerosene. P can is filled with 6 parts of the first liquid and 4 parts of the second liquid. Find the percentage of the Kerosene in the new mixture.
solution:
Solution: Use the weighted average of the two percentages with weights equal to the parts mixed.

  • Multiply each percentage by its number of parts: 6 × 25 = 150 and 4 × 30 = 120.

  • Add these to get total kerosene units: 150 + 120 = 270.

  • Divide by total parts: total parts = 6 + 4 = 10, so percentage = 270 ÷ 10 = 27%.

Answer: 27%

title: In mixture of litres, the ratio of milk and water
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a mixture of 25 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 4 : 1. How many litres of milk must be added to make the ratio 16 : 1?
solution:
When a mixture's ratio changes because only one ingredient is added, the quantity of the untouched ingredient stays fixed. Express both the original and target ratios in terms of that fixed quantity, then find how much of the added ingredient is needed to reach the new ratio.

  1. In the original 25-litre mixture, milk : water = 4 : 1, so total parts = 5. Milk = (4/5) × 25 = 20 litres; Water = (1/5) × 25 = 5 litres.

  2. Only milk is added, so the water quantity remains fixed at 5 litres throughout.

  3. For the new ratio of milk : water = 16 : 1 with water fixed at 5 litres, the required milk quantity is 16 × 5 = 80 litres.

  4. Milk to be added = required milk − original milk = 80 − 20 = 60 litres.

Check: the new mixture has milk = 20 + 60 = 80 litres and water = 5 litres, giving 80 : 5 = 16 : 1, confirming the result. Hence, 60 litres of milk must be added.

title: To earn an extra profit, shopkeeper mixes kg of rice
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: To earn an extra profit, a shopkeeper mixes 30 kg of rice purchased at Rs 36/kg with 26 kg of rice purchased at Rs 20/kg. What percentage of profit will he make if he sells the mixture at Rs 30/kg?
solution:
Concept: When two quantities of goods with different cost prices are mixed, the cost price of the mixture is the quantity-weighted average of the individual cost prices — the total cost of both lots divided by the total quantity. The profit percentage on the mixture is then found in the usual way: (Selling Price − Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price × 100, using this weighted cost price as the base.

Applying this to the given mixture:

  1. Total cost of the mixture = (30 kg × ₹36/kg) + (26 kg × ₹20/kg) = ₹1080 + ₹520 = ₹1600.

  2. Total quantity of the mixture = 30 kg + 26 kg = 56 kg.

  3. Cost price of the mixture per kg = ₹1600 ÷ 56 = ₹200/7 ≈ ₹28.57 per kg.

  4. Selling price per kg = ₹30.

  5. Profit per kg = ₹30 − ₹200/7 = ₹10/7.

  6. Profit percentage = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100 = [(10/7) ÷ (200/7)] × 100 = (10 ÷ 200) × 100 = 5%.

Cross-check: Working with totals instead of per-kg values gives the same result — total revenue from selling all 56 kg at ₹30/kg is 56 × 30 = ₹1680, so the total profit is ₹1680 − ₹1600 = ₹80, and the profit percentage is (80 ÷ 1600) × 100 = 5%, confirming the answer.

Hence, the shopkeeper makes a profit of 5%.

title: In chemistry lab two beakers and contains and of spirit
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a chemistry lab two beakers A and B contains 36% and 40% of spirit respectively. If two liters from A is mixed with 4 liters of B. The ratio of spirit and water in the resulting mixture is:
solution:
Concept

When two liquid solutions are blended, the amount of any component in the mixture is the sum of that component's amount in each part, where component amount = volume × its fractional concentration. The remaining volume is the other component. Once you have the component totals, the required ratio is just one total to the other.

Application

  1. Spirit drawn from A = 2 × 36% = 2 × 0.36 = 0.72 litre.

  2. Spirit drawn from B = 4 × 40% = 4 × 0.40 = 1.60 litre.

  3. Total spirit = 0.72 + 1.60 = 2.32 litre.

  4. Total mixture poured = 2 + 4 = 6 litre.

  5. Water = total − spirit = 6 − 2.32 = 3.68 litre.

  6. Spirit : Water = 2.32 : 3.68. Multiply both by 100 to clear decimals → 232 : 368, then divide by their HCF 8 → 29 : 46.

Cross-check

Scale the answer back: 29 + 46 = 75 parts represent 6 litre, so 1 part = 0.08 litre. Spirit = 29 × 0.08 = 2.32 litre and water = 46 × 0.08 = 3.68 litre, which matches the totals computed above. Hence the ratio of spirit to water is 29 : 46.

title: Jeweler mixed gold and copper in two proportions. In type
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A jeweler mixed gold and copper in two proportions. In type A alloy, 6 gm gold is mixed with 5 gm copper and in type B alloy, 5 gm gold is mixed with 3 gm copper. If the jeweler mixed 122 gm gold and 90 gm copper, then find the weight of type B alloy.
solution:
Concept

In a fixed-ratio mixture (alloy), each constituent is a fixed fraction of every batch. If you mix a quantity of one alloy and a quantity of another, the total of each constituent is the sum of its contributions from both alloys. So two unknown alloy quantities can be found by writing one linear equation per constituent and solving the simultaneous pair.

Application

  1. Type A is gold:copper = 6:5, so one A-batch = 6 + 5 = 11 gm. Type B is gold:copper = 5:3, so one B-batch = 5 + 3 = 8 gm. Let a = number of A-batches and b = number of B-batches.

  2. Gold equation (total gold = 122): 6a + 5b = 122.

  3. Copper equation (total copper = 90): 5a + 3b = 90.

  4. Eliminate b: multiply the gold equation by 3 and the copper equation by 5 to get 18a + 15b = 366 and 25a + 15b = 450. Subtract: 7a = 84, so a = 12.

  5. Substitute a = 12 into 5a + 3b = 90: 60 + 3b = 90, so 3b = 30 and b = 10.

  6. Weight of type B alloy = b x 8 = 10 x 8 = 80 gm.

Cross-check

Weight of type A alloy = a x 11 = 12 x 11 = 132 gm. Total alloy = 132 + 80 = 212 gm, which equals total gold + total copper = 122 + 90 = 212 gm. Gold used = 6(12) + 5(10) = 72 + 50 = 122 and copper used = 5(12) + 3(10) = 60 + 30 = 90, matching the given amounts exactly.

Therefore the weight of type B alloy is 80 gm.

title: Rice mixture ratio for 15% gain
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In what ratio should rice costing Rs. 90 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 63 per kg so that selling the mixture at Rs. 86.25 per kg gives a gain of 15%?
solution:
CONCEPT

When a mixture is sold at a gain, first remove the gain from the selling price to find the cost price of the mixture. In alligation, the ratio of the dearer item to the cheaper item equals the opposite differences from the required mean cost.

APPLICATION

  1. Selling price of the mixture = Rs. 86.25 per kg and gain = 15%.

  2. Cost price of the mixture = 86.25 / 1.15 = Rs. 75 per kg.

  3. Dearer rice costs Rs. 90 per kg and cheaper rice costs Rs. 63 per kg, so the required mean cost Rs. 75 lies between them.

  4. By alligation, dearer : cheaper = (75 - 63) : (90 - 75) = 12 : 15 = 4 : 5.

CROSS-CHECK

Using 4 : 5, the weighted cost is (4 × 90 + 5 × 63) / 9 = (360 + 315) / 9 = Rs. 75 per kg. Adding 15% gives 75 × 1.15 = Rs. 86.25, matching the given selling price.

CONTRAST

  • 5 : 4 gives a higher weighted cost because it puts more quantity on the costlier rice.

  • 3 : 5 gives a lower weighted cost because it puts too little quantity on the costlier rice for this target mean.

  • 2 : 3 also keeps the weighted cost below the required mean for the stated selling-price condition.

RESULT

The required ratio of Rs. 90 rice to Rs. 63 rice is 4 : 5.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q69
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a mixture of 60 litres the ratio of milk and water is 2 : 1. The amount of water that must be added to make the ratio 1 : 2 is
solution:
Concept

In a mixture-adjustment problem where only one component is added (here, water), the quantity of the other component (milk) stays fixed throughout. So the required addition can be found by fixing the constant quantity, writing it against the new total for the desired ratio, and solving for the unknown amount added.

Application

  1. The 60 litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1, so milk = (2/3) × 60 = 40 litres and water = (1/3) × 60 = 20 litres.

  2. Only water is added, so the milk quantity stays fixed at 40 litres; let x litres of water be added.

  3. The new ratio of milk to water must be 1 : 2, so 40 / (20 + x) = 1 / 2.

  4. Cross-multiplying: 20 + x = 80, so x = 60.

Cross-check

Adding 60 litres of water gives a new water quantity of 20 + 60 = 80 litres, with milk still 40 litres. The ratio 40 : 80 simplifies to 1 : 2, which matches the required ratio, confirming the value.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2023 Q65
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In what ratio should tea costing ₹62 per kg be mixed with tea costing ₹72 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹64.50 per kg?
solution:
Concept

When two ingredients with different unit prices are mixed to obtain an intermediate price, the alligation rule compares each ingredient's distance from the mean price.

The quantity ratio of the cheaper ingredient to the dearer ingredient is (dearer price − mean price) : (mean price − cheaper price).

Application

  1. Let the required quantities of the ₹62 tea and the ₹72 tea be x kg and y kg respectively.

  2. By the weighted-average equation, 62x + 72y = 64.50(x + y).

  3. Rearranging gives 64.50x − 62x = 72y − 64.50y, so 2.50x = 7.50y.

  4. Therefore x : y = 7.50 : 2.50 = 3 : 1.

Cross-check

Using three equal parts of ₹62 tea and one equal part of ₹72 tea gives (3 × 62 + 1 × 72) ÷ 4 = 258 ÷ 4 = ₹64.50 per kg.

Hence, the tea costing ₹62 per kg and the tea costing ₹72 per kg should be mixed in the ratio 3 : 1.

title: Fuel dealer mixes two brands of fuel which cost in
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A fuel dealer mixes two brands of fuel which cost in the ratio 2 : 3. A solution containing 30% Brand A and remaining Brand B yields profit of 10% when sold at RS 297. What is cost of brand B?
solution:
Key steps:

  1. Compute the cost price (CP) per litre from the selling price (SP) and profit: CP = SP ÷ (1 + profit%) = 297 ÷ 1.10 = 270.

  2. Let the unit costs of Brand A and Brand B be 2c and 3c respectively, since their costs are in the ratio 2:3.

  3. The mixture contains 30% Brand A and 70% Brand B, so the mixture cost per litre = 0.3×(2c) + 0.7×(3c) = 2.7c.

  4. Set this equal to the CP found: 2.7c = 270 ⇒ c = 100.

  5. Therefore the cost of Brand B = 3c = 3×100 = 300.

Answer: 300

title: DSSSB TGT Special Education Teacher 24 Jun 2025 Shift 3 Q60
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of rice costing ₹195 and ₹138 per kg to get a mixture of rice worth ₹149 per kg?
solution:
Concept: Alligation is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients of different unit costs must be mixed to obtain a mixture of a specified mean cost. For a cheaper item priced a and a dearer item priced b mixed to get mean price m (where a < m < b), the rule of alligation gives Quantity(cheaper) : Quantity(dearer) = (b − m) : (m − a).

  1. Identify the given costs and mean: dearer price b = ₹195, cheaper price a = ₹138, mean price m = ₹149 (since a < m < b, the standard alligation rule applies).

  2. Apply the alligation rule: Quantity(cheaper) : Quantity(dearer) = (b − m) : (m − a) = (195 − 149) : (149 − 138) = 46 : 11.

  3. The question asks for the ratio in the order costly-to-cheap (₹195 rice to ₹138 rice), so invert the ratio: Quantity(₹195 rice) : Quantity(₹138 rice) = 11 : 46.

Cross-check: verify by computing the mean cost of a mixture in ratio 11:46 — (195 × 11 + 138 × 46) / (11 + 46) = (2145 + 6348) / 57 = 8493 / 57 = ₹149, which matches the given mean price, confirming the ratio.

So the required ratio in which the grocer must mix the ₹195 and ₹138 rice is 11 : 46.

title: In what ratio Sugar costing Rs.15 per kg be mixed
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In what ratio Sugar costing Rs.15 per kg be mixed with sugar costing Rs.24 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs.20 per kg?
solution:
Find the ratio in which sugar at Rs.15 per kg (lower price) and sugar at Rs.24 per kg (higher price) must be mixed to get a mixture worth Rs.20 per kg.

Method 1 (Alligation):

  • Difference between higher price and mean price: 24 − 20 = 4.

  • Difference between mean price and lower price: 20 − 15 = 5.

  • Therefore quantities of Rs.15 and Rs.24 sugars should be in the ratio 4 : 5 (lower : higher).

Method 2 (Algebra):

  • Let x kg be at Rs.15 and y kg be at Rs.24. Then (15x + 24y)/(x + y) = 20.

  • Multiply both sides: 15x + 24y = 20x + 20y → 24y − 20y = 20x − 15x → 4y = 5x.

  • So x : y = 4 : 5.

Final answer: Mix sugar costing Rs.15 per kg and Rs.24 per kg in the ratio 4 : 5.

title: Three different liquids which have water, water and of water
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Three different liquids which have 10% water, 20% water and x% of water are mixed in the ratio of their quantity 2 : 3 : 4 respectively. If 12% of water is present in final mixture, calculate value of x.
solution:
Concept

When several solutions are blended, the amount of a component (here, water) is conserved. The water in the mixture equals the sum of the water contributed by each part. Expressing each contribution as concentration x quantity and dividing by the total quantity gives the final concentration. This is the weighted average (alligation) principle: final % = (sum of conc x parts) / (total parts).

Application

Take the quantities in the given ratio 2 : 3 : 4, so the parts are 2, 3 and 4 and the total is 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts. Setting the conserved water equal to 12% of the whole:

  1. Water from the first liquid = 10% of 2 parts = 0.10 x 2 = 0.20 parts.

  2. Water from the second liquid = 20% of 3 parts = 0.20 x 3 = 0.60 parts.

  3. Water from the third liquid = x% of 4 parts = (x/100) x 4 = 0.04x parts.

  4. Total water = 12% of 9 parts = 0.12 x 9 = 1.08 parts.

  5. Form the equation: 0.20 + 0.60 + 0.04x = 1.08.

  6. Combine the known terms: 0.80 + 0.04x = 1.08.

  7. Isolate the unknown: 0.04x = 1.08 - 0.80 = 0.28.

  8. Solve: x = 0.28 / 0.04 = 7.

So x = 7%.

Cross-check

Substitute x = 7 back: water = 10x2 + 20x3 + 7x4 = 20 + 60 + 28 = 108 percent-parts over 9 parts, i.e. 108 / 9 = 12%, which matches the given final concentration. The third liquid (7%) is leaner than the 12% target while the first (10%) is also below it; only the 20% liquid is richer, and because it carries fewer parts than the third, the blend settles below the simple midpoint, consistent with a low value for the unknown.

title: The ratios of salt and sugar in mixtures and are
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The ratios of salt and sugar in mixtures A and B are 3 : 4 and 5 : 9, respectively. A and B are taken in the ratio 2 : 3 and mixed to form a new mixture C. What is the ratio of sugar and salt in C?
solution:
CONCEPT

In a mixture-ratio problem, first convert each internal ratio into fractions of the total mixture. When two mixtures are combined in a given quantity ratio, multiply each component fraction by the amount of that mixture before adding the components.

APPLICATION

  1. Let the quantities of mixtures A and B be 2x and 3x.

  2. In A, salt : sugar = 3 : 4, so salt = (3/7) × 2x = 6x/7 and sugar = (4/7) × 2x = 8x/7.

  3. In B, salt : sugar = 5 : 9, so salt = (5/14) × 3x = 15x/14 and sugar = (9/14) × 3x = 27x/14.

  4. Put the totals on denominator 14: total sugar = 16x/14 + 27x/14 = 43x/14; total salt = 12x/14 + 15x/14 = 27x/14.

CROSS-CHECK

Using a concrete scale with A = 28 units and B = 42 units gives sugar = 16 + 27 = 43 and salt = 12 + 15 = 27, so the same ratio appears.

RESULT

Therefore, the ratio of sugar to salt in C is 43 : 27.

title: Dishonest milkman professes to sell his milk at cost price
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A dishonest milkman professes to sell his milk at cost price but he mixes it with water and thereby gains 25%. The percentage of water in the mixture is:
solution:
Key idea: the milkman sells the mixture at the cost price of pure milk, and a 25% gain means the cost price of the mixture is lower than that selling price.

  • Assume the cost price of 1 litre of pure milk = 1.

  • The milkman sells 1 litre of the mixture at 1 (he sells at cost price of milk). Since he gains 25%, the cost price of 1 litre of the mixture = 1 ÷ 1.25 = 4/5 = 0.8.

  • This 0.8 is the cost of milk present in 1 litre of mixture. Since 1 litre of pure milk costs 1, the fraction of milk in the mixture = 0.8/1 = 4/5 = 80%.

  • Therefore the fraction of water = 1 - 4/5 = 1/5 = 20%.

Answer: 20%.

title: Grams of sugar solution has of sugar in it. How
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: 300 grams of sugar solution has 40% of sugar in it. How much sugar should be added to make it 55% in the solution?
solution:
Step-by-Step Solution

To solve this, we must ensure the amount of sugar represents the desired percentage of the total weight of the solution.

  1. Analyze the Initial State:

    • Total initial solution = 300 grams

    • Sugar concentration = 40%

    • Initial sugar amount = 0.40 * 300 = 120 grams

    • Initial water/other components amount = 300 - 120 = 180 grams

  2. Analyze the Target State:

    • Let 'x' be the grams of sugar to be added.

    • New sugar amount = 120 + x

    • New total solution weight = 300 + x

    • Target sugar concentration = 55%

  3. Set up the Equation:

    • (New sugar amount) / (New total solution weight) = 0.55

    • (120 + x) / (300 + x) = 0.55

  4. Solve for x:

    • 120 + x = 0.55 * (300 + x)

    • 120 + x = 165 + 0.55x

    • x - 0.55x = 165 - 120

    • 0.45x = 45

    • x = 45 / 0.45

    • x = 100 grams.

title: In college, of the number of students are girls and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: In a college, 63% of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. If 15% of the number of girls failed and 65% of the number of boys passed in the examination, then the percentage of total number of students who passed is:
solution:
Concept: When a population splits into two groups with different pass rates, the overall pass percentage is the weighted average of each group's own pass rate, weighted by that group's share of the total population — not a plain average of the two given rates.

Application: Take the total number of students as 100 (only the percentages matter, so any total works).

  1. Girls are 63% of the class, i.e. 63 students; boys are the remaining 37%, i.e. 37 students.

  2. 15% of the girls failed, so 100% − 15% = 85% of the girls passed: girls who passed = 85% of 63 = 53.55.

  3. 65% of the boys passed directly, so boys who passed = 65% of 37 = 24.05.

  4. Total students who passed = 53.55 + 24.05 = 77.6, out of 100 students in all — so 77.6% of the total students passed.

Cross-check: Working from the failures instead: girls who failed = 15% of 63 = 9.45; boys who failed = 35% of 37 = 12.95; total who failed = 22.4. So total who passed = 100 − 22.4 = 77.6%, matching the value obtained above.

title: The average age of class of students and teacher reduces
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The average age of a class of 34 students and a teacher reduces by 0.5 years, if the teacher is excluded. The initial average of the class including teacher is 16 years. Find the age of the teacher.
solution:
First, calculate the total age of the class including the teacher. There are 34 students + 1 teacher = 35 people.

With an average age of 16 years, the total sum is 35 × 16 = 560 years. Next, find the average age when the teacher is excluded.

The average reduces by 0.5 years, so it becomes 16 - 0.5 = 15.5 years. The total age of the 34 students is then 34 × 15.5 = 527 years.

Finally, subtract the students' total age from the initial total to find the teacher's age: 560 - 527 = 33 years.

title: The average age of man and his son is years.

bodyHtml: The average age of a man and his son is 36 years. The ratio of their ages is 3:1 respectively. What is the man's age?
solution:
Concept: When the average of two quantities is given, their sum equals the average multiplied by the number of quantities (here, 2 people). When two quantities are in the ratio a : b, they can be represented as ax and bx using a common multiplier x, so their sum is (a + b)x.

  1. Sum of the man's and son's ages = average × 2 = 36 × 2 = 72 years.

  2. Since the man : son age ratio is 3 : 1, let the man's age = 3x and the son's age = x.

  3. So 3x + x = 72, which gives 4x = 72, i.e., x = 18.

  4. Man's age = 3x = 3 × 18 = 54 years.

Cross-check: Son's age = x = 18 years. Average = (54 + 18) ÷ 2 = 36 years, matching the given average, and 54 : 18 simplifies to 3 : 1, matching the given ratio.

So, the man's age is 54 years.

title: Father tells his son,"I was of your present age when

bodyHtml: A father tells his son,"I was of your present age when you were born." If the father is now 36 years of age, how old was the boy 5 years ago?
solution:
To find the age of the boy 5 years ago, we can use algebraic expressions to represent the relationship between the father's and the son's ages.

Step-by-Step Analysis
Define Variables:

Let the son's current age be x.

When the son was born, the son's age was 0.

At that time, the father was x years old (based on the statement "I was of your present age when you were born").

Formulate the Father's Current Age:

Since the father was x years old when the son was born, the father is currently x + x = 2x years old.

We are given that the father is currently 36 years old.

So, 2x = 36.

Solve for x (Son's current age):

x = 36 / 2 = 18 years old.

Calculate the Son's age 5 years ago:

Son's age 5 years ago = 18 - 5 = 13.

title: The age of Manish is half of that of his
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: The age of Manish is half of that of his mother. His mother is 9 years younger to his father, and Manish is 7 years older than his sister. The age of his father is three times that of his sister, what is the age of Manish?
solution:
Concept

Age word-problems are solved by translating each relationship into a linear equation in a single chosen variable, then substituting one equation into another until one unknown remains. The phrase "A is younger than B by k" means B = A + k, and "A is k times B" means A = k·B. Pin every quantity to one base variable so the system collapses to a single equation.

Setting up the equations

Let Manish's age be M. Translate each statement, expressing everything in terms of M:

  1. Manish is half his mother's age, so mother = 2M.

  2. Mother is 9 years younger than father, so father = mother + 9 = 2M + 9.

  3. Manish is 7 years older than his sister, so sister = M − 7.

  4. Father's age is three times the sister's age, so father = 3 × (M − 7).

Solving

Equate the two expressions for the father's age:

  1. 2M + 9 = 3(M − 7)

  2. 2M + 9 = 3M − 21

  3. 9 + 21 = 3M − 2M

  4. M = 30

Cross-check

With M = 30: mother = 60, father = 2(30) + 9 = 69, sister = 30 − 7 = 23. Verify the last condition: 3 × 23 = 69 = father. Every relationship holds, so Manish is 30 years old.

title: Vaibhav is elder by years to Rohit. After years Vaibhav
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Vaibhav is elder by 3 years to Rohit. After 10 years Vaibhav will be thrice his present age and Rohit will be six time of his present age. How old is Rohit?
solution:
Concept:

In an ages problem, translate each word statement into a linear equation in the persons' present ages. A phrase like "after t years a person's age becomes k times the present age" means (present age) + t = k × (present age), and "A is elder by d years to B" means A = B + d. Solving the resulting equations gives every present age.

Application:

  1. Let Vaibhav's present age be V and Rohit's present age be R. The phrase "Vaibhav is elder by 3 years to Rohit" gives V = R + 3.

  2. "After 10 years Vaibhav will be thrice his present age" gives V + 10 = 3V, so 2V = 10 and V = 5.

  3. "Rohit will be six times his present age" gives R + 10 = 6R, so 5R = 10 and R = 2.

  4. Hence Rohit's present age is 2 years.

Cross-check:

With V = 5 and R = 2, the gap V − R = 5 − 2 = 3, matching "elder by 3 years". After 10 years Vaibhav is 5 + 10 = 15 = 3 × 5, and Rohit is 2 + 10 = 12 = 6 × 2. All three conditions hold, so R = 2 years.

title: Father is twice as old as his son. If years
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A father is twice as old as his son. If 30 years ago the age of the father was 5 times the age of the son, what is the present age of the father?
solution:
Concept

Linear age problems are solved by translating each verbal relationship into an algebraic equation in the unknown present ages, then solving the system. A relationship 'A is k times B' becomes A = k·B, and a past condition 't years ago' shifts every age by subtracting t.

Application

  1. Let the son's present age be s and the father's present age be f.

  2. 'Father is twice as old as his son' gives f = 2s.

  3. '30 years ago' subtracts 30 from each age, and 'father was 5 times the son' gives f − 30 = 5(s − 30).

  4. Substitute f = 2s: 2s − 30 = 5s − 150.

  5. Collect terms: 150 − 30 = 5s − 2s, so 120 = 3s, giving s = 40.

  6. Therefore f = 2s = 2 × 40 = 80.

The father's present age is 80 years.

Cross-check

Son is 40 and father is 80, so the father is twice the son today. 30 years ago the father was 50 and the son was 10, and 50 = 5 × 10, so both conditions hold.

title: Grand father has grandchildren. Age difference of two children among
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: A grand father has 3 grandchildren. Age difference of two children among them is 3. Eldest child age is 3 times the youngest child’s age and the eldest child's age is two years more than the sum of ages of other two children. What is the age of the eldest child?
solution:
Let A, B and C are ages of the children starting with eldest and ending in youngest.

Given Eldest is three times youngest ⇒ A = 3 × C ----(i)

Also Eldest is two years more than sum of other two ⇒ A = B + C + 2 ----(ii)

From Eq. (i) & (ii)

⇒ 3C = B + C + 2

⇒ 2C – B = 2

⇒ B = 2C - 2

So the ages are A = 3C, B = 2C – 2 and C = C.

Given difference between two of them is 3 years.

⇒ A - B = 3 or A - C = 3 or B - C = 3

⇒ C + 2 = 3 or 2C = 3 or C – 2 = 3

⇒ C = 1 or C = 3/2 or C = 5

For C = 1 ⇒ A = 3 and B = 0 (Not possible)

C = 3/2 is not possible

∴ C = 5 ⇒ A = 15 and B = 8 years.

Age of elder child = 15 years

title: Professor passed one sixth of his life in childhood, one
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml:
A professor spent one-sixth of his life in childhood, one-twelfth in youth, and one-seventh of his life as a bachelor.

Five years after his marriage, a son was born. The son died four years before the professor at an age equal to half the professor's final age.

What was the professor's age?
solution:
Let x be the professor's age at death.

  • Age when the son was born = one sixth + one twelfth + one seventh of life plus 5 = x/6 + x/12 + x/7 + 5.

  • The son died four years before the father, and the son's age at death equals half the father's final age, so the son's age at death = x/2.

  • The son's age at death also equals the difference between the father's age at the son's death and the father's age when the son was born: (x - 4) - (x/6 + x/12 + x/7 + 5).

  • Set these equal:

  • (x - 4) - (x/6 + x/12 + x/7 + 5) = x/2.

  • Combine fractions: x/6 + x/12 = x/4, and x/4 + x/7 = 11x/28. So the equation becomes x - 9 - 11x/28 = x/2.

  • Multiply both sides by 28 to clear denominators: 28x - 252 - 11x = 14x. This simplifies to 17x - 252 = 14x, so 3x = 252.

  • Therefore x = 252/3 = 84.

Answer: The professor's age is 84 years.

bodyHtml: The ratio of present age of Amit is to Manish is 3 : 2, while five years ago, Amit’s age was two times of Manish’s age at that time. Five years hence, the sum of ages of Manish and Amit is equal to Lalit’s age at that time, then find present age of Lalit?

title: At an IIM entrepreneurship summit, two young founders Karan and
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: At an IIM entrepreneurship summit, two young founders Karan and Deepak introduced their startup. In their quirky opening, they said: "The product of our ages is 240. And just like in our startup strategy, twice Deepak's age is 4 years more than Karan's age." How old was Deepak two years ago?
solution:
Let Deepak's present age be D. Then Karan's age is 2D - 4.

Their age product is D(2D - 4) = 240, so D^2 - 2D - 120 = 0.

D = 12, so Deepak's age two years ago was 10 years.

title: Radha is twice as old as Rita was years ago.
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: Radha is twice as old as Rita was 2 years ago. If difference between their ages is 2 years, how old is Radha today?
solution:
Let Rita's present age be x. Radha's age is x + 2 because their age difference is 2.

Radha is twice as old as Rita was 2 years ago, so x + 2 = 2(x - 2).

Solving gives x = 6, so Radha is 8 years old today.

title: IOCL Technical Attendant Numerical Ability 2024 Q78
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
bodyHtml: दस वर्ष पहले, अनिल की माता की आयु अनिल की आयु की तीन गुना थी। अब से दस वर्ष बाद, उसकी माता की आयु उसकी आयु की दोगुनी होगी। अनिल की वर्तमान आयु का उसकी माता की वर्तमान आयु से अनुपात, _____ है।
solution:
आयु-आधारित प्रश्नों में वर्तमान आयुओं को चर मानकर भूत और भविष्य की आयुओं को समान समयांतर से घटाया या जोड़ा जाता है। अनुपात निकालने से पहले दोनों समय-संबंधों से एक साथ बने रैखिक समीकरण हल किए जाते हैं।

अनुप्रयोग

  1. अनिल की वर्तमान आयु A वर्ष और उसकी माता की वर्तमान आयु M वर्ष मानें।

  2. दस वर्ष पहले की शर्त से M − 10 = 3(A − 10), इसलिए M = 3A − 20।

  3. दस वर्ष बाद की शर्त से M + 10 = 2(A + 10), इसलिए M = 2A + 10।

  4. दोनों M-मान बराबर रखने पर 3A − 20 = 2A + 10, अतः A = 30। फिर M = 2(30) + 10 = 70।

  5. वर्तमान आयुओं का अनुपात A : M = 30 : 70 = 3 : 7 है।

पुनः जाँच

  • दस वर्ष पहले आयुएँ 20 और 60 थीं; 60, 20 का तीन गुना है।

  • दस वर्ष बाद आयुएँ 40 और 80 होंगी; 80, 40 का दोगुना है।

अतः अनिल की वर्तमान आयु और उसकी माता की वर्तमान आयु का अनुपात 3 : 7 है।

title: The operating system is responsible for:
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: The operating system is responsible for:

options.label: A
options.html: Controlling peripheral devices such as monitor, printers, disk drives

options.label: B
options.html: Provide an interface that allows users to choose programs to run/manipulate files

solution:
Answer: All of the above is correct.

  • Controlling peripheral devices (monitor, printers, disk drives): the operating system manages device drivers and I/O services so applications can use hardware without dealing with low-level details.

  • Providing a user interface to run programs and manipulate files: the OS offers command-line or graphical interfaces and program-launching facilities to let users and applications interact with the system.

  • Managing user files on disk: the OS implements the file system, handling storage allocation, organization, access control, and file operations.

Why this matters: The operating system acts as an intermediary between hardware and users/applications, providing resource management, device control, file management, and user interfaces so software can run reliably and users can interact with the computer.

title: Which of the following is NOT function of an operating
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is NOT a function of an operating system ?
solution: Data encryption is not a core OS function, unlike memory management, task scheduling, and file management which are standard responsibilities.

title: Which of the following is the primary purpose of an
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is the primary purpose of an operating system ?
solution: The primary purpose of an operating system is to manage hardware resources and provide a platform for application software.

title: Which of the following is not an application software?
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is not an application software?
solution: Application software is designed to perform user-oriented tasks. MS-Word, MS-Access, and Notepad are application programs. An operating system manages computer hardware and provides services for programs, so it is system software, not application software.

title: Which of the following option is an example of system
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is the best example of core system software?
solution:
Correct answer: Operating System.

Core system software manages the computer hardware and provides services for application programs. An operating system is the primary example because it manages memory, processors, files, devices, and user interaction.

Antivirus software is a utility program and may be grouped under system utilities in a broad classification, but it is not the best example of core system software. Oracle and MS Word are application software.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2019 — Q16
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is not a service supported by an operating system?
solution:
Concept

An operating system manages hardware resources and provides standard services that programs and users need, such as controlled input/output, resource accounting, and protection. A compiler is a language-processing tool: it translates source code into another form.

Application

Compare each choice with the standard operating-system service categories. Protection, accounting, and I/O operations are listed OS responsibilities. Compilation belongs to the program-development toolchain, so Compilation is the service not supported as an operating-system service in this classification.

Contrast and cross-check

  • Protection controls access to processes, memory, files, and devices.

  • Accounting records how users and processes consume resources.

  • Compilation translates source programs into object or executable code.

  • I/O operations provide controlled data transfer between programs and devices.

Result

Therefore, the required value is Compilation.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q8
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: On systems with multiple operating systems, the decision to load a particular one is made by
solution:
Concept

During startup, firmware hands control to boot software. A boot loader locates a bootable operating-system kernel, loads it into memory, and transfers execution to it.

On a multiboot system, the same boot stage can present configured operating-system entries so that one kernel is selected before it is loaded.

Application

The question asks which component makes the operating-system choice at boot time. The component with boot entries and responsibility for loading the chosen kernel is the boot loader.

Contrast

  • Bootstrap names the startup process or initial routine more generally; it is not the specific multiboot selection component named here.

  • A process control block records the execution context and management data of a process after the operating system is managing processes.

  • A file control block records file metadata for file-system operations.

  • A boot loader provides the startup-stage path from a selected boot entry to the corresponding operating-system kernel.

Cross-check and result

If the user selects an operating system from a GRUB-style startup menu, the boot loader loads or chain-loads that system. Therefore, the answer is boot loader.

title: An operating system is
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: An operating system is
solution: An operating system is fundamentally defined as a collection of software routines that manage computer hardware resources and provide essential services for application programs. It serves as the core interface between software applications and computer hardware.

title: Which of the following is not primary responsibility of an
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is not a primary responsibility of an Operating System in a computer system?
solution:
An Operating System is responsible for managing hardware and system resources such as the processor, memory, and input/output devices.
Database Management is not a primary function of an OS; it is handled by specialized software like DBMS (Database Management Systems).

title: On systems where there are multiple operating system, the decision
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: On a system where multiple operating systems are installed, the decision to load a particular one at startup is made by ______.
solution:
Concept

Between power-on and the operating system taking over, a small program called the boot loader (bootstrap loader) runs first. It is responsible for locating the installed operating system(s), presenting a choice when more than one is installed, and loading the selected kernel into memory before handing over control.

Application

On a multi-boot machine, right after the hardware self-test, the boot loader reads the boot configuration, offers the installed operating systems to choose from, and loads the selected OS's kernel into memory. This is exactly the "decision to load a particular one" the question describes — it happens through the boot loader, not through any component that only becomes active after an OS is already running.

Why the other options don't fit

  • Process control block — created for a process only after the OS has already started running it; tracks that process's state, not OS selection.

  • File control block — belongs to the file system, tracking a file's attributes and disk location; unrelated to booting.

  • "More than one of the above" — wrong because a single dedicated program does this job, not a combination of components.

  • "None of the above" — wrong because one of the listed components does perform exactly this task.

title: Operating system is an interface between
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: An operating system is an interface between:
solution: An operating system acts as an interface between the user and the computer hardware/system. It manages resources such as CPU, memory, storage, and I/O devices and provides a usable environment for running programs. Hence, the best answer among the options is User and computer.

title: Which of the following OS is time bound system:
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following OS is a time bound system:
solution: Hard Real time system is a time bound operating system which has well-defined fixed time constraints. Processing must be done within the defined constraints. Otherwise the system will fail.

title: In Unix, process is
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: In Unix, a process is a
solution: The correct option is C: running program. In Unix and computing in general, a program is a passive entity stored on disk, whereas a process is an active instance of that program in execution, loaded into memory with allocated resources.

title: Which of the following is an example of batch processing
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is an example of a batch processing operating system ?
solution: IBM OS/360 is an example of a batch processing operating system.

title: Which of the following is an example of time-sharing operating
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is an example of a time-sharing operating system?
solution:
Concept

A time-sharing (multi-user) operating system lets many users interact with one computer at the same time by giving each a very short CPU time slice in rapid rotation. The fast switching makes every user feel as if they have the machine to themselves. The defining trait is concurrent interactive access by multiple users from separate terminals - not merely the ability to store more than one user account.

Application

Test each option against that defining trait - concurrent multi-user terminal access with CPU time-slicing:

  • MS-DOS - single user, one task at a time; no concurrency or time-slicing.

  • Windows 10 - supports multiple accounts, but the design serves one interactive desktop session; account creation is multi-user storage, not concurrent terminal time-sharing.

  • macOS - same as above: multiple accounts are supported, yet the architecture targets a single interactive desktop user.

  • UNIX - designed so many users at separate terminals share the CPU through rapid time slices simultaneously.

Result

Only UNIX matches the time-sharing definition (concurrent interactive multi-user access via CPU time-slicing). Having multiple user accounts, as in Windows 10 or macOS, is not the same as time-sharing, so UNIX is the correct choice.

title: Which of the following is an example of real-time operating
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is an example of a real-time operating system?
solution:
A real-time operating system (RTOS) is built to process inputs and deliver outputs within a strict, deterministic time bound, or deadline, so that timing is guaranteed and not just fast on average. A general-purpose operating system instead optimizes for overall throughput and fair multitasking, where occasional delay is acceptable.

QNX is a microkernel-based RTOS engineered from the ground up for deterministic, low-latency task scheduling. This is why it is widely used in embedded, automotive, and industrial control systems, where missing a timing deadline can cause the system to fail.

  • Windows 10: a general-purpose desktop operating system optimized for interactive multitasking, not for deterministic timing guarantees.

  • UNIX: a general-purpose multi-user, multitasking operating system; standard UNIX does not provide the deterministic guarantees of a true RTOS (separate real-time UNIX variants exist but are not standard UNIX itself).

  • Linux: a general-purpose operating system; although real-time patches or variants (such as PREEMPT_RT) exist, the standard/vanilla Linux kernel does not guarantee hard real-time deadlines.

Among the given options, only QNX is built as a true real-time operating system, so QNX is the correct answer.

title: Almost the entire code of UNIX operating system is written
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Almost the entire code of UNIX operating system is written in _________ programming language.
solution: The correct answer is C. UNIX was originally written partly in assembly, but almost the entire operating system was rewritten in the C programming language at Bell Labs. This made UNIX much more portable across different hardware systems.

title: Which of the following is not characteristic of embedded system?
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is not a characteristic of an embedded system?
solution: An embedded system is usually designed for a dedicated task. Common characteristics include being reactive and real-time, single-functioned, and tightly constrained by resources such as memory, power, cost, and processing capacity. Being multi-functioned is a characteristic of a general-purpose computer, not a typical embedded system.

title: Unix is operating system.
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Unix is a _________ operating system.
solution: Unix is a multi-user and multitasking operating system. Multi-user means more than one user can use the system, often through terminals or network connections. Multitasking means the operating system can manage multiple processes at the same time. Therefore, the correct option is multi-user and multitasking.

title: Which of the following option is Multitasking operating system.
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is generally not a multitasking operating system?
solution:
Correct answer: MS-DOS.

The corrected question asks for the operating system that is generally not multitasking. Windows, Unix, and Mac OS X support multitasking.

Standard MS-DOS is generally considered a single-tasking operating system, so it is the correct option.

title: Unix was developed in
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Unix was developed at _________.
solution:
Correct answer: AT&T Bell Labs.

Unix was originally developed at AT&T Bell Labs in the late 1960s and early 1970s by Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie, and others.

Sun Microsystems, Intel, and Microsoft Corporation are important technology companies, but they were not the original developers of Unix.

title: Which of the following option is not need of embedded
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is not a requirement of an embedded system?
solution:
Correct answer: Large size.

An embedded system is designed for a specific task and usually works with limited resources. Important requirements include efficient use of resources, reliability, and low power consumption.

Large size is not a requirement. In fact, embedded systems are generally expected to be compact and purpose-specific.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2019 — Q20
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Multiprogramming systems

options.label: A
options.html: Are easier to develop than single programming systems.

options.label: C
options.html: Execute more jobs in the same time period.

options.label: D
options.html: Are used in only large mainframe computers.

solution:
Concept

Multiprogramming keeps several jobs in memory so the CPU can switch to a ready job whenever the current job waits for input/output. Its central performance aim is to reduce CPU idle time and raise system throughput, which is the number of jobs completed per unit time. Throughput is different from the turnaround time of one particular job.

Application

  1. With only one resident job, an input/output wait can leave the CPU idle even though the system still has useful work to finish.

  2. With several resident jobs, the operating system can schedule a ready job during that waiting interval, so CPU work and another job’s input/output wait overlap.

  3. Because a larger share of the same time interval is spent doing useful CPU work, the system can complete more jobs in that interval. Therefore the applicable statement is “Execute more jobs in the same time period.”

Contrast

  • “Are easier to develop than single programming systems” concerns implementation effort; coordinating several jobs requires additional scheduling, memory-management, and protection mechanisms.

  • “Execute each job faster” concerns individual turnaround time; multiprogramming improves aggregate resource use but does not guarantee that every job finishes sooner.

  • “Are used in only large mainframe computers” imposes a hardware-size restriction that is not part of the definition of multiprogramming.

Cross-check and result

Compare two equal time windows. If the only resident job waits for input/output, some CPU slots are idle; if another ready job uses those slots, more useful processing is completed before the window ends. This confirms the throughput interpretation and the result “Execute more jobs in the same time period.”

title: Which of the following options best describes key function of
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following options best describes a key function of a multimedia operating system?

options.label: C
options.html: Providing database management tools for metadata indexing

options.label: D
options.html: Ensuring real-time scheduling and synchronization of multimedia data streams

solution:
A Multimedia Operating System differs fundamentally from a standard general-purpose OS (like basic Linux or Windows) because it must handle continuous, time-dependent data media streams natively.

1. Real-Time Scheduling (Timing constraints)
In a standard OS, a slight delay in executing a background task or opening a file is acceptable. However, in a multimedia environment, a delay causes jitter or frame drops.

To prevent this, a multimedia OS employs Real-Time Scheduling Algorithms (like Rate Monotonic or Earliest Deadline First).

These algorithms ensure that the CPU processes incoming audio and video frames before their strict deadlines expire.

2. Stream Synchronization
A standard video clip contains separate tracks: one for audio data and one for video data. These independent data blocks are read from disk or network interfaces simultaneously.

The multimedia operating system is tasked with managing these distinct streams and synchronizing them relative to a shared master clock. It maps timestamps to individual packets so that a specific audio sample plays at the exact millisecond its corresponding video frame is rendered on screen.

3. Resource Management & Quality of Service (QoS)
To stream high-definition content flawlessly, the OS must reserve a guaranteed amount of hardware resources. It implements resource reservation protocols that lock down specific CPU cycles, memory bandwidth, and network throughput for media playbacks, preventing a heavy background download from disrupting your video playback experience.

title: Special software that is used to create job queue is
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: A special software that is used to create a job queue is called
solution: A spooler is specialized software designed to manage job queues in operating systems. It buffers data between processes and devices, ensuring sequential processing for efficiency.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q163
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: The part of OS that remains in memory permanently is called
solution:
Concept: An operating system is organized into a core resident part and several loadable or user-level components. The kernel is the portion of the OS that is loaded into main memory at boot and stays resident throughout system operation, because it must continuously manage the CPU, memory, and I/O devices and service interrupts and system calls on demand.

Application: Among Shell, Command Interpreter, API, and Kernel, only the kernel matches the description "the part of the OS that remains in memory permanently" — the other three are either user-level programs that can be started and stopped, or an interface specification rather than a resident program.

Contrast with the other options:

  • Shell: a command-line or graphical interface program that a user can launch, replace, or exit; it is not a fixed, always-loaded part of the OS.

  • Command Interpreter: the component that reads and executes typed commands, often implemented as the shell itself; it too runs as a user-level process rather than a permanently memory-resident module.

  • API: a specification of the calls and protocols by which programs request OS services; it is a programming interface, not a piece of code that must sit in memory at all times.

Cross-check: standard operating-system textbook definitions (e.g., Silberschatz, Operating System Concepts) describe the kernel as the part of the OS that is always running and resident in main memory — this matches only the Kernel option.

Hence, the correct answer is Kernel — the always-resident core of the operating system.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2019 — Q17
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which option gives the complete set, among those listed, of operating systems that can provide a graphical user interface (GUI)?
solution:
Concept

A graphical user interface lets a user interact with a computer through windows, icons, menus, and pointing actions instead of relying only on typed commands.

GUI support is a capability of an operating-system environment; an operating system may offer both graphical desktops and command-line interfaces.

Application

  • Windows provides an integrated graphical desktop and shell.

  • Linux distributions can run graphical desktop environments such as GNOME or KDE Plasma.

  • Solaris has also provided graphical desktop environments, including GNOME-based desktops.

Cross-check and contrast

  • Windows names one GUI-capable operating system.

  • Linux names another GUI-capable operating-system family.

  • Solaris names a third GUI-capable operating system.

Because each named operating system can provide a GUI, selecting only one of the individual names would leave out the other valid examples.

Therefore, the complete answer by value is All of these.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q37
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following versions of Windows does not have a Start button?
solution:
Concept

A desktop operating system can expose application launching through either a persistent taskbar control or a separate full-screen launcher. A change in launcher design may therefore remove the visible desktop control while retaining keyboard and screen-based access to applications.

Application

Windows 8 introduced the full-screen Start screen and removed the traditional Start button from the desktop taskbar. The Windows key and screen-edge controls opened the Start screen instead.

Contrast

  • Windows Vista displays an orb-shaped Start control that opens the Start menu.

  • Windows 7 also displays a taskbar Start control that opens the Start menu.

  • None of the above would require all three named releases to retain that desktop control, which is inconsistent with the Windows 8 interface change.

Result

Therefore, the version without the desktop Start button is Windows 8.

title: Which of the following are system software? Compiler Word Processor
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml:
Which of the following are system software?

A. Compiler B. Word Processor C. Interpreter D. Linker E. Assembler

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: System software manages hardware resources and enables application execution, whereas application software performs specific user tasks. A Compiler translates high-level code to machine code (System Software). B Word Processor is designed for document creation (Application Software). C Interpreter translates and executes code line-by-line (System Software). D Linker combines object files into an executable program (System Software). E Assembler translates assembly language to machine code (System Software). Thus, A, C, D, and E are classified as system software.

title: Which of the following statements are true:
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following statements are true:

options.label: A
options.html: System calls are executed in user mode as well as Kernel mode

options.label: B
options.html: Privileged instruction is required to move from user mode to kernel mode.

options.label: C
options.html: Parameters of the system calls cannot be passed into register

options.label: D
options.html: Parameters of the system calls are pushed to and popped off by operating system from Stack

solution:
a. False. System calls are executed in kernel mode. The transition occurs when a user application requests a system service.
b. True. A privileged instruction, often invoked via a system call, is required to transition from user mode to kernel mode.
c. False. Parameters of system calls can often be passed in registers, particularly in architectures that support this method.
d. True. In many cases, parameters can be passed on the stack, and the operating system manages these parameters when the system call is made.

title: Which of the following is NOT type of operating system
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is NOT a type of operating system process ?
solution: In operating system architecture, Application process is not a distinct, fundamental classification of a process. Instead, all applications that a user runs (like a web browser or text editor) are technically executed and categorized as User processes.

title: What is the primary purpose of system call in an
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: What is the primary purpose of a system call in an operating system ?

options.label: A
options.html: Run arbitrary user code with full system access

options.label: B
options.html: Request access to system resources and services in a controlled manner

options.label: C
options.html: Communicate directly with hardware devices without OS intervention

options.label: D
options.html: Manage other processes and control system behavior

solution: A system call serves as the fundamental interface between a user application and the operating system kernel. Its primary purpose is to allow programs to request access to protected system resources, such as files, memory, or network connections, in a controlled and secure manner. This mechanism ensures that user code cannot directly manipulate hardware or access critical data without permission, maintaining system stability and security. Option A is incorrect because user code runs in a restricted mode (user space) and cannot have full system access without transitioning to kernel mode via a system call. Option C is wrong because direct hardware communication bypasses the OS, which violates security and stability principles; the OS must mediate all hardware interactions. Option D describes process management functions, which are tasks performed by the OS itself rather than the specific purpose of a system call interface. Therefore, Option B accurately defines the core function of system calls as controlled resource requests.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q166
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which of the following is NOT a system call ?
solution:
A system call is the interface through which a running program asks the operating-system kernel for a service that user-space code is not permitted to perform on its own — creating or terminating a process, moving data to or from a file or device, or passing data between processes. Invoking one switches the processor from user mode into kernel mode and back. A library function, by contrast, is ordinary code that executes entirely in user space; it may request a kernel service internally, but the routine itself is not that kernel interface.

The classification used in standard operating-system courses, and in Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne's table of process-control examples, turns on one question about a named routine: does the kernel itself provide a service of that name, or is the name purely a user-space convenience layered on top of some other kernel service?

Applying that test to each option:

  • fork() names a kernel process-control service: the kernel allocates a new process control block and duplicates the caller's address-space mapping, producing a child process that starts with a copy of the parent's memory image. No user-space routine can do this by itself.

  • exit() names the kernel's process-termination service (exit / exit_group on Linux), which releases the process's resources and leaves an exit status for the parent to collect. The C library entry of the same name first runs the program's registered termination handlers and flushes its stdio buffers, and reaches that kernel service through the low-level _exit call. Standard operating-system texts list exit() among the process-control system calls on the strength of the kernel service it denotes.

  • read() names a kernel file- and device-management service: the kernel transfers up to a requested number of bytes from an open file descriptor into a buffer the program supplies, since only the kernel may safely touch the underlying file system or device.

  • printf() names no kernel service at all: formatting its arguments against a format string happens entirely in user space inside the C standard I/O library, and the resulting characters reach the terminal or file only afterwards, through a separate write() system call.

Cross-check by exclusivity: fork(), exit() and read() each name a service the kernel itself provides — their user-space wrappers exist only to enter the kernel — whereas printf() has no kernel counterpart of that name and is a formatting convenience built on top of write().

A note on precision: read strictly as C-library entries, exit() is documented in manual section 3 alongside printf(), and the raw termination call is _exit(); under the standard operating-system classification this question uses, however, exit() denotes the kernel's termination service, and printf() is the only one of the four with no kernel service behind its name. Hence printf() is the answer — it is the one library routine among four names that otherwise denote kernel services.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q24
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Match the following Windows API calls with their functionally corresponding UNIX system calls for process control and file manipulation. List I (Windows): A. CreateProcess; B. WaitForSingleObject; C. CreateFile; D. CloseHandle. List II (UNIX): 1. open; 2. close; 3. fork; 4. wait. Select the correct code.
solution:
CONCEPT

System-call interfaces expose operating-system services such as creating processes, waiting for process completion, opening files, and releasing file handles.

Calls from different operating-system families are matched by the service they perform, not by the similarity of their names.

APPLICATION

  1. Process creation: Windows CreateProcess starts a new process; the corresponding UNIX call is fork. Therefore A maps to 3.

  2. Process waiting: Windows WaitForSingleObject can wait for a process handle; the corresponding UNIX process-waiting call is wait. Therefore B maps to 4.

  3. File opening: Windows CreateFile opens or creates a file object; the corresponding UNIX call is open. Therefore C maps to 1.

  4. Handle release: Windows CloseHandle releases an open object handle; the corresponding UNIX file-descriptor operation is close. Therefore D maps to 2.

CROSS-CHECK / CONTRAST

  • A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2 swaps the two process-control functions: process creation is paired with wait, while waiting is paired with fork.

  • A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1 swaps both the process-control pair and the file-manipulation pair.

  • A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1 preserves the process-control pair but swaps file opening with handle closing.

Thus the complete matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

title: Consider the statements below and choose the correct combination of
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml:
Consider the statements below and choose the correct combination of "Yes" or "No" for each:

S1: Can two processes that are not parent/child be concurrently executing the same program executable?

S2: Can two running processes share the complete process image in physical memory (not just parts of it)?
solution:
Answer: (S1) Yes; (S2) No

  • S1 — Yes: Multiple processes can execute the same program binary concurrently. For example, launching the same executable twice creates two separate processes, each with its own process control block, registers, and stacks.

  • S2 — No: Processes do not share the complete process image in physical memory. Each process has its own virtual address space (private heap, stack, and writable data).

  • Notes/Exceptions: The operating system can map the same read-only code pages or shared libraries into multiple processes, and after a fork the kernel may use copy-on-write so pages are shared until modified. These mechanisms do not mean the entire, writable process image is shared by default.

Therefore the correct combination is: the first statement is Yes and the second statement is No.

title: Operating systems must provide mechanism for parent processes to create
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Operating systems must provide a mechanism for parent processes to create new child processes. Which of the following statements is true when a parent process creates new process?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.html: The parent waits until some or all of its children have terminated

options.label: C
options.html: The parent waits for the child process by issuing a signal ( ) system call

solution: Standard operating system models define two primary behaviors for parent processes after creating children. First, the parent may continue execution concurrently with its children. Second, the parent might block and wait until specific or all children terminate. Both scenarios are valid mechanisms in process management theory.

title: Which processing technique involves executing multiple tasks simultaneously
subject: Operating System
bodyHtml: Which processing technique involves executing multiple tasks simultaneously?
solution:
Correct answer: Parallel processing.

Parallel processing executes multiple tasks at the same time, usually using separate processing resources such as multiple processors or cores. Serial and sequential processing execute tasks one after another. Concurrent processing can make tasks appear to progress together through interleaving, but strict simultaneous execution is parallel processing.

title: Process is if it cannot affect or be affected by
